verdicts.death: put to death, whether by court, by God directly, or by the sword
verdicts.plague: plague, disease, or fire from God, usually on a group
verdicts.captivity: carried captive, bound, or handed to enemies
verdicts.curse: a pronounced curse or standing sentence without immediate death
verdicts.restitution: the wrong was made good under the law of restitution
verdicts.spared: guilty, but spared on repentance, intercession, or by the withdrawal of witnesses
verdicts.reprieve: sentence pronounced but softened, delayed, or stayed
verdicts.temporal: a bounded judgment in this life: sickness, defeat, loss, humiliation
verdicts.unrecorded: the offense and the statute are recorded; scripture does not record the sentence
verdicts.blessed: kept the law, and the blessing scripture records for it

cases.name: Adam and Eve
cases.charge: Eating from the tree God forbade
cases.summary: Given one prohibition in the garden, they ate from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil after the serpent's persuasion. The first transgression, and the pattern for every one after it: a plain command, a rationalization, a broken boundary.
cases.offense: The Lord permitted every tree but one. The woman, deceived, took the fruit and gave it to the man, who ate knowingly. Both then hid, and both shifted blame, to the serpent, to each other, to God for the gift of the other.
cases.judgment: No death that day, but a sentence on all that followed: pain in childbearing, toil against a cursed ground, and expulsion from the garden lest they eat of the tree of life. Death entered as the long consequence.

cases.name: Cain
cases.charge: Murder of his brother Abel
cases.summary: The first murder. Angry that his brother's offering was accepted and his own was not, Cain rose up in the field and killed Abel, then denied knowledge of it to God's face.
cases.offense: Warned directly that sin crouched at his door and that he must master it, Cain instead led his brother out and struck him down. Asked where Abel was, he answered with a lie and a taunt: am I my brother's keeper?
cases.judgment: Not death but a heavier exile: the ground would no longer yield to him, and he became a fugitive and a wanderer. God set a mark on him so that no one would kill him, extending the very mercy Cain had denied.

cases.name: Ham and the curse on Canaan
cases.charge: Uncovering and publishing his father's nakedness
cases.summary: Noah drank of his vineyard and lay uncovered in his tent. Ham saw his father's nakedness and told his two brothers outside, who walked in backward with a garment and covered him without looking.
cases.offense: Dishonor of a father, in the very thing the law later forbids: the nakedness of thy father thou shalt not uncover. Shem and Japheth showed what honor looks like; Ham showed the opposite and made it public.
cases.judgment: When Noah awoke and knew what his younger son had done to him, he cursed Canaan, Ham's son: a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren. Shem and Japheth were blessed in the same breath.

cases.name: Lamech
cases.charge: Killing a man and boasting of it; claiming seventy-sevenfold vengeance
cases.summary: Cain's descendant Lamech, first recorded polygamist, told his two wives he had killed a man for wounding him and a young man for bruising him, and claimed that if Cain were avenged sevenfold, Lamech would be seventy-sevenfold.
cases.offense: A killing far out of proportion to the injury, then a song to celebrate it. Lamech takes the protection God extended to Cain and twists it into a license for private vengeance without limit.
cases.judgment: Scripture records no sentence on Lamech. His line is not heard from after the Flood account opens; the whole world of Cain's descendants ends in Genesis 7.

cases.name: The builders of Babel
cases.charge: Building a tower to make themselves a name and resist being scattered
cases.summary: With one language and one purpose, the whole earth settled in Shinar and built a city and a tower whose top would reach to heaven, to make themselves a name and not be scattered abroad. The Lord came down to see it.
cases.offense: Direct defiance of the command to replenish the earth, in the form of a monument to human self-sufficiency. The stated aim was a name for themselves, not for God.
cases.judgment: The Lord confounded their language so they could not understand one another and scattered them over the face of all the earth. The building stopped, and the place was named Babel, confusion.

cases.name: The generation of the Flood
cases.charge: Corruption and violence filling the earth
cases.summary: A whole world under judgment. The earth was filled with violence and every imagination of the heart was continually evil, so God resolved to blot out what he had made, sparing only Noah's household.
cases.offense: Not one offense but a saturation: corruption of all flesh, violence without restraint, wickedness so total that it grieved God that he had made man.
cases.judgment: The Flood. Every living thing on the dry land perished; eight souls were carried through in the ark. The waters were both execution and cleansing.

cases.name: The sons of God and the giants
cases.charge: Leaving their proper estate; taking wives of the daughters of men
cases.summary: Before the Flood the sons of God took wives of whomever they chose among the daughters of men, and giants were in the earth in those days. The New Testament and the Apocrypha both treat this as a transgression that was judged.
cases.offense: Jude names it: angels who kept not their first estate but left their own habitation. Second Peter calls them the angels that sinned. Sirach calls the giants themselves the old giants who fell away in the strength of their foolishness, and the Wisdom of Solomon says the proud giants perished.
cases.judgment: The angels are reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. The giants and the world they filled with violence went under the Flood; Noah alone was carried through.

cases.name: Abel
cases.charge: Bringing the firstlings of his flock and the fat thereof
cases.summary: The first offering scripture records as accepted, and the first man it calls righteous. Abel brought the firstlings and the fat, and the Lord had respect unto him. His brother's envy killed him, and his blood still speaks.
cases.offense: Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain: the first and the best, not the leftover, and brought in faith. The law of the firstlings and the fat was written later; Abel kept it before it was written.
cases.judgment: The Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering. By it he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh. Christ names him righteous Abel, the first of the prophets whose blood was shed. His blessing is a standing before God that outlasted his life.

cases.name: Enoch
cases.charge: Walking with God three hundred years
cases.summary: Seventh from Adam, he walked with God after Methuselah was born, and was not, for God took him. Before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God. He is the first man scripture says did not see death.
cases.offense: Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters. Jude records that he prophesied of the Lord coming with ten thousands of his saints to execute judgment on the ungodly. Sirach: Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, being an example of repentance to all generations.
cases.judgment: And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him. By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.

cases.name: Noah
cases.charge: Doing according to all that God commanded him
cases.summary: In a world where every imagination of man's heart was only evil continually, one man was just and perfect in his generations and walked with God. He was told to build an ark and did it exactly, and he and his house were the only ones saved through the flood.
cases.offense: Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God. Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he. By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house. Peter calls him a preacher of righteousness.
cases.judgment: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord. With thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons' wives with thee. After the flood God blessed Noah and his sons, gave them the earth, set the bow in the cloud, and swore that the waters would no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. Eight souls were saved by water, and the world began again from his house.

cases.name: Er and Onan
cases.charge: Wickedness before the Lord; refusing to raise up seed to a dead brother
cases.summary: Judah's firstborn Er was wicked in the sight of the Lord and the Lord slew him. His brother Onan, told to raise up seed to Er by Tamar, deliberately spilled his seed rather than give his brother an heir, and the Lord slew him also.
cases.offense: Er's sin is unnamed; the verdict is not. Onan's is precise: he knew the seed would not be his, and each time he went in to Tamar he prevented conception. He took the wife but refused the duty, cheating the dead and the widow.
cases.judgment: Both died at the Lord's hand, not by any court. The duty Onan refused was later written into the law of the kinsman: the firstborn she bears shall succeed in the name of his brother that is dead.

cases.name: Esau
cases.charge: Despising his birthright; marrying Hittite wives; purposing to kill his brother
cases.summary: The firstborn of Isaac sold his birthright for a single meal, took wives of the Canaanites to his parents' grief, and when the blessing went to Jacob resolved to kill him. The prophets and apostles treat him as the pattern of the profane man.
cases.offense: Hebrews names it: a fornicator or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. His marriages were a grief of mind to Isaac and Rebekah. His hatred of Jacob was murder in the heart.
cases.judgment: He found no place of repentance, though he sought the blessing with tears. Malachi: I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste. Obadiah sentences his house for its violence against Jacob: the house of Esau shall be for stubble.

cases.name: Job's three friends
cases.charge: Speaking of God the thing that is not right; condemning the righteous
cases.summary: Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar came to comfort Job and spent thirty chapters insisting his suffering proved hidden sin. Eliphaz went so far as to invent the sins: thou hast taken a pledge from thy brother for nought, and stripped the naked of their clothing. When the Lord answered out of the whirlwind, he answered them too.
cases.offense: Job had asked them earlier: will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him? They had judged a man on suspicion, condemned the just, and defended God with false accusations against his servant. Job's cause was right; their theology was not.
cases.judgment: My wrath is kindled against thee and against thy two friends, for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath. They were ordered to bring seven bullocks and seven rams to Job and have him pray for them, lest I deal with you after your folly. He did, and the Lord accepted Job.

cases.name: Joseph's brothers
cases.charge: Conspiracy to murder; selling a brother; deceiving their father with a bloodied coat
cases.summary: Ten brothers plotted to kill Joseph out of envy, then sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver and dipped his coat in goat's blood so Jacob would think him dead. Twenty years later they stood before him in Egypt.
cases.offense: Envy became conspiracy; conspiracy became man-stealing, which the law makes capital; and the cover-up was a lie that broke their father's heart for two decades. In Egypt they confessed among themselves: we are verily guilty concerning our brother.
cases.judgment: The famine and Joseph's testing brought the guilt to the surface. Joseph forgave them: ye thought evil against me, but God meant it unto good. They were spared, and the reconciliation is the founding story of the twelve tribes.

cases.name: Judah and Tamar
cases.charge: Withholding Shelah from his brother's widow; going in to a woman he took for a harlot
cases.summary: Judah promised Tamar his third son and never gave him, then lay with her himself on the road to Timnath. When her pregnancy came to light he ordered her burned, until she produced his signet, bracelets and staff. He judged himself: she hath been more righteous than I.
cases.offense: After Er and Onan died, Judah sent Tamar to her father's house to wait for Shelah, and let her wait. Tamar covered her face and sat in an open place, and Judah, taking her for a harlot, went in to her for the price of a kid, leaving his signet and staff as a pledge. Three months later he was told his daughter in law was with child by whoredom, and said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt.
cases.judgment: No sentence fell on Tamar; Judah stopped it himself when the pledge was laid before him, confessed that the fault was his for withholding Shelah, and knew her again no more. She bore Pharez and Zarah, and Pharez stands in the line of David and of Christ. The judgment recorded is a confession that spared the innocent and let the guilty man's own mouth condemn him.

cases.name: Lot's wife
cases.charge: Looking back toward Sodom against the angel's command
cases.summary: The angels told Lot's household to escape for their lives and not look behind them. His wife looked back from behind him and became a pillar of salt. Christ made her a proverb in three words.
cases.offense: A plain instruction, given for her own life, disregarded. The look back is treated in scripture as a turning of the heart toward what God was destroying.
cases.judgment: She became a pillar of salt on the plain, and the Wisdom of Solomon says the standing pillar remained as a monument of an unbelieving soul. Remember Lot's wife.

cases.name: Pharaoh and Abimelech, who took Sarah
cases.charge: Taking another man's wife into the king's house
cases.summary: Twice Abraham called Sarah his sister, and twice a king took her. Neither king knew she was married, and both were judged before they touched her: the Lord guards the marriage bed even where the husband has failed to.
cases.offense: In Egypt, Pharaoh's princes commended Sarai and she was taken into Pharaoh's house. In Gerar, Abimelech sent and took Sarah. Both acted on Abraham's word that she was his sister, and Abimelech pleaded the integrity of his heart; but the woman was a man's wife, and that fact, not their knowledge of it, was what the Lord answered.
cases.judgment: The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai. To Abimelech he came in a dream: thou art but a dead man, for the woman is a man's wife. The Lord had closed up every womb of the house of Abimelech, and opened them only when Sarah was restored and Abraham, the prophet, prayed for him.

cases.name: Reuben
cases.charge: Lying with Bilhah, his father's concubine
cases.summary: Jacob's firstborn went up to his father's bed and lay with Bilhah, and Israel heard of it. Nothing more is said until the deathbed, where it cost Reuben the birthright.
cases.offense: The nakedness of thy father's wife shalt thou not uncover, later a capital offense in the law. Chronicles states the consequence plainly: because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph.
cases.judgment: Unstable as water, thou shalt not excel. The double portion went to Joseph, the rule to Judah. Reuben's tribe never produced a judge, prophet, or king.

cases.name: Shechem son of Hamor
cases.charge: Defiling Dinah, daughter of Jacob
cases.summary: Shechem, prince of the country, saw Dinah, took her, and lay with her and defiled her. He then asked for her in marriage and agreed to circumcision to get her. Her brothers answered with the sword.
cases.offense: He had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob's daughter, which thing ought not to be done. The law would later require the seducer of an unbetrothed virgin to endow her and the rapist to die.
cases.judgment: On the third day, while the men of the city were sore, Simeon and Levi killed every male, Hamor and Shechem among them, and took Dinah out of his house. Jacob condemned the manner of it; the brothers answered, should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?

cases.name: Simeon and Levi at Shechem
cases.charge: Deceitful covenant; slaughter of a city for one man's crime
cases.summary: To avenge Dinah, the brothers proposed circumcision to the men of Shechem as a condition of peace, then killed the whole city while it was disabled and plundered it. Jacob never forgot it.
cases.offense: They answered Shechem and Hamor deceitfully. A covenant made in bad faith, used as a weapon; collective slaughter for an individual's offense; and spoil taken from the dead. Vengeance that belonged to God taken into their own hands.
cases.judgment: On his deathbed Jacob passed sentence: instruments of cruelty are in their habitations; cursed be their anger, for it was fierce. I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel. Simeon was absorbed into Judah; Levi had no tribal land.

cases.name: Sodom and Gomorrah
cases.charge: Grievous sin; inhospitality and violence against strangers
cases.summary: Cities whose sin was grave enough that its cry reached heaven. When two visitors lodged with Lot, the men of the city surrounded the house demanding them. Judgment fell the next morning.
cases.offense: The prophets later name the fuller charge: pride, fullness of bread, careless ease, and no help for the poor and needy, a hardness that showed itself in the mob at Lot's door.
cases.judgment: Fire and brimstone from the Lord out of heaven, overthrowing the cities and the plain. Lot's wife, looking back, became a pillar of salt. Held up ever after as the type of sudden ruin.

cases.name: Abraham
cases.charge: Obeying the Lord's voice; keeping his charge, his commandments, his statutes, and his laws
cases.summary: Told to leave country, kindred and father's house for a land he would be shewed, he went. Told to offer his only son, he rose early in the morning. The Lord's own account of him, given to Isaac, is the law kept: Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.
cases.offense: By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went. He believed in the Lord, and he counted it to him for righteousness. He circumcised every male of his house the selfsame day he was commanded. He commanded his children and his household after him to keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment. When tried, he offered up Isaac, accounting that God was able to raise him up.
cases.judgment: I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing. By myself have I sworn, saith the Lord, for because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only son: that in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven; and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice. He was called the friend of God, and the covenant with his seed stands.

cases.name: Isaac
cases.charge: Dwelling in the land the Lord told him of, and not going down into Egypt in the famine
cases.summary: A famine came, and the natural road was Egypt, where his father had gone. The Lord appeared and said, Go not down into Egypt; sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee. Isaac stayed in Gerar, sowed in a famine year, and reaped an hundredfold.
cases.offense: The Lord appeared unto him, and said, Go not down into Egypt; dwell in the land which I shall tell thee of: sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee. And Isaac dwelt in Gerar. When the herdmen of Gerar strove with him for the wells he dug, he removed and digged another rather than fight for what was his.
cases.judgment: Then Isaac sowed in that land, and received in the same year an hundredfold: and the Lord blessed him. And the man waxed great, and went forward, and grew until he became very great. At Beer-sheba the Lord appeared to him the same night: fear not, for I am with thee, and will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham's sake. Abimelech came to him to make a covenant, saying, We saw certainly that the Lord was with thee.

cases.name: Job
cases.charge: Perfect and upright, fearing God and eschewing evil; sinning not with his lips in all his loss
cases.summary: The Lord himself gave the character: there is none like him in the earth. He lost his oxen, his sheep, his camels, his servants, his ten children and his health in a day and a night, and said, Blessed be the name of the Lord. The Lord turned his captivity, and gave him twice as much as he had before.
cases.offense: That man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil. He rose up early in the morning and offered burnt offerings for his children, lest they had sinned. When all was taken he fell down upon the ground and worshipped: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord. In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly. His own account of the law he kept: I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless; I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame; I made a covenant with mine eyes.
cases.judgment: The Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before. So the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, seven sons and three daughters, and in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job; and he saw his sons' sons, even four generations. James: ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.

cases.name: Joseph
cases.charge: Refusing his master's wife: how can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
cases.summary: Sold by his brothers, bought by Potiphar, tempted daily by his master's wife, Joseph refused, fled, and was jailed on her lie. The Lord was with him in the pit, in the prison, and in the palace, and he became the man through whom the whole house of Israel was kept alive.
cases.offense: His master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me. But he refused: Behold, my master wotteth not what is with me in the house; how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God? She spake to Joseph day by day, and he hearkened not unto her. When she caught him by his garment, he left his garment in her hand, and fled. Years later he told his brothers: ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.
cases.judgment: The Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man. The keeper of the prison committed to Joseph's hand all the prisoners, because the Lord was with him, and that which he did, the Lord made it to prosper. Pharaoh said, Thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled. The psalm: the word of the Lord tried him; the king sent and loosed him, and made him lord of his house. Wisdom: she delivered him not, but brought him the sceptre of the kingdom.

cases.name: Lot
cases.charge: A righteous man vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked; sheltering the strangers at his door
cases.summary: He chose the plain of Sodom and lived to regret it, but Peter calls him just Lot, vexed from day to day with the unlawful deeds of the city. He took the two strangers into his house and stood in his door against the men of the city. The angels took him by the hand and led him out before the fire fell.
cases.offense: Lot sat in the gate of Sodom and rose up to meet the two angels, and pressed upon them greatly to turn in to his house, and made them a feast, and baked unleavened bread. When the men of the city compassed the house he went out and shut the door after him and said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly. Peter: that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds.
cases.judgment: The men said unto Lot, Hast thou here any besides? bring them out of this place: for we will destroy this place. While he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters; the Lord being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city. God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow. The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations.

cases.name: Amalek
cases.charge: Attacking Israel's stragglers on the way out of Egypt
cases.summary: Amalek came out against Israel at Rephidim and, as Deuteronomy records, smote the hindmost, the feeble and faint and weary, and feared not God. Israel prevailed while Moses' hands were held up.
cases.offense: An unprovoked attack on a nation just out of bondage, aimed at those least able to defend themselves. No fear of God, no cause of war.
cases.judgment: The Lord swore war with Amalek from generation to generation and commanded that his remembrance be blotted out from under heaven. Saul was sent to execute it and failed; the sentence passed to David and was finished under Hezekiah.

cases.name: Moses and the uncircumcised son
cases.charge: Neglecting the sign of the covenant in his own house
cases.summary: On the road to Egypt to deliver Israel, the Lord met Moses at the inn and sought to kill him. Zipporah took a sharp stone, circumcised her son, and cast the foreskin at his feet. So he let him go.
cases.offense: The covenant with Abraham required every male circumcised on the eighth day; the uncircumcised man-child was to be cut off from his people. The deliverer of Israel had not kept it in his own household, and it had to be set right before he could speak for God to Pharaoh.
cases.judgment: The death sentence was stayed the moment the neglect was remedied. The narrative gives no further comment; the priority is the comment.

cases.name: Pharaoh of the Exodus
cases.charge: Oppressing Israel; drowning their sons; refusing the Lord's command
cases.summary: The king who did not know Joseph enslaved Israel, ordered their male infants thrown into the river, and when Moses came in the Lord's name answered, Who is the Lord? He hardened his heart through ten plagues and drowned in the sea he pursued Israel into.
cases.offense: Forced labor with rigor, infanticide by decree, contempt for the Name, and repeated broken promises: each time the plague lifted he hardened his heart and would not let the people go. Paul says he was raised up for this, that God's name might be declared in all the earth.
cases.judgment: Ten plagues on Egypt ending in the death of every firstborn, Pharaoh's included. Then his army in the Red Sea: the waters returned and covered the chariots and horsemen; there remained not so much as one of them. Wisdom says a strange death.

cases.name: Israel at the first Passover
cases.charge: Doing as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron: the lamb, the blood on the door, the unleavened bread
cases.summary: On the night the destroyer went through Egypt, every house of Israel that did as it was told was passed over. The children of Israel went away, and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they. The ordinance was made perpetual on the spot.
cases.offense: Take you a lamb according to the house of your fathers; kill it in the evening; take of the blood and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post; eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs, in haste; none of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning. And the children of Israel went away, and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they. By faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them.
cases.judgment: The blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you. At midnight the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, and against the children of Israel not so much as a dog moved his tongue. He brought them forth also with silver and gold: and there was not one feeble person among their tribes. Thus did all the children of Israel; as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they. And it came to pass the selfsame day.

cases.name: Moses
cases.charge: Refusing to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter; faithful in all the Lord's house; very meek, above all the men upon the face of the earth
cases.summary: He gave up the court of Egypt to be counted with slaves, and led them forty years through a wilderness that murmured against him at every turn. The Lord's testimony on him is unmatched: my servant Moses, who is faithful in all mine house; with him will I speak mouth to mouth. He was buried by God.
cases.offense: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter; choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season. Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth. When the Lord offered to make of him a great nation instead of Israel, he pleaded for the people and asked to be blotted out of the book rather than that they be. According to all that the Lord commanded Moses, so did he: the whole tabernacle, and Moses blessed them.
cases.judgment: With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold. The Lord spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. Sirach: he made him glorious in the sight of kings, and gave him commandments before his people, and shewed him part of his glory; he sanctified him in his faithfulness and meekness, and chose him out of all men. His eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated at a hundred and twenty; and there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses.

cases.name: Shiphrah and Puah, the midwives
cases.charge: Fearing God and not doing as the king of Egypt commanded them
cases.summary: Pharaoh ordered the Hebrew midwives to kill every son at the birthstool. They feared God more than the king and saved the men children alive. God dealt well with them, and because they feared God, he made them houses.
cases.offense: The king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah: when ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, if it be a son, then ye shall kill him. But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive. Called to account, they answered him and the killing did not pass through their hands.
cases.judgment: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty. And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses. Two women's names are written; Pharaoh's is not.

cases.name: Aaron and Israel at the golden calf
cases.charge: Idolatry within weeks of the covenant
cases.summary: While Moses was on the mountain receiving the law that forbade it, the people made a golden calf and worshipped it. The covenant was broken almost before the ink was dry.
cases.offense: Impatient at Moses' delay, they pressed Aaron, who gathered their gold and cast a calf; they declared it the god that brought them out of Egypt and rose up to play. Aaron built it an altar and proclaimed a feast.
cases.judgment: Moses ground the calf to powder and made them drink it. The Levites, called to the Lord's side, put about three thousand to the sword, and the Lord sent a plague on the people. Aaron was spared but not excused.

cases.name: Aaron and Miriam
cases.charge: Speaking against Moses; challenging his authority
cases.summary: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses, using his marriage as a pretext to ask whether the Lord had not also spoken through them. God summoned all three and answered plainly.
cases.offense: Envy of Moses' unique standing, aired as a grievance. God declared that with Moses he spoke mouth to mouth, not in visions, and asked why they were not afraid to speak against him.
cases.judgment: Miriam became leprous, white as snow; struck, it seems, as the instigator. Moses interceded, and after seven days shut out of the camp she was healed. A measured discipline, not death.

cases.name: Balaam
cases.charge: Divination for hire; counseling Moab to seduce Israel into idolatry
cases.summary: Hired by Balak to curse Israel, Balaam could only bless. So he taught Balak a surer way: draw Israel into fornication and the feasts of Baal-peor and let their own God judge them. It worked, and it killed him.
cases.offense: A prophet who loved the wages of unrighteousness, pressed God for permission he had already been refused, and when he could not curse the people, arranged their sin. Christ names the doctrine of Balaam as still at work in the churches.
cases.judgment: Balaam the son of Beor they slew with the sword when Israel went against Midian, together with the kings of Midian. Jude: they ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished.

cases.name: Israel and the fiery serpents
cases.charge: Speaking against God and against Moses; loathing the bread from heaven
cases.summary: Discouraged on the way around Edom, the people spoke against God and Moses: there is no bread, no water, and our soul loatheth this light bread. The Lord sent fiery serpents, and much people of Israel died.
cases.offense: Contempt for the provision and the deliverer in a single complaint. Paul cites it: neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents.
cases.judgment: The serpents bit and many died. When the people confessed, Moses made a serpent of brass on a pole; whoever looked, lived. The Wisdom of Solomon says they were troubled for a small season to be admonished, saved not by the thing they saw but by God. Christ took it as the figure of his own lifting up.

cases.name: Israel at Baal-peor
cases.charge: Fornication with the daughters of Moab; sacrificing to their gods
cases.summary: In Shittim the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, who called them to the sacrifices of their gods. Israel ate, bowed down, and joined himself unto Baal-peor. The plague took twenty-four thousand.
cases.offense: Balaam's counsel executed: sexual sin as the door to idol worship. Hosea says they went to Baal-peor and separated themselves unto that shame, and their abominations were according as they loved. Psalm 106 adds that they ate the sacrifices of the dead.
cases.judgment: The Lord commanded the heads of the offenders hanged up before the sun, and the judges to slay every man his men that were joined to Baal-peor. A plague ran through the camp until Phinehas stayed it. Paul: fell in one day three and twenty thousand.

cases.name: Korah, Dathan, and Abiram
cases.charge: Rebellion against God-appointed authority
cases.summary: Korah led 250 leaders in a challenge to Moses and Aaron, claiming the whole congregation was holy and needed no mediator. The earth answered the claim.
cases.offense: They gathered against Moses, charging him with lifting himself above the assembly. It was not merely a personnel dispute but a rejection of the order God had set, framed in the language of equality.
cases.judgment: The ground opened and swallowed Korah's company with their households, and fire consumed the 250 who offered incense. When the people murmured the next day, a plague killed 14,700 more until Aaron's incense stayed it.

cases.name: Moses at the waters of Meribah
cases.charge: Failing to honor God as holy before the people
cases.summary: Told to speak to the rock so it would give water, Moses instead struck it twice and spoke rashly to the people. The water came, but so did a sentence: he would not enter the promised land.
cases.offense: God said speak to the rock; Moses struck it and said, 'must we fetch you water?', taking to himself and Aaron what belonged to God, and disobeying the specific instruction in anger.
cases.judgment: No death, but the leader who had carried the nation forty years was barred from the land for it. A case that measures how much is required of those entrusted with much.

cases.name: Nadab and Abihu
cases.charge: Offering strange fire not commanded
cases.summary: Two priests, sons of Aaron, offered fire before the Lord that he had not commanded. Fire came out from the Lord and consumed them on the spot.
cases.offense: They took their censers, put fire and incense in them, and offered 'strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not.' Presumption in the very act of worship, from those who of all people knew the ordinances.
cases.judgment: Fire from before the Lord devoured them, and they died. Aaron was forbidden even to mourn. A warning that nearness to holy things raises the standard rather than lowering it.

cases.name: Sihon and Og
cases.charge: Refusing Israel passage and coming out to battle against them
cases.summary: Israel asked only to pass through on the king's highway, turning neither to the right nor to the left. Sihon gathered his people and came out to fight, and Og after him. Both kingdoms were given into Israel's hand, and the land east of Jordan became the first inheritance.
cases.offense: Moses sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites with words of peace: let me pass through thy land; we will not turn into the fields or the vineyards. Sihon would not suffer Israel to pass, but gathered all his people and fought at Jahaz. Og king of Bashan came out against them at Edrei, the last of the remnant of giants.
cases.judgment: Israel smote Sihon with the edge of the sword and possessed his land from Arnon to Jabbok. Of Og the Lord said, Fear him not, for I have delivered him into thy hand; they smote him and his sons and all his people until none was left him alive. The psalms remember it as mercy that endureth for ever: who smote great kings, and gave their land for an heritage.

cases.name: The blasphemer in the camp
cases.charge: Blaspheming the Name in a quarrel
cases.summary: In a fight within the camp, a man blasphemed the Name and cursed. He was held until the Lord's mind was made known, and his case set the statute for all Israel.
cases.offense: The son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian man blasphemed the Name in the course of a brawl. The offense was against God directly, spoken and heard by witnesses.
cases.judgment: The Lord commanded that the whole congregation stone him outside the camp, the witnesses laying their hands on his head. From his case came the law: whoever blasphemes the Name shall be put to death.

cases.name: The complainers at Taberah and the lusters at Kibroth-hattaavah
cases.charge: Murmuring against the Lord; lusting after flesh and despising the manna
cases.summary: The people complained and the fire of the Lord burned in the outskirts of the camp. Days later the mixed multitude fell to lusting and Israel wept for the meat of Egypt. Quail came, and with the quail a plague.
cases.offense: Contempt for God's provision. They said the manna had dried up their souls and named the fish and cucumbers of Egypt as what they missed, forgetting the brick-kilns. Psalm 78 calls it tempting God in their heart and speaking against him.
cases.judgment: Fire consumed the complainers at Taberah until Moses prayed. At Kibroth-hattaavah, while the flesh was yet between their teeth, the Lord smote the people with a very great plague; the place is named for the graves of the lusters. Paul: these things were our examples.

cases.name: The congregation, the day after Korah
cases.charge: Murmuring that Moses and Aaron had killed the people of the Lord
cases.summary: The earth had swallowed Korah's company the day before, and fire had consumed the two hundred and fifty. The next morning the whole congregation gathered against Moses and Aaron and called the dead the people of the Lord. The plague began before the sentence was finished being spoken.
cases.offense: On the morrow all the congregation murmured against Moses and against Aaron, saying, Ye have killed the people of the Lord. They took the side of the rebels the Lord had just judged, and made the judgment itself the grievance.
cases.judgment: The glory of the Lord appeared and wrath went out from him; the plague was begun. Moses sent Aaron running into the congregation with a censer to make an atonement, and he stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stayed. Fourteen thousand and seven hundred died, beside them that died about the matter of Korah.

cases.name: The generation that died in the wilderness
cases.charge: Ten provocations; unbelief at Kadesh-barnea
cases.summary: Those numbered from twenty years old who had seen the signs in Egypt and at the sea, and had tempted the Lord ten times, were sentenced at Kadesh to wander until every one of them had fallen in the wilderness. Only Caleb and Joshua of that generation entered the land.
cases.offense: Not one act but a pattern: at the sea, at Marah, over the manna, at Rephidim, at the calf, at Taberah, at Kibroth-hattaavah, and finally refusing the land God had sworn to give. Hebrews names the root: they could not enter in because of unbelief. Then, told the sentence, they presumed to go up anyway and were beaten back.
cases.judgment: Forty years, a year for each day of the search. Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness. Sirach counts them: the six hundred thousand footmen gathered together in the hardness of their hearts, whom he pitied not.

cases.name: The man gathering sticks on the Sabbath
cases.charge: Working on the Sabbath
cases.summary: A man was found gathering sticks on the Sabbath day. Because the penalty had not yet been specified, he was held while the Lord's judgment was sought.
cases.offense: The command to keep the Sabbath was already given; his act of gathering fuel was plain work on the day of rest, done openly and witnessed.
cases.judgment: The Lord commanded that he be put to death; the congregation stoned him outside the camp. A hard case, preserved precisely because the sentence was not obvious and had to be asked.

cases.name: The manna hoarders
cases.charge: Keeping manna overnight; going out to gather on the Sabbath
cases.summary: Told to gather only a day's portion, some kept manna until morning and it bred worms and stank. Told there would be none on the seventh day, some went out to gather anyway and found nothing.
cases.offense: Distrust dressed as prudence. The first was hoarding against a promise of daily provision; the second was Sabbath-breaking against a double portion already given. Moses was angry at the one, and the Lord at the other: how long refuse ye to keep my commandments?
cases.judgment: The hoarded bread rotted. The Sabbath gatherers went out and found nothing, and were rebuked. Small, exact, and recorded so the next test would be understood.

cases.name: The Midianites, in the matter of Peor
cases.charge: Beguiling Israel with their wiles into fornication and the worship of Baal-peor
cases.summary: Balaam could not curse Israel, so he taught Balak how to make Israel curse itself. The daughters of Midian and Moab drew the people to Peor, and twenty-four thousand died in the plague. The Lord then told Moses to avenge Israel of the Midianites before he was gathered to his people.
cases.offense: On Balaam's counsel the women of Midian invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods; the people ate, and bowed down, and joined themselves to Baal-peor. Cozbi, the daughter of a prince of Midian, was brought into the camp itself. They vexed Israel with their wiles, wherewith they beguiled you in the matter of Peor.
cases.judgment: Vex the Midianites, and smite them. Israel warred against Midian as the Lord commanded Moses and slew all the males, the five kings of Midian, and Balaam the son of Beor with the sword. Moses was angry that the women who had caused the trespass were kept alive, and the sentence was carried through on them also.

cases.name: The ten spies
cases.charge: Bringing an evil report; making the congregation to murmur
cases.summary: Twelve men searched Canaan forty days. Ten came back and told the people the land eats its inhabitants and the giants made them as grasshoppers. Caleb and Joshua said the Lord would bring them in. The people believed the ten.
cases.offense: They did not deny the land was good; they denied that God could give it. Their report turned a nation from faith to fear in one night and had the people ready to choose a captain back to Egypt and stone the two who believed.
cases.judgment: The men that brought up the evil report died by the plague before the Lord. Caleb and Joshua lived, and forty-five years later Caleb took his mountain.

cases.name: Zimri and Cozbi
cases.charge: Bringing a Midianite woman into the camp in the sight of the congregation
cases.summary: While the congregation wept at the tabernacle door over the plague, Zimri, a prince of Simeon, walked a Midianite princess past them into his tent. Phinehas followed with a javelin and thrust them both through.
cases.offense: Open defiance of the judgment in progress: not hidden sin but sin paraded before Moses and the mourning assembly, by a leader, with the daughter of a chief of Midian. The offense was against the whole camp's standing before God.
cases.judgment: Both died on the javelin, and the plague was stayed. God gave Phinehas a covenant of everlasting priesthood because he was zealous for his God and made an atonement. Sirach ranks him third in glory; the Maccabees claim him as father.

cases.name: Caleb and Joshua
cases.charge: Wholly following the Lord when ten spies and the whole congregation would not
cases.summary: Twelve men saw the same land, the same cities and the same giants. Ten said, We be not able. Two said, The Lord is with us: fear them not. The ten died of the plague; the whole generation died in the wilderness; and Caleb and Joshua were the only two of six hundred thousand who walked into the land.
cases.offense: Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it. Joshua and Caleb rent their clothes and said, If the Lord delight in us, then he will bring us into this land; only rebel not ye against the Lord, neither fear ye the people of the land; for they are bread for us. The congregation bade stone them with stones. Forty-five years later Caleb could still say, I wholly followed the Lord my God.
cases.judgment: But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land whereinto he went; and his seed shall possess it. Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun. At eighty-five Caleb took Hebron, as strong that day as the day Moses sent him: because that he wholly followed the Lord God of Israel. Joshua led Israel over Jordan and divided the inheritance, and the Lord magnified him in the sight of all Israel.

cases.name: Phinehas
cases.charge: Zealous for his God at Peor; making an atonement for the children of Israel
cases.summary: While the congregation wept at the door of the tabernacle and the plague was running, a prince of Simeon walked a Midianite woman into the camp in front of them. Phinehas took a javelin and went in after them, and the plague was stayed at twenty-four thousand. The Lord gave him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.
cases.offense: When Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, and took a javelin in his hand; and he went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel. The psalm: then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and so the plague was stayed. And that was counted unto him for righteousness unto all generations for evermore.
cases.judgment: Phinehas hath turned my wrath away from the children of Israel, while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Israel in my jealousy. Wherefore say, Behold, I give unto him my covenant of peace: and he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his God, and made an atonement for the children of Israel. Sirach and Mattathias both name him first among the zealous, and the high priesthood ran in his line to the captivity.

cases.name: The daughters of Zelophehad
cases.charge: Asking rightly for their father's inheritance, and marrying within their tribe as commanded
cases.summary: Five sisters with no brother came to the door of the tabernacle and asked why their father's name should be done away from among his family because he had no son. The Lord said, The daughters of Zelophehad speak right, and made a statute of judgment for all Israel. They then married as they were told, and kept the inheritance in Manasseh.
cases.offense: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah stood before Moses, and before Eleazar the priest, and before the princes and all the congregation, saying, Our father died in the wilderness, and was not in the company of them that gathered themselves together against the Lord in the company of Korah; but died in his own sin, and had no sons. Give unto us therefore a possession among the brethren of our father. When the heads of Manasseh asked that the inheritance not pass to another tribe by marriage, the Lord commanded them to marry within the family of their father's tribe; even as the Lord commanded Moses, so did the daughters of Zelophehad.
cases.judgment: The daughters of Zelophehad speak right: thou shalt surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father's brethren; and thou shalt cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them. And it became a statute of judgment: if a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter. Joshua and Eleazar gave them an inheritance among the brethren of their father, according to the commandment of the Lord. Their names are written four times in the law and the histories.

cases.name: The sons of Levi at the golden calf
cases.charge: Answering, Who is on the Lord's side? and executing the sentence on their own brethren
cases.summary: When Moses stood in the gate of the camp and asked who was on the Lord's side, all the sons of Levi gathered to him, took their swords, and went through the camp. Three thousand fell. For that day the priesthood and the service of the sanctuary were given to the tribe, and Moses' last blessing names it.
cases.offense: Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the Lord's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him. Put every man his sword by his side, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour. And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses. Deuteronomy: who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed thy word, and kept thy covenant.
cases.judgment: Consecrate yourselves to day to the Lord, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother; that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day. Of Levi he said, Let thy Thummim and thy Urim be with thy holy one; they shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Israel thy law: they shall put incense before thee, and whole burnt sacrifice upon thine altar. Bless, Lord, his substance, and accept the work of his hands. The tribe was taken instead of the firstborn of all Israel to keep the charge of the tabernacle.

cases.name: Achan
cases.charge: Taking devoted spoil from Jericho
cases.summary: Jericho's spoil was placed under the ban, devoted wholly to God. Achan took a garment, silver, and a wedge of gold and hid them in his tent. Israel's next battle failed because of it.
cases.offense: He 'saw, coveted, and took,' then buried the goods under his tent. One man's hidden theft brought defeat at Ai and the death of thirty-six soldiers before the cause was found by lot.
cases.judgment: Achan and his household, with the stolen goods, were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. The accursed thing, once purged, restored Israel's standing.

cases.name: Adoni-bezek
cases.charge: Mutilating seventy kings
cases.summary: Judah defeated the Canaanite king Adoni-bezek and cut off his thumbs and great toes. He said it himself: seventy kings with thumbs and toes cut off had gathered their meat under my table; as I have done, so God hath requited me.
cases.offense: Systematic cruelty to defeated enemies, which he counted as his glory. The law of Israel limits punishment to measure, eye for eye and no more; he had exceeded all measure on seventy men.
cases.judgment: The same mutilation, once. He was brought to Jerusalem and died there. A pagan king pronouncing the lex talionis on himself is the point of the record.

cases.name: The Gibeonites, and Israel's oath
cases.charge: Obtaining a covenant by fraud; Israel making it without asking counsel of the Lord
cases.summary: The Gibeonites came to Joshua in old clothes with moldy bread claiming to be from a far country, and Israel made peace with them. Three days later the fraud was found out. The oath stood anyway.
cases.offense: On the Gibeonite side, a treaty by deception. On Israel's side, the text is explicit: the men took of their victuals, and asked not counsel at the mouth of the Lord. The covenant forbidden with the inhabitants of the land was made through negligence.
cases.judgment: Because the princes had sworn by the Lord, the Gibeonites could not be killed, but were made hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and the altar. Centuries later, when Saul broke that oath, God sent famine on Israel for it.

cases.name: Rahab
cases.charge: Receiving the spies with peace, and believing that the Lord had given Israel the land
cases.summary: A harlot of Jericho hid two Israelite spies under the flax on her roof, confessed that the Lord their God is God in heaven above and in earth beneath, and asked for her father's house. She bound the scarlet line in the window. When the wall fell, hers was the one house left, and she is in the line of Christ.
cases.offense: I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us. For the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath. Now therefore, I pray you, swear unto me by the Lord, since I have shewed you kindness, that ye will also shew kindness unto my father's house. She let them down by a cord through the window, and bound the scarlet line in the window as they said. James: was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?
cases.judgment: Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive, and her father's household, and all that she had; and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day. By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace. Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse; and Jesse begat David the king.

cases.name: Abimelech son of Gideon
cases.charge: Murder of seventy brothers on one stone; usurping a crown
cases.summary: Gideon's son by a Shechemite concubine hired vain and light persons with silver from the house of Baal-berith, killed his seventy brothers on one stone, and had himself made king at Shechem. Only Jotham escaped, and his parable from Mount Gerizim pronounced the sentence.
cases.offense: Fratricide financed by an idol's treasury, in pursuit of a kingship God had not given and Gideon had refused. Jotham: if ye have dealt truly, rejoice in Abimelech; if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and devour the men of Shechem, and fire from Shechem devour Abimelech.
cases.judgment: God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem; he destroyed the city and sowed it with salt, and at Thebez a woman dropped a millstone on his head. He had his armor-bearer finish him so it would not be said a woman slew him. Thus God rendered the wickedness of Abimelech.

cases.name: Eglon king of Moab
cases.charge: Possessing the city of palm trees and taking tribute of Israel eighteen years
cases.summary: The Lord strengthened Eglon against Israel because Israel did evil, and for eighteen years Israel served him. When they cried, the Lord raised up Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite with a message from God, and the message was a dagger.
cases.offense: Eglon gathered Ammon and Amalek, smote Israel, and took the city of palm trees. He held Israel under tribute for eighteen years, a fat man in a summer parlour receiving the present of the people he oppressed.
cases.judgment: Ehud brought the present, then said, I have a message from God unto thee, and thrust the dagger into his belly so that the haft went in after the blade. Israel followed him down and slew about ten thousand men of Moab, all lusty and men of valour, and Moab was subdued, and the land had rest fourscore years.

cases.name: Eli and his sons
cases.charge: Corrupt priesthood; a father who would not restrain it
cases.summary: Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas treated the Lord's offering with contempt and lay with the women at the tabernacle door. Eli rebuked them weakly but did not remove them. The house fell together.
cases.offense: The sons seized the sacrifices by force and defiled worship; the father honored his sons above God by tolerating it. A failure of office compounded by a failure of discipline.
cases.judgment: Both sons died on the same day in battle; the ark was captured; Eli fell and broke his neck at the news. The priesthood was stripped from his line as foretold.

cases.name: Gideon's ephod
cases.charge: Making an ephod from the spoil; Israel whoring after it
cases.summary: Gideon refused the crown and said the Lord should rule, then asked for the golden earrings of the spoil and made an ephod of them and put it in Ophrah. All Israel went a whoring after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his house.
cases.offense: The man who had thrown down his father's altar of Baal built a new object of worship out of victory. The text does not say he meant idolatry; it says what it became. The gold of Midian was the same material as the calf.
cases.judgment: A snare unto Gideon and to his house. As soon as he died, Israel turned to Baal-berith, and his seventy sons were murdered by the son he had by a concubine in Shechem.

cases.name: Israel in the days of the Judges
cases.charge: Serving Baalim and Ashtaroth; intermarrying with the Canaanites; every man doing right in his own eyes
cases.summary: After Joshua's generation died a generation arose that knew not the Lord. They forsook him for the gods of the peoples round about, took their daughters as wives, and were sold into the hands of Mesopotamia, Moab, Canaan, Midian, Ammon, and the Philistines in turn.
cases.offense: The cycle the book itself describes: the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, served Baalim, forsook the God of their fathers. Judges 3 records the intermarriage that drove it; Psalm 106 says they were mingled among the heathen and learned their works.
cases.judgment: The anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers. Each time they cried out he raised a judge; each time the judge died they returned and corrupted themselves more than their fathers. The book ends with no king and every man right in his own eyes.

cases.name: Jabin and Sisera
cases.charge: Mightily oppressing Israel twenty years with nine hundred chariots of iron
cases.summary: Jabin reigned in Hazor and Sisera commanded his host, and for twenty years they mightily oppressed the children of Israel. Deborah sent for Barak, the Lord discomfited the chariots at Kishon, and Sisera died in a tent with a nail through his temples.
cases.offense: Israel again did evil after Ehud was dead, and the Lord sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan. Sisera, captain of his host, had nine hundred chariots of iron and used them to oppress Israel mightily for twenty years, so that the highways were unoccupied and the travellers walked through byways.
cases.judgment: The Lord discomfited Sisera and all his chariots and all his host with the edge of the sword before Barak; the river of Kishon swept them away. Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, who gave him milk and a nail. The hand of Israel prospered and prevailed against Jabin until they had destroyed him. Deborah sang it: so let all thine enemies perish, O Lord.

cases.name: Jephthah's vow
cases.charge: A rash vow, and its performance on his daughter
cases.summary: Before battle with Ammon, Jephthah vowed that whatever came out of his doors to meet him on his return would be the Lord's and offered as a burnt offering. His only child came out with timbrels. He did with her according to his vow.
cases.offense: The vow itself was the sin: sworn thoughtlessly with the lips, as Leviticus describes, binding himself to a thing God never asked and, on the plain reading, forbade. Ecclesiastes: suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin. The text records that she bewailed her virginity and knew no man; readers have long divided over whether the sacrifice was literal or a life devoted, and the text does not settle it.
cases.judgment: He lost his only child and his line ended with him. The daughters of Israel kept a yearly lament for her. Jephthah is nonetheless counted among the faithful in Hebrews 11, which is the record's own tension.

cases.name: Micah's idols and the tribe of Dan
cases.charge: A house of gods, a hired Levite, and a tribe that stole both
cases.summary: Micah of Ephraim stole silver from his mother, returned it, and she had it made into a graven and molten image. He set up a house of gods, consecrated his own son, then hired a wandering Levite as priest. The Danites, migrating north, took the priest and the idols for themselves.
cases.offense: Every layer breaks a law: theft from a parent, images made from the stolen silver, a shrine that was not the chosen place, a priest who was not of Aaron, and then armed robbery of the whole apparatus by a tribe that founded its northern city on it. The narrator's refrain: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.
cases.judgment: The Danites set up the graven image and Jonathan son of Gershom and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land. Dan's idolatry ran unbroken from this to Jeroboam's calf at the same city.

cases.name: Samson
cases.charge: Marrying a Philistine; going in to a harlot; betraying his Nazarite vow to Delilah
cases.summary: A Nazarite from the womb who repeatedly went down to the Philistines for women: a wife at Timnath against his parents' counsel, a harlot at Gaza, and Delilah in Sorek, to whom he told all his heart. He woke from her lap shaven, and the Lord had departed from him.
cases.offense: Get her for me, for she pleaseth me well: the whole pattern in one sentence. Marriage with the uncircumcised, fornication, and the surrender of the sign of his consecration, each time with eyes that saw what they wanted. Hebrews still lists him among those who through faith waxed valiant.
cases.judgment: The Philistines put out his eyes, bound him with fetters of brass, and set him grinding in the prison house. In the temple of Dagon he prayed once more, and the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life. He died with them.

cases.name: The men of Beth-shemesh
cases.charge: Looking into the ark of the Lord
cases.summary: When the Philistines returned the ark on a cart, the men of Beth-shemesh rejoiced, offered the kine, and looked into the ark. The Lord smote them with a great slaughter, and they asked, who is able to stand before this holy Lord God?
cases.offense: Even the Kohathites who carried the ark were forbidden to go in and see when the holy things were covered, lest they die. Farmers at harvest opened it for curiosity. The Levites of a priestly city should have known.
cases.judgment: The text gives the number as fifty thousand and threescore and ten men, a figure long debated; the sentence is not. They sent the ark on to Kirjath-jearim and it stayed there twenty years.

cases.name: The men of Gibeah, and Benjamin
cases.charge: Sodomy, gang rape and murder of a stranger's concubine; a tribe that shielded the guilty
cases.summary: The men of Gibeah surrounded the house where a Levite lodged, demanding him; they were given his concubine and abused her all night until she died on the threshold. He cut her into twelve pieces and sent them through Israel. Benjamin refused to surrender the guilty, and Israel went to war.
cases.offense: The crime of Sodom repeated in Israel, then compounded by the tribe: they would not hearken to the voice of their brethren to put away evil from Israel. Hosea names it twice as the depth of the nation's corruption: they have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah.
cases.judgment: After two defeats Israel destroyed Benjamin, the city, the cattle, and all that came to hand; six hundred men survived at the rock Rimmon, and the tribe was rebuilt from them. Israel wept at Bethel that a tribe was lacking.

cases.name: The Philistines and the captured ark
cases.charge: Setting the ark of God in the house of Dagon, and keeping it seven months
cases.summary: The Philistines took the ark in battle and set it beside Dagon as a trophy. Dagon fell on his face before it twice, the second time without head or hands, and the men of Ashdod, Gath and Ekron were smitten with emerods until they sent it home on a new cart with golden offerings.
cases.offense: They carried the ark of God into the house of Dagon and set it by Dagon, as if the God of Israel had been taken captive by their god. When Ashdod could bear it no longer they moved it to Gath, and Gath to Ekron, each city passing the judgment along rather than sending the ark back.
cases.judgment: The hand of the Lord was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and he destroyed them and smote them with emerods; the men of Gath, small and great, were smitten; in Ekron there was a deadly destruction throughout all the city. Their priests and diviners told them to give glory unto the God of Israel and not harden their hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh did, and the ark went back with five golden emerods and five golden mice, a trespass offering.

cases.name: Gideon
cases.charge: Throwing down the altar of Baal in his father's house; going against Midian with three hundred, as the Lord said
cases.summary: Threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it from the Midianites, the least in his father's house was called a mighty man of valour. He cut down Baal's altar by night, sent home thirty-one thousand seven hundred men because the Lord said the army was too big, and broke the Midianites with pitchers, lamps and trumpets.
cases.offense: Throw down the altar of Baal that thy father hath, and cut down the grove that is by it: and build an altar unto the Lord thy God. Then Gideon took ten men of his servants, and did as the Lord had said unto him. The Lord said, The people that are with thee are too many; and Gideon sent home all that were fearful, and then all but three hundred, and went down against a host like grasshoppers for multitude with the men who lapped. They cried, The sword of the Lord, and of Gideon.
cases.judgment: The Lord looked upon him, and said, Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites: have not I sent thee? The Lord set every man's sword against his fellow throughout all the host, and Midian was subdued before the children of Israel, so that they lifted up their heads no more. And the country was in quietness forty years in the days of Gideon. His name stands in the roll of faith: who through faith subdued kingdoms, out of weakness were made strong. The ephod he made afterward is its own case.

cases.name: Hannah
cases.charge: Praying in bitterness of soul, vowing a son to the Lord, and giving him when she had him
cases.summary: Barren, provoked yearly by her rival, mistaken for a drunkard by the high priest, she poured out her soul before the Lord and vowed that if he gave her a son she would give him back for all his days. He did, and she did: she brought Samuel to Shiloh as soon as he was weaned. The Lord gave her five more.
cases.offense: She vowed a vow, and said, O Lord of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the Lord all the days of his life. When he was weaned she took him up with three bullocks and brought him unto the house of the Lord in Shiloh: for this child I prayed; therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord. The law of vows: when thou vowest a vow unto the Lord thy God, thou shalt not slack to pay it.
cases.judgment: Eli answered, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition. The Lord remembered her, and she bare a son, and called his name Samuel. Her song: my heart rejoiceth in the Lord; the barren hath born seven. And the Lord visited Hannah, so that she conceived, and bare three sons and two daughters. And the child Samuel grew before the Lord, and all Israel from Dan to Beer-sheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord.

cases.name: Jael
cases.charge: Blessed above women in the tent: the nail, the hammer, and Sisera
cases.summary: Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Heber the Kenite, whose house was at peace with Jabin. Jael covered him with a mantle, gave him milk, and when he slept drove a tent nail through his temples into the ground. Deborah's song puts the blessing on her twice over.
cases.offense: Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said unto him, Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; fear not. He asked water and she gave him milk, and covered him. Then Jael Heber's wife took a nail of the tent, and took an hammer in her hand, and went softly unto him, and smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground: for he was fast asleep and weary. So he died. She had chosen Israel's side over her husband's peace with the oppressor.
cases.judgment: Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be, blessed shall she be above women in the tent. She put her hand to the nail, and her right hand to the workmen's hammer; and with the hammer she smote Sisera, she smote off his head. So let all thine enemies perish, O Lord: but let them that love him be as the sun when he goeth forth in his might. And the land had rest forty years.

cases.name: Ruth and Boaz
cases.charge: Ruth: cleaving to Naomi and to Naomi's God. Boaz: the law of gleaning, and the law of the kinsman, done to the letter
cases.summary: A Moabite widow left her people for a mother in law with nothing, and said, thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God. A man of Bethlehem let her glean, ordered handfuls dropped on purpose, and then went to the gate and redeemed her under the law before ten elders. Their son was Obed, the father of Jesse, the father of David.
cases.offense: Ruth: Intreat me not to leave thee; whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God. Boaz to Ruth: It hath fully been shewed me, all that thou hast done unto thy mother in law since the death of thine husband. Boaz to his reapers: Let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her. At the gate: The day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. And the near kinsman drew off his shoe.
cases.judgment: The Lord recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust. The Lord make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel. So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife; and the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son. Blessed be the Lord, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel. They called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

cases.name: Absalom
cases.charge: Murder of Amnon; conspiracy and rebellion against the king his father; lying with his father's concubines
cases.summary: David's son killed his brother, fled, was restored, then stole the hearts of Israel at the gate with flattery, raised a rebellion from Hebron, drove his father from Jerusalem, and lay with David's concubines on the roof before all Israel by Ahithophel's counsel.
cases.offense: The stubborn and rebellious son of Deuteronomy 21 on a national scale: murder, treason, and the uncovering of his father's bed as a political act. The rebellion was fueled by a daily lie at the gate: see, thy matters are good, but there is no man deputed of the king to hear thee.
cases.judgment: Caught by his hair in an oak as his mule went from under him, he was run through by Joab and ten armor-bearers, cast into a pit, and covered with a great heap of stones. He had raised a pillar for his own name; the stones were his monument instead.

cases.name: Adonijah
cases.charge: Exalting himself to be king; asking for the king's concubine
cases.summary: David's fourth son exalted himself, saying, I will be king, and gathered chariots, horsemen, Joab, and Abiathar for a coronation feast at En-rogel while David lay dying. Solomon was anointed the same day. Pardoned once, Adonijah then asked for Abishag the Shunammite.
cases.offense: The narrator notes that his father had never displeased him at any time in saying, why hast thou done so. He usurped a throne the Lord had assigned to Solomon by name. The request for Abishag was, as Solomon read it, a second bid for the kingdom through the king's woman.
cases.judgment: Solomon had spared him on condition of worthiness. The second offense was the end of it: Benaiah fell upon him and he died. Abiathar was banished and Joab executed in the same purge.

cases.name: Agag king of the Amalekites
cases.charge: The sword that made women childless
cases.summary: The Lord had sworn war with Amalek from generation to generation for what they did to Israel on the way out of Egypt. Saul was sent to finish it and spared Agag. Samuel did not: as thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women.
cases.offense: Agag was king of a people whose whole memory before the Lord was one act: smiting the feeble and the faint at the rear of Israel's march, without fear of God. In his own day he came to Samuel delicately, saying, Surely the bitterness of death is past, as though the old blood had dried.
cases.judgment: Samuel said, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites, and hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal. The sentence pronounced at Rephidim was carried out by a prophet's hand when the king's hand failed.

cases.name: Ahithophel
cases.charge: Treason against David; counsel of incest; suicide
cases.summary: David's counselor, whose word was as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God, joined Absalom, advised him to take his father's concubines publicly, and asked for twelve thousand men to kill David that night. When Hushai's counsel was preferred, he went home, set his house in order, and hanged himself.
cases.offense: Betrayal of the king he served, compounded by counsel that made the rebellion irreversible. Psalm 41 and Psalm 55 are read as David's lament over him: mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread. Peter cites the psalm of Judas.
cases.judgment: The Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the Lord might bring evil upon Absalom. He was buried in the sepulchre of his father, a self-executed sentence.

cases.name: Amnon
cases.charge: Rape of his sister Tamar
cases.summary: David's firstborn feigned sickness to get his half-sister alone, and when she pleaded that such a thing should not be done in Israel, forced her, then hated her more than he had loved her and had her thrown out. David was very wroth and did nothing.
cases.offense: Incest and rape together, both capital under the law he was heir to. Tamar had named the law and offered him the lawful way of asking the king; he would not hearken to her voice. Then he added public shame to the crime.
cases.judgment: Two years later Absalom had him killed at the sheep-shearing feast when his heart was merry with wine. Nathan's sentence on David's house, the sword shall never depart, began its work here.

cases.name: Baanah and Rechab
cases.charge: Murder of Ish-bosheth in his bed
cases.summary: Two captains of Saul's son entered his house at noon under pretense of fetching wheat, killed him as he lay on his bed, cut off his head, and carried it all night to David at Hebron expecting a reward.
cases.offense: Murder of a righteous person in his own house upon his bed, as David put it, done with guile for gain. They dressed it as service to the Lord's cause and David's.
cases.judgment: David commanded his young men to slay them; their hands and feet were cut off and hung over the pool in Hebron. Ish-bosheth's head was buried in Abner's grave.

cases.name: David and Bathsheba
cases.charge: Adultery and the arranged death of Uriah
cases.summary: The king took another man's wife, and when she conceived, engineered her husband's death to cover it. The prophet Nathan exposed it with a parable, and David confessed, but the consequences ran through his house for years.
cases.offense: David lay with Bathsheba, wife of Uriah the Hittite, then recalled Uriah to mask the pregnancy; when that failed, he had him set in the front of battle to die. Adultery, deceit, and murder by another's hand.
cases.judgment: The child died. Nathan declared that the sword would never depart from David's house, and it did not, his own sons rose against him. David was not executed; he repented, and the throne stood, but under a lasting wound.

cases.name: David's numbering of the people
cases.charge: Numbering Israel in pride; a plague on the nation
cases.summary: David commanded Joab to number Israel and Judah. Joab objected; the king's word prevailed. When the count came in, David's heart smote him: I have sinned greatly. Gad offered three judgments, and David chose to fall into the hand of the Lord.
