cases.offense: The narratives lay the provocation to God's anger against Israel and to Satan; the act is David's, and he owns it. A king measuring his strength in men, as if the Lord had not multiplied them and would not fight for them. Exodus required a ransom for every soul numbered, lest there be a plague among them.
cases.judgment: Pestilence: seventy thousand men died from Dan to Beersheba in three days. The angel stood at Araunah's threshingfloor with drawn sword when the Lord said, it is enough. David bought the floor and built an altar; it became the temple site.

cases.name: Goliath of Gath
cases.charge: Defying the armies of the living God, morning and evening, forty days
cases.summary: Six cubits and a span, with a spear like a weaver's beam, Goliath stood in the valley of Elah and reproached Israel for forty days. A shepherd boy came in the name of the Lord of hosts and took his head with his own sword.
cases.offense: He stood and cried unto the armies of Israel, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together. When David came he cursed him by his gods and promised his flesh to the fowls. David named the crime exactly: he hath defied the armies of the living God.
cases.judgment: This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand, that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. The stone sunk into his forehead and he fell upon his face to the earth; David stood upon him, drew his sword out of the sheath, and cut off his head with it. The Philistines fled and Israel spoiled their tents.

cases.name: Israel asking for a king
cases.charge: Rejecting the Lord's rule to be like the nations
cases.summary: The elders came to Samuel and demanded a king to judge them like all the nations. The Lord told Samuel: they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me. Warned what a king would take from them, they said, nay, but we will have a king over us.
cases.offense: Deuteronomy allowed a king on God's terms; Israel wanted one on the nations' terms, to go out before them and fight their battles, as if the Lord had not. Samuel later named it: your wickedness is great, which ye have done in the sight of the Lord, in asking you a king. Hosea: I gave thee a king in mine anger.
cases.judgment: The Lord granted the request and sent thunder and rain in wheat harvest as a sign of his displeasure. The people feared and confessed, and Samuel answered, fear not; ye have done all this wickedness, yet turn not aside from following the Lord. They got Saul.

cases.name: Joab
cases.charge: Murder of Abner and Amasa in time of peace
cases.summary: David's general killed Abner in the gate of Hebron under cover of a private word, avenging Asahel's death in battle, and years later killed Amasa with a kiss and a hidden sword. David laid both on Solomon's charge.
cases.offense: Two captains of the host, both under the king's protection, both killed by treachery outside any battle. David's sentence in life: the Lord shall reward the doer of evil according to his wickedness. His charge at death: he shed the blood of war in peace.
cases.judgment: Joab fled to the horns of the altar. Solomon cited the statute that the altar is no refuge for a murderer and sent Benaiah to kill him there, that the innocent blood be taken away from David's house. He was buried in his own house in the wilderness.

cases.name: King Saul
cases.charge: Unlawful sacrifice; sparing what was devoted; consulting a medium
cases.summary: A king undone by a pattern of partial obedience. He offered a sacrifice that was not his to offer, spared Agag and the best of the spoil against a direct command, and at the end sought a medium the law condemned.
cases.offense: At Gilgal he would not wait for Samuel and offered the burnt offering himself. Sent to devote Amalek utterly, he kept the king and the best livestock and called it sacrifice. Finally, cut off from God, he consulted the witch of Endor.
cases.judgment: The kingdom was torn from him and given to another. 'To obey is better than sacrifice.' He died by his own hand on Gilboa the next day, his sons with him.

cases.name: King Solomon
cases.charge: Multiplying foreign wives; building high places to their gods
cases.summary: The wisest king loved many strange women, seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, from the very nations the Lord had said, ye shall not go in to them. When he was old they turned his heart, and he built high places for Chemosh and Molech in the hill before Jerusalem.
cases.offense: Deuteronomy 17 forbade the king to multiply wives, horses, or silver, and named the reason: that his heart turn not away. Solomon did all three. Nehemiah cites him as the proof that even the beloved of God was made to sin by outlandish women. Sirach: thou didst stain thine honour and pollute thy seed.
cases.judgment: The Lord was angry, and told him the kingdom would be rent from his son and given to his servant, leaving one tribe for David's sake. Adversaries were raised up in his own lifetime; Jeroboam received the ten tribes at his death. So the kingdom was divided.

cases.name: Michal
cases.charge: Despising the king in her heart for dancing before the ark
cases.summary: As the ark came into the city of David with shouting and trumpets, Michal, Saul's daughter, watched from a window and despised David in her heart for leaping and dancing. She met him with contempt: how glorious was the king of Israel to day.
cases.offense: Contempt for worship, delivered as contempt for a husband. David answered that it was before the Lord, who chose him over her father's house, and that he would be yet more vile than thus.
cases.judgment: Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death. In Israel that was the end of a line; the house of Saul ended in her.

cases.name: Nabal
cases.charge: Churlish refusal of hospitality; railing on the Lord's anointed
cases.summary: David's men had guarded Nabal's shepherds all season. At sheep-shearing David asked for provision; Nabal, churlish and evil in his doings, answered, who is David? and sent them away. Abigail's wisdom stopped David's sword. The Lord did not stop his own.
cases.offense: Ingratitude and contempt where the law commands open hands, delivered by a man drunk at his own feast. His wife's verdict: as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him.
cases.judgment: Ten days after his heart died within him and became as a stone, the Lord smote Nabal, that he died. David blessed the Lord who had pleaded his cause and kept him from avenging himself.

cases.name: Saul and Doeg at Nob
cases.charge: Slaughter of the priests of the Lord on an informer's report
cases.summary: Doeg the Edomite, Saul's chief herdsman, told the king that Ahimelech had given David bread and Goliath's sword. Saul summoned the priests, condemned them unheard, and when his own guard refused to strike them, Doeg killed eighty-five men in linen ephods and then the whole city of Nob.
cases.offense: For Saul, judicial murder of the priesthood on a suspicion; Ahimelech's defense was true and ignored. For Doeg, a report shaped to kill and a hand willing to do what Israelites would not. Psalm 52 is David's indictment of him: thy tongue deviseth mischiefs, like a sharp razor.
cases.judgment: Psalm 52 pronounces it: God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place. Saul's own end came at Gilboa. Abiathar alone escaped Nob and carried the ephod to David.

cases.name: Saul's house and the Gibeonites
cases.charge: Breaking Israel's sworn covenant by slaying the Gibeonites
cases.summary: Three years of famine in David's reign were traced by inquiry of the Lord to Saul and his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites in his zeal for Israel, against the oath Joshua had sworn. David asked the Gibeonites what atonement they required.
cases.offense: Joshua's oath had been sworn by the Lord God of Israel four centuries before. Saul's breach of it was blood-guilt on the land, and the land, as Numbers says, cannot be cleansed of blood but by the blood of him that shed it.
cases.judgment: Seven of Saul's sons and grandsons were hanged before the Lord at Gibeah, sparing Mephibosheth for David's own oath to Jonathan. Rizpah kept the bodies from the birds until the rain came. Then David buried Saul's bones, and God was intreated for the land.

cases.name: Saul's rash oath, and the people at the blood
cases.charge: A rash oath that snared the army; the people eating flesh with the blood; the son who unknowingly broke the oath
cases.summary: Saul adjured the people to eat nothing until evening, and the army fainted in the pursuit. Jonathan, who had not heard, ate honey; the people, famished, fell on the spoil and ate with the blood; and when the lot fell on Jonathan the people would not let the king kill the man who had wrought the day's salvation.
cases.offense: Saul's oath was his own, not the Lord's, and it was a curse on any man that eateth any food until evening. The people were so faint that when evening came they flew upon the spoil and did eat with the blood, which the law forbids. Jonathan tasted a little honey on the end of his rod and his eyes were enlightened; he called his father's oath a trouble to the land.
cases.judgment: Saul was told, The people sin against the Lord, in that they eat with the blood, and he rolled a great stone and had the beasts slain on it, and built his first altar. Then the Lord answered him not, and the lot taken to find the cause fell on Jonathan. Saul swore he should surely die; the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not, on the witness that he had wrought with God that day. The oath was Saul's; the mercy was the people's; the silence was the Lord's.

cases.name: Sheba son of Bichri
cases.charge: Insurrection: we have no part in David
cases.summary: On the heels of Absalom's rebellion, Sheba the Benjamite blew a trumpet and cried, every man to his tents, O Israel, and all Israel went up after him. David judged him more dangerous than Absalom. He was besieged in Abel of Beth-maachah.
cases.offense: Rebellion against the established government, immediately after the last one had been crushed at the cost of twenty thousand men. A man of Belial, the text calls him.
cases.judgment: A wise woman of the city asked Joab why he would destroy a mother in Israel for one man; the people cut off Sheba's head and threw it over the wall, and Joab blew the trumpet and went home.

cases.name: Shimei son of Gera
cases.charge: Cursing the king and casting stones at him
cases.summary: As David fled Jerusalem, Shimei of Saul's house came out cursing and throwing stones and dust: come out, thou bloody man, thou man of Belial. David forbade Abishai to kill him and later swore he would not put him to death. Solomon inherited the case.
cases.offense: Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people. He did it in the king's face, in his hour of weakness, with the king's own guard at hand. His later apology at the Jordan was accepted for David's lifetime only.
cases.judgment: Solomon confined him to Jerusalem on pain of death. Three years later Shimei went to Gath after runaway servants, and Solomon had Benaiah kill him: the Lord shall return thy wickedness upon thine own head.

cases.name: The Amalekite who claimed to kill Saul
cases.charge: Claiming to have slain the Lord's anointed
cases.summary: A young Amalekite came to David at Ziklag with Saul's crown and bracelet and said he had killed the wounded king at his own request. The earlier chapter says Saul fell on his own sword. Either way, his mouth condemned him.
cases.offense: He expected reward for the death of Saul. David judged him on his own testimony: how wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thine hand to destroy the Lord's anointed? Whether he lied for gain or did the deed, the charge stood.
cases.judgment: Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee. David had him executed on the spot.

cases.name: Uzzah and the ark
cases.charge: Touching the ark, transported unlawfully
cases.summary: The ark was moved on a new cart rather than borne by the Levites as the law required. When the oxen stumbled, Uzzah put out his hand to steady it and died at once.
cases.offense: The deeper fault was corporate: the ark was to be carried on staves by Kohathites, never touched, never carted. Uzzah's reach was the moment the accumulated carelessness came due.
cases.judgment: God struck him for his error, and he died there beside the ark. David, first angry then afraid, left the ark three months until he learned to move it the way the law prescribed.

cases.name: Abigail
cases.charge: Keeping David from shedding blood and avenging himself with his own hand
cases.summary: Her husband Nabal railed on David's men; David strapped on his sword to kill every male of the house by morning. Abigail met him on the road with two hundred loaves and a speech that is one of the wisest in scripture, and turned him back. Ten days later the Lord smote Nabal, and David sent for her.
cases.offense: Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and fell before David on her face: Now therefore, my lord, as the Lord liveth, seeing the Lord hath withholden thee from coming to shed blood, and from avenging thyself with thine own hand. The Lord will certainly make my lord a sure house; because my lord fighteth the battles of the Lord, and evil hath not been found in thee all thy days. That this shall be no grief unto thee, nor offence of heart unto my lord, that thou hast shed blood causeless.
cases.judgment: David said to Abigail, Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, which sent thee this day to meet me: and blessed be thy advice, and blessed be thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself with mine own hand. When Nabal was dead, David sent and communed with Abigail, to take her to him to wife; and she became his wife, and bore him Chileab. The ill-married wife of a churl became the wife of the king, for a wise word spoken in time.

cases.name: Barzillai the Gileadite
cases.charge: Bringing beds, wheat, and honey to the king and his hungry men in the wilderness at Mahanaim
cases.summary: When David fled from Absalom, an old man of Rogelim brought provision for the king and the people with him, saying, The people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness. David wanted to keep him at court for life. Barzillai was eighty and asked only to die in his own city; David took his son instead, and charged Solomon on his deathbed to remember the house.
cases.offense: Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim brought beds, and basons, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched corn, and beans, and lentiles, and honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine, for David, and for the people that were with him, to eat: for they said, The people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness. He had provided the king of sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he was a very great man.
cases.judgment: The king said unto Barzillai, Come thou over with me, and I will feed thee with me in Jerusalem. Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, that will I do for thee. And the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him. David to Solomon: shew kindness unto the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be of those that eat at thy table: for so they came to me when I fled because of Absalom thy brother. Centuries later his family was still known by his name.

cases.name: David
cases.charge: A man after the Lord's own heart; keeping his commandments and following him with all his heart, save only in the matter of Uriah
cases.summary: Shepherd, giant-killer, hunted man who twice had Saul in his hand and would not touch the Lord's anointed, king who danced before the ark and would not build a house until told he could. The Lord made a covenant with his house that has a Son sitting on it for ever. His one great fall is its own case; this is the rest.
cases.offense: The Lord hath sought him a man after his own heart. The Lord forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the Lord's anointed, to stretch forth mine hand against him. He judged and did justice unto all his people. Because David did that which was right in the eyes of the Lord, and turned not aside from any thing that he commanded him all the days of his life, save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite. His own words: I have kept the ways of the Lord, and have not wickedly departed from my God. For all his judgments were before me, and I did not put away his statutes from me.
cases.judgment: Thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever. Therefore the Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands in his eyesight. The sure mercies of David. He gave them a king, David, to whom also he gave testimony, and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will. Of this man's seed hath God according to his promise raised unto Israel a Saviour, Jesus.

cases.name: Obed-edom the Gittite
cases.charge: Keeping the ark of God in his house three months, after it had killed Uzzah
cases.summary: Uzzah had just died for touching the ark, and David was afraid to bring it into the city. It went instead into the house of Obed-edom of Gath, and stayed three months. The Lord blessed him and all his household so visibly that David heard of it and came back for the ark with sacrifices and dancing.
cases.offense: David was afraid of the Lord that day, and said, How shall the ark of the Lord come to me? So David would not remove the ark of the Lord unto him into the city of David: but David carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. He took in what the king was afraid of, and kept it as it was meant to be kept.
cases.judgment: And the ark of the Lord continued in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months: and the Lord blessed Obed-edom, and all his household. It was told king David, saying, The Lord hath blessed the house of Obed-edom, and all that pertaineth unto him, because of the ark of God. The Chronicles count him afterward among the porters and the singers before the ark, with eight sons and sixty-two able men of his house: for God blessed him.

cases.name: Solomon at Gibeon
cases.charge: Asking for an understanding heart to judge the people, and not for long life, riches, or the life of his enemies
cases.summary: Offered anything he wanted, the young king asked for wisdom to judge a great people. The speech pleased the Lord, who gave him the wisdom and added the riches and honour he had not asked. The kingdom he built on it was the greatest Israel ever had. What he did with his wives afterward is another case.
cases.offense: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people? And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing. In Wisdom: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me; I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.
cases.judgment: Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies; but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment; behold, I have done according to thy words: lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee. And I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour. All the earth sought to Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.

cases.name: Ahab
cases.charge: Marrying Jezebel; serving Baal; sparing Ben-hadad whom the Lord appointed to destruction
cases.summary: Ahab did more to provoke the Lord than all the kings before him: he married a Zidonian, built Baal a house in Samaria, and made a grove. He spared the king of Syria for a trade deal after the Lord gave him the victory, and sold himself to work wickedness in Naboth's vineyard.
cases.offense: Idolatry, intermarriage, and the release of an enemy God had devoted, on top of the judicial murder his wife arranged for him. Elijah's word: thou hast sold thyself to work evil in the sight of the Lord.
cases.judgment: Because he humbled himself at Elijah's sentence, the evil on his house was deferred to his son's days. His own end was not: an arrow at a venture found the joints of his harness at Ramoth-gilead, and dogs licked his blood at the pool of Samaria as the Lord had said.

cases.name: Ahab the son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah
cases.charge: Prophesying lies in the Lord's name to the captives; committing adultery with their neighbours' wives
cases.summary: Two prophets among the exiles told the captives the exile would be short. The Lord's letter by Jeremiah named them, named their adultery, and named their end: roasted in the fire by the king of Babylon, and their names turned into a curse.
cases.offense: They have committed villany in Israel, and have committed adultery with their neighbours' wives, and have spoken lying words in my name, which I have not commanded them; even I know, and am a witness, saith the Lord.
cases.judgment: Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, of Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and of Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, which prophesy a lie unto you in my name; Behold, I will deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon; and he shall slay them before your eyes; and of them shall be taken up a curse by all the captivity of Judah which are in Babylon, saying, The Lord make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire.

cases.name: Ahaz
cases.charge: Burning his children in the fire; copying the altar of Damascus; sacrificing to the gods that smote him
cases.summary: Ahaz walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, made molten images for Baalim, burnt his children in the fire after the abominations of the heathen, and hired Assyria against Syria with the temple's silver. Defeated, he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus because they had helped his enemies.
cases.offense: Child sacrifice, the sin the Canaanites were destroyed for; a pagan altar pattern installed in the Lord's house; shutting up the temple doors; and the logic of a lost man, worship whoever is winning. Wisdom describes the Canaanites he imitated as merciless murderers of children.
cases.judgment: The Lord delivered him into the hand of Syria and of Israel, who slew a hundred and twenty thousand in one day, and Assyria distressed him instead of strengthening him. In the time of his distress did he trespass yet more against the Lord: this is that king Ahaz. He was buried outside the kings' sepulchres.

cases.name: Ahaziah of Israel
cases.charge: Inquiring of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron
cases.summary: Ahab's son fell through a lattice in Samaria and sent messengers to ask Baal-zebub whether he would recover. Elijah met them on the road: is it not because there is not a God in Israel that ye go to inquire of Baal-zebub? Two captains of fifty sent to arrest the prophet were consumed by fire.
cases.offense: A king of Israel treating a Philistine idol as his oracle, and then sending soldiers against the man who told him so. The law forbids the ruler to consult mediums and spiritists, and forbids the people to listen to them.
cases.judgment: Thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die. So he died according to the word of the Lord which Elijah had spoken, and having no son, his brother reigned.

cases.name: Ahaziah of Judah
cases.charge: Walking in the ways of the house of Ahab, his mother being his counsellor to do wickedly
cases.summary: Athaliah's son reigned one year. He took the house of Ahab for his counsellors after his father's death, went with Joram to war, and went to visit him in Jezreel on the very day Jehu came to execute the house of Ahab. His destruction, the chronicler says, was of God.
cases.offense: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly. Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the Lord like the house of Ahab, for they were his counsellors after the death of his father to his destruction. He walked also after their counsel, and went with Jehoram to fight against Hazael.
cases.judgment: The destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram: for when he was come, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu, whom the Lord had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab. Jehu's men found him hid in Samaria, brought him to Jehu, and slew him; and they buried him, because, they said, he is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart. His father's name bought him a grave; his mother's counsel had cost him the throne.

cases.name: Amaziah
cases.charge: Bringing home the gods of Seir and bowing to them
cases.summary: Having beaten Edom with the Lord's help, Amaziah brought back the gods of the children of Seir, set them up as his gods, and burned incense to them. A prophet asked why he sought gods that could not deliver their own people; the king told him to stop before he was smitten.
cases.offense: Worship of the defeated enemy's idols, which the law says are to be burned, not carried home. Then, lifted up in pride, he provoked a war with Israel he was warned against and lost.
cases.judgment: The prophet's parting word: I know that God hath determined to destroy thee, because thou hast done this. Israel broke down Jerusalem's wall and plundered the temple; after that Amaziah's own people conspired against him at Lachish and killed him there.

cases.name: Amaziah the priest of Bethel
cases.charge: Forbidding Amos to prophesy at the king's chapel; accusing him to Jeroboam of conspiracy
cases.summary: A priest of the calf at Bethel sent word to Jeroboam that Amos had conspired against him, then told the prophet to go earn his bread in Judah. Amos answered that he was no prophet's son but a herdman the Lord had taken from the flock, and gave Amaziah a sentence for his wife, his children, his land and himself.
cases.offense: Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words. Also Amaziah said unto Amos, O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there: but prophesy not again any more at Bethel: for it is the king's chapel, and it is the king's court.
cases.judgment: Thou sayest, Prophesy not against Israel. Therefore thus saith the Lord; Thy wife shall be an harlot in the city, and thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword, and thy land shall be divided by line; and thou shalt die in a polluted land: and Israel shall surely go into captivity forth of his land.

cases.name: Amon
cases.charge: Serving his father's idols and refusing his father's repentance
cases.summary: Manasseh's son reigned two years, sacrificed to all the carved images his father had made, and humbled not himself before the Lord as Manasseh had humbled himself, but trespassed more and more.
cases.offense: He had both examples in one man, the apostasy and the repentance, and chose the first. He forsook the Lord God of his fathers and walked not in the way of the Lord.
cases.judgment: His own servants conspired against him and slew him in his house. The people of the land killed the conspirators and made Josiah, eight years old, king in his stead.

cases.name: Asa in his latter years
cases.charge: Hiring the king of Syria against Israel; imprisoning the seer who reproved him; seeking to the physicians and not to the Lord
cases.summary: For thirty-five years Asa was one of Judah's best kings. Then Baasha fortified Ramah, and Asa emptied the temple treasury to buy Ben-hadad's help instead of relying on the Lord who had given him the Ethiopians. Rebuked, he put the seer in the stocks; diseased, he sought physicians; and he died in the forty-first year of his reign.
cases.offense: Hanani the seer said: Because thou hast relied on the king of Syria, and not relied on the Lord thy God, therefore is the host of the king of Syria escaped out of thine hand. Were not the Ethiopians a huge host? Yet because thou didst rely on the Lord he delivered them into thine hand. Asa was wroth with the seer and put him in a prison house, and oppressed some of the people the same time. When his feet were diseased, in his disease he sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians.
cases.judgment: Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars. The disease in his feet became exceeding great, and he slept with his fathers in the forty-first year. The chronicler is careful to keep the account whole: the heart of Asa was perfect all his days, and the last chapter is still written.

cases.name: Athaliah
cases.charge: Destroying the seed royal of Judah; usurping the throne
cases.summary: Ahab's daughter, married into Judah's line, saw her son Ahaziah dead at Jehu's hand and murdered all the seed royal to reign herself. One infant, Joash, was hidden in the house of the Lord for six years. In the seventh, Jehoiada the priest brought him out.
cases.offense: Mass murder of her own grandchildren for a crown, and six years of Baal worship in Jerusalem: her sons had broken up the house of God and given its dedicated things to Baalim.
cases.judgment: She heard the trumpets, rent her clothes, and cried, treason. Jehoiada would not have her killed in the house of the Lord; they took her out by the horse gate and slew her there. Then the people tore down Baal's house and killed Mattan his priest.

cases.name: Baasha
cases.charge: Walking in the way of Jeroboam after being raised up to destroy Jeroboam's house
cases.summary: Baasha killed Nadab and every soul of the house of Jeroboam, exactly as Ahijah had prophesied. Then he reigned twenty-four years in the same sins, and the same prophecy was spoken over his own house by Jehu the son of Hanani.
cases.offense: He conspired against Nadab at Gibbethon and slew him, and left not to Jeroboam any that breathed. That was the word of the Lord. But he walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin, wherewith he made Israel to sin, and provoked the Lord with the work of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam, and because he killed him.
cases.judgment: Forasmuch as I exalted thee out of the dust and made thee prince over my people Israel, and thou hast walked in the way of Jeroboam: I will take away the posterity of Baasha. Him that dieth of Baasha in the city shall the dogs eat. Zimri did it in the days of Elah his son, leaving him not one that pisseth against a wall, neither of his kinsfolks nor of his friends.

cases.name: Babylon, the lady of kingdoms
cases.charge: Showing no mercy to the captives; saying, I am, and none else beside me; trusting in her sorceries
cases.summary: Babylon was the Lord's hammer against Judah, and was judged for how she swung it: without mercy, laying a heavy yoke on the ancient, and saying in her heart, I shall be a lady for ever. Isaiah and Jeremiah both name the end before the beginning: the Medes, the sudden fall, the perpetual desolation.
cases.offense: I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand: thou didst shew them no mercy; upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke. And thou saidst, I shall be a lady for ever. Thou hast trusted in thy wickedness: thou hast said, None seeth me. Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee; and thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me. Jeremiah adds the account: they have devoured Israel; the violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon, shall the inhabitant of Zion say.
cases.judgment: Therefore shall evil come upon thee; thou shalt not know from whence it riseth. Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon. Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them. Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees' excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah; it shall never be inhabited. Belshazzar saw the hand write it on the wall the night it came.

cases.name: Ben-hadad and the Syrians at Aphek
cases.charge: Saying the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys
cases.summary: Beaten at Samaria, the Syrians told their king the God of Israel was a hill god and would lose on level ground. The Lord heard it. A prophet told Ahab the outcome before the battle: that ye may know that I am the Lord.
cases.offense: The servants of the king of Syria said, Their gods are gods of the hills; therefore they were stronger than we: but let us fight against them in the plain, and surely we shall be stronger than they. Ben-hadad numbered the Syrians and went up to Aphek with a host that filled the country.
cases.judgment: Because the Syrians have said, The Lord is God of the hills, but he is not God of the valleys, therefore will I deliver all this great multitude into thine hand. Israel slew of the Syrians an hundred thousand footmen in one day; the rest fled to Aphek, and a wall fell on twenty and seven thousand of them. Ben-hadad survived only because Ahab, against the word of the Lord, let him go.

cases.name: Edom, in the day of his brother
cases.charge: Standing on the other side when strangers carried Jacob away; rejoicing over Judah's fall; cutting off those that escaped
cases.summary: When Babylon took Jerusalem, Esau's descendants looked on, entered the gate in the day of calamity, laid hands on the substance, stood in the crossway to cut off the fugitives, and delivered up those that remained. Psalm 137 remembers them shouting, rase it, rase it, even to the foundation.
cases.offense: Obadiah: for thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee. Amos: he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually. The law had forbidden Israel to abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother; Edom kept no such law.
cases.judgment: As thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head. The house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble; there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau. Malachi: they shall build, but I will throw down.

cases.name: Gehazi
cases.charge: Greed and lying to a prophet
cases.summary: Elisha refused payment from the healed Syrian Naaman. His servant Gehazi ran after Naaman, invented a story to collect silver and garments, then lied to Elisha's face about where he had been.
cases.offense: Covetousness turned to fraud: he claimed the prophet had sent him, took the goods, hid them, and denied it. He traded the integrity of the prophetic office for money.
cases.judgment: Elisha, knowing all of it, pronounced that Naaman's leprosy would cling to Gehazi and his seed forever. He went out from his presence a leper, white as snow.

cases.name: Hananiah the son of Azur
cases.charge: Prophesying a lie in the name of the Lord
cases.summary: In the temple, before the priests and all the people, Hananiah declared that the Lord would break Babylon's yoke within two years and bring back the vessels and the captives. He broke the wooden yoke from Jeremiah's neck to prove it.
cases.offense: Deuteronomy's test: the prophet who presumes to speak a word in my name which I have not commanded him, that prophet shall die. He made the people to trust in a lie and preached rebellion against the Lord, who had told Judah to serve Babylon.
cases.judgment: Jeremiah: the Lord hath not sent thee. This year thou shalt die, because thou hast taught rebellion against the Lord. So Hananiah the prophet died the same year in the seventh month.

cases.name: Hezekiah and the ambassadors of Babylon
cases.charge: Showing all his treasures to Babylon in the pride of his heart
cases.summary: Healed of a mortal sickness and given fifteen years, Hezekiah received envoys from Babylon and showed them the house of his precious things, the silver, the gold, the armor, everything. Isaiah asked what they had seen. Nothing hidden, said the king.
cases.offense: Chronicles: Hezekiah rendered not again according to the benefit done unto him, for his heart was lifted up. God left him, to try him, that he might know all that was in his heart. A king glorying in his riches before the empire that would carry them away.
cases.judgment: All that is in thine house shall be carried into Babylon, and of thy sons shall they take away, and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon. Hezekiah humbled himself, and the wrath came not in his days: is it not good, if peace and truth be in my days?

cases.name: Hiel the Bethelite
cases.charge: Rebuilding Jericho under the oath Joshua swore before the Lord
cases.summary: When Jericho fell, Joshua adjured Israel: cursed be the man that riseth up and buildeth this city; he shall lay the foundation in his firstborn and set up the gates in his youngest son. Five hundred years later, in the days of Ahab, Hiel built it, and buried both.
cases.offense: In the days of Ahab, when every old boundary was being moved, Hiel of Bethel undertook what the oath forbade and rebuilt Jericho. Whether he mocked the curse or had never learned it, he laid the foundation and hung the gates.
cases.judgment: He laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Joshua the son of Nun. The sentence waited five centuries and lost nothing in the waiting.

cases.name: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah
cases.charge: Murder of Gedaliah the governor at his own table; slaughter of the Jews and Chaldeans with him, and of seventy pilgrims
cases.summary: Of the seed royal, hired by the king of the Ammonites, Ishmael ate bread with Gedaliah at Mizpah and killed him, then killed the men with him, then killed seventy mourners on their way to the house of the Lord and threw them in a pit. He escaped to Ammon with eight men. Scripture records no sentence on him; it records what his deed cost the remnant.
cases.offense: Johanan had warned Gedaliah that Baalis king of the Ammonites had sent Ishmael to slay him, and Gedaliah believed him not. Ishmael came with ten men and they did eat bread together in Mizpah, and there he smote Gedaliah with the sword, and slew him whom the king of Babylon had made governor. Fourscore men came from Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria with offerings; he went out weeping to meet them and slew them and cast them into the pit, sparing ten for their hidden treasures.
cases.judgment: Johanan recovered the captives at the great waters of Gibeon, but Ishmael escaped from Johanan and went to the Ammonites. No court reached him and no plague is written. What the deed left behind was a remnant so afraid of the Chaldeans that they fled to Egypt against the word of the Lord, and died there. The law's sentence on the murderer stands written where he cannot flee it.

cases.name: Jehoahaz (Shallum) of Judah
cases.charge: Doing evil in the sight of the Lord according to all that his fathers had done
cases.summary: Josiah's son reigned three months. Pharaoh-necho put him in bands at Riblah, laid tribute on the land, and carried him to Egypt, where he died. Jeremiah told the people to weep not for the dead Josiah but for the son who would never see his native country again.
cases.offense: Jehoahaz was twenty and three years old when he began to reign; and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done. He had his father's throne and none of his father's tender heart.
cases.judgment: Pharaoh-nechoh put him in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem; and put the land to a tribute. Jeremiah: Weep ye not for the dead, neither bemoan him: but weep sore for him that goeth away: for he shall return no more, nor see his native country. He shall die in the place whither they have led him captive, and shall see this land no more. He is the first of the last four kings of Judah, and the first to die in exile.

cases.name: Jehoiachin (Coniah)
cases.charge: Doing evil as his father Jehoiakim had done; a signet plucked from the Lord's right hand
cases.summary: Eighteen years old and three months on the throne when Nebuchadnezzar came. Jeremiah's word over him is one of the hardest in the book: though Coniah were the signet on my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence; write ye this man childless, for no man of his seed shall prosper sitting upon the throne of David.
cases.offense: Jehoiachin did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father had done. He inherited Jehoiakim's throne and Jehoiakim's ways, and the wrath that had been laid up against the house.
cases.judgment: I will give thee into the hand of them that seek thy life, and I will cast thee out, and thy mother that bare thee, into another country, where ye were not born; and there shall ye die. He went out to the king of Babylon with his mother, his servants, his princes and his officers, and was carried away with ten thousand captives and all the craftsmen and smiths. Thirty-seven years later Evil-merodach lifted up his head out of prison and set his throne above the kings that were with him in Babylon: a kindness, still in Babylon.

cases.name: Jehoiakim
cases.charge: Building with unrighteousness; shedding innocent blood; burning the scroll of the Lord's words
cases.summary: Necho's puppet king built a great house with unpaid labor, killed the prophet Urijah for prophesying like Jeremiah, and when Jeremiah's scroll was read to him, cut it with a penknife leaf by leaf and burned it in the hearth. Neither he nor his servants were afraid.
cases.offense: Jeremiah's indictment: thine eyes and thine heart are not but for thy covetousness, and for to shed innocent blood, and for oppression, and for violence. Withholding wages, murder of a prophet, and the deliberate destruction of the written word.
cases.judgment: He shall be buried with the burial of an ass, drawn and cast forth beyond the gates of Jerusalem. He shall have none to sit upon the throne of David, and his dead body shall be cast out in the day to the heat and in the night to the frost. His son reigned three months and went to Babylon; his brother was the last king.

cases.name: Jehoram of Judah
cases.charge: Slaying all his brethren with the sword; walking in the way of the house of Ahab; making high places and compelling Judah to fornication
cases.summary: Jehoshaphat's eldest son married Ahab's daughter, killed his six brothers to secure the throne, and led Judah to the high places. A writing came to him from Elijah naming the sentence: a great plague on his people, his children and his wives, and a disease of the bowels that would take two years to kill him.
cases.offense: When Jehoram was risen up to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself and slew all his brethren with the sword, and divers also of the princes of Israel. He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, like as did the house of Ahab, for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife. He made high places in the mountains of Judah and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit fornication, and compelled Judah thereto.
cases.judgment: Edom revolted, and Libnah. The Philistines and Arabians came up and carried away all the substance of the king's house, and his sons also and his wives, so that there was never a son left him save the youngest. After all this the Lord smote him in his bowels with an incurable disease, and after two years his bowels fell out and he died of sore diseases. His people made no burning for him; he departed without being desired; and they buried him in the city of David, but not in the sepulchres of the kings.

cases.name: Jehoshaphat's alliances
cases.charge: Joining affinity with Ahab; going to Ramoth-gilead with him; joining with Ahaziah to make ships
cases.summary: A king who sought the Lord and taught the law through Judah kept making common cause with the house of Ahab. He nearly died at Ramoth-gilead in Ahab's place, was told by Jehu the seer that wrath was upon him for helping the ungodly, and later lost a whole fleet at Ezion-geber for the same fault.
cases.offense: Jehoshaphat had riches and honour in abundance, and joined affinity with Ahab. He went down to Samaria and said, I am as thou art, and my people as thy people; and we will be with thee in the war. Years afterward he joined himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, who did very wickedly, to make ships to go to Tarshish.
cases.judgment: At Ramoth-gilead the captains of the chariots compassed him about to fight, and he cried out, and the Lord helped him and moved them to depart from him. On his return Jehu the son of Hanani met him: Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the Lord? therefore is wrath upon thee from before the Lord. Of the ships, Eliezer prophesied, Because thou hast joined thyself with Ahaziah, the Lord hath broken thy works; and the ships were broken, that they were not able to go to Tarshish.

cases.name: Jehu
cases.charge: Executing the house of Ahab, then keeping the calves of Jeroboam
cases.summary: Anointed to cut off the house of Ahab, Jehu killed Joram, Ahaziah, Jezebel, seventy sons of Ahab, and every worshipper of Baal in Samaria, and destroyed Baal out of Israel. But from the golden calves at Bethel and Dan Jehu departed not.
cases.offense: Zeal for the Lord that stopped exactly where it became inconvenient to the throne. He took no heed to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart. Hosea adds that the blood of Jezreel would be visited on his house, judging the manner of his executions even where the sentence was God's.
cases.judgment: Because he had done well in executing what was right, his sons sat on Israel's throne to the fourth generation. Because of the calves, the Lord began in those days to cut Israel short: Hazael smote them in all their coasts. His dynasty ended with Zechariah, murdered after six months.

cases.name: Jeroboam son of Nebat
cases.charge: Two golden calves; priests of the lowest of the people; a feast devised of his own heart
cases.summary: Given ten tribes by the Lord, Jeroboam feared the people would return to Jerusalem to worship, so he set calves in Bethel and Dan, saying, behold thy gods, O Israel, made priests of any who were not Levites, and moved the feast to a month of his own choosing. Every king of Israel after him is measured by his sin.
cases.offense: State idolatry engineered for political security, borrowing the words of Aaron's calf. He was warned at the altar itself by a man of God from Judah, saw his hand wither, and after all this returned not from his evil way.
cases.judgment: The Lord promised to cut off from Jeroboam every male, and to take away the remnant of his house as a man takes away dung. Baasha killed his son Nadab and all his house. Israel's captivity two centuries later is charged to the sins of Jeroboam, which he made Israel to sin.

cases.name: Jezebel
cases.charge: Killing the prophets of the Lord; promoting Baal; witchcrafts
cases.summary: Ahab's Zidonian queen cut off the prophets of the Lord, fed four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal at her table, swore to kill Elijah, and stirred up her husband to every evil. Jehu named her whoredoms and witchcrafts as the reason there could be no peace.
cases.offense: A foreign woman ruling a king of Israel into apostasy, with the machinery of state turned against the Lord's prophets. Revelation makes her name the type of the woman who calls herself a prophetess and teaches the servants of God to commit fornication and eat things sacrificed to idols.
cases.judgment: Elijah pronounced it: the dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel. Jehu had her eunuchs throw her from the window; horses trod her underfoot, and when they went to bury her they found no more than the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands.

cases.name: Jezebel and Naboth's vineyard
cases.charge: Judicial murder to seize an inheritance
cases.summary: Ahab coveted Naboth's vineyard; Naboth would not sell his fathers' inheritance. Jezebel arranged false witnesses to accuse him of blaspheming God and the king, had him stoned, and handed the land to Ahab.
cases.offense: Covetousness executed through the machinery of law itself: a proclaimed fast, suborned witnesses, a capital charge, and a stoning, every step a mockery of the statutes it borrowed.
cases.judgment: Elijah met Ahab in the stolen vineyard with a sentence on the whole house. Dogs would lick Ahab's blood and eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel. Both came to pass.

cases.name: Joash of Judah
cases.charge: Forsaking the Lord after Jehoiada's death; stoning Zechariah in the temple court
cases.summary: The boy king saved by the priest Jehoiada did right all the days of Jehoiada. When the priest died, the princes of Judah came and Joash hearkened to them, left the house of the Lord, and served groves and idols. Jehoiada's son Zechariah rebuked him by the Spirit; the king had him stoned in the court of the temple.
cases.offense: Apostasy the moment his mentor's restraint was gone, then the murder of that mentor's son for prophesying against it. Thus Joash the king remembered not the kindness which Jehoiada his father had done to him. Christ counts Zechariah's blood among the prophets' blood required of that generation.
cases.judgment: Zechariah's dying word, the Lord look upon it and require it, was answered within the year: a small Syrian company defeated a very great host, and his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada and slew him on his bed. He was not buried in the sepulchres of the kings.

cases.name: Johanan and the remnant that went down to Egypt
cases.charge: Asking the word of the Lord, swearing to obey it, and refusing it; burning incense to the queen of heaven in Egypt
cases.summary: The remnant asked Jeremiah to pray for direction and swore to obey whatever the Lord said. Ten days later the answer came: stay in the land and I will build you; go to Egypt and the sword you fear will overtake you there. They called the prophet a liar, took him with them to Egypt, and there openly returned to the queen of heaven.
cases.offense: Ye dissembled in your hearts, when ye sent me unto the Lord your God, saying, Pray for us unto the Lord our God; and according unto all that the Lord our God shall say, so declare unto us, and we will do it. In Egypt the men who knew their wives burned incense to other gods answered Jeremiah: we will certainly do whatsoever thing goeth forth out of our own mouth, to burn incense unto the queen of heaven, as we did in the cities of Judah; for then had we plenty of victuals.
cases.judgment: Then it shall come to pass, that the sword, which ye feared, shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine, whereof ye were afraid, shall follow close after you there in Egypt; and there ye shall die. I will take the remnant of Judah, that have set their faces to go into the land of Egypt, and they shall all be consumed, and fall in the land of Egypt; none shall return but such as shall escape. The sign given was Pharaoh-hophra delivered into the hand of his enemies, as Zedekiah had been.

cases.name: Jonah
cases.charge: Fleeing from the presence of the Lord to avoid his commission; anger at God's mercy
cases.summary: Told to go east to Nineveh, Jonah bought passage west to Tarshish. A storm, a lot, and a fish brought him back. He preached, the city repented, and he was angry enough to die because God spared it. A gourd, a worm, and a wind finished the lesson.
cases.offense: Refusal of a prophet's commission, with the reason given afterward in his own words: I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful. He would rather drown than see Nineveh forgiven. Then anger without cause, twice, at the mercy he himself had received.
cases.judgment: Three days and nights in the belly of the fish, out of which he prayed and was vomited on dry land, and the word of the Lord came the second time. The book ends on God's question, unanswered: should not I spare Nineveh? Christ made his three days the sign of the resurrection.

cases.name: Josiah at Megiddo
cases.charge: Going to battle against Necho without inquiring of the Lord
cases.summary: The reformer king, promised he would be gathered to his grave in peace, went out against Pharaoh Necho, who was marching to Carchemish and had no quarrel with Judah. Necho sent word that God had commanded him to make haste and that Josiah should not meddle with God, who was with him. Josiah disguised himself and fought anyway.
cases.offense: Chronicles is unusually direct: he hearkened not unto the words of Necho from the mouth of God. A war without cause, without inquiry, against a warning the narrator credits as divine. The best king since David died of a battle that was not his.
cases.judgment: Archers hit him in the valley of Megiddo; his servants carried him to Jerusalem and he died. Jeremiah lamented for him, and the lament became an ordinance in Israel. The promise of a peaceful grave was kept in the sense that he did not see the evil that followed.

cases.name: Manasseh
cases.charge: Rebuilding the high places; altars to the host of heaven in the temple; passing his sons through the fire; witchcraft; filling Jerusalem with innocent blood
cases.summary: Hezekiah's son undid everything his father had done and more: altars for Baal, a grove, worship of all the host of heaven in both courts of the Lord's house, his children through the fire, observing times, enchantments, familiar spirits, wizards. He shed innocent blood until Jerusalem was filled from one end to another.
cases.offense: The record says he seduced Judah to do more evil than the nations the Lord destroyed before them. Every capital offense against God in the handbook's tenth part appears in his reign. Judah's captivity, decades later, is charged to him by name.
cases.judgment: The Lord brought the captains of the host of Assyria, who took Manasseh among the thorns, bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon. There he humbled himself greatly and prayed; the Prayer of Manasseh preserves the tradition of it. God brought him back to his kingdom and he took away the strange gods. But the sentence on Judah for his sins stood: the Lord would not pardon.

cases.name: Moab and Ammon
cases.charge: Magnifying themselves against the Lord and against his people; rejoicing over the sanctuary when it was profaned
cases.summary: Lot's two sons, neighbours to Israel from the wilderness on, are judged in Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Amos and Zephaniah for one long habit: pride against the Lord and gladness at Judah's ruin. Ammon ripped up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge its border; Moab said, Aha, against the house of Judah.
cases.offense: We have heard of the pride of Moab; he is very proud: of his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart. He shall be no more praised, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord. Of Ammon: because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary, when it was profaned; and against the land of Israel, when it was desolate; and against the house of Judah, when they went into captivity. Amos: they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border.
cases.judgment: Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord. Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days. Of Ammon: I will deliver thee to the men of the east for a possession, and Rabbah shall be a stable for camels; Zephaniah: Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation. Nebuchadnezzar came through both.

cases.name: Nineveh under Jonah
cases.charge: Wickedness come up before the Lord
cases.summary: Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown. The people believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth from the greatest to the least; the king rose from his throne, sat in ashes, and decreed that man and beast cry mightily unto God and turn from the violence in their hands.
cases.offense: The charge is given in one line, their wickedness is come up before me, and Nahum a century later spells out what Assyria's wickedness was: a bloody city, full of lies and robbery, whose prey departeth not.
cases.judgment: God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way, and repented of the evil that he had said he would do unto them. Jeremiah states the rule: if that nation turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil I thought to do. Christ: the men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation and condemn it.

cases.name: Nineveh under Nahum
cases.charge: A bloody city, full of lies and robbery, mistress of witchcrafts
cases.summary: The repentance of Jonah's day did not last. Nahum's burden against Nineveh charges the city with blood, plunder, harlotries, and witchcrafts by which she sold nations; the Lord is slow to anger, and will not at all acquit the wicked.
cases.offense: Assyria had been the rod of God's anger against Israel and then gloried in its own hand. Zephaniah names the heart of it: this is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me.
cases.judgment: The gates of the rivers shall be opened, and the palace dissolved. Nineveh is laid waste; who will bemoan her? There is no healing of thy bruise. Tobit records hearing of its destruction by Nebuchadnezzar and Ahasuerus before he died, and rejoicing over it.

cases.name: Pashur the son of Immer
cases.charge: Smiting the prophet and putting him in the stocks; prophesying lies
cases.summary: Pashur, chief governor in the house of the Lord, heard Jeremiah prophesy the city's fall, struck him, and put him in the stocks at the high gate of Benjamin overnight. In the morning Jeremiah gave him a new name.
cases.offense: A priest using his office to punish the word of God, while himself prophesying comfort that was a lie. The law reserves stripes for the wicked after judgment; he used them on the Lord's messenger before any.
cases.judgment: The Lord hath not called thy name Pashur, but Magor-missabib, terror on every side. Thou shalt go into captivity to Babylon, and there thou shalt die and be buried, thou and all thy friends, to whom thou hast prophesied lies.

cases.name: Pelatiah and the princes at the east gate
cases.charge: Devising mischief and giving wicked counsel in the city
cases.summary: In vision Ezekiel saw twenty-five men at the east gate of the temple, princes of the people, Jaazaniah and Pelatiah among them, who said, it is not near; let us build houses: this city is the caldron, and we be the flesh. He was told to prophesy against them.
cases.offense: Rulers who reassured the city against the prophets, treating Jerusalem as a safe pot for its own meat, while multiplying slain in its streets. The Lord: ye have not walked in my statutes, neither executed my judgments, but have done after the manners of the heathen.
cases.judgment: As Ezekiel prophesied, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died. The prophet fell on his face and cried out, wilt thou make a full end of the remnant of Israel?

cases.name: Pharaoh-hophra and Egypt
cases.charge: Saying, My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself; a staff of reed to the house of Israel
cases.summary: Judah leaned on Egypt against Babylon, and Egypt broke under the hand like a reed and ran into it. Ezekiel's word against Pharaoh is against the boast of ownership: the river was his, he had made it. Forty years of desolation were decreed, and Egypt was to be the basest of kingdoms afterward.
cases.offense: Behold, I am against thee, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon that lieth in the midst of his rivers, which hath said, My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself. Because they have been a staff of reed to the house of Israel: when they took hold of thee by thy hand, thou didst break, and rend all their shoulder; and when they leaned upon thee, thou brakest, and madest all their loins to be at a stand.
cases.judgment: I will give Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar. The land of Egypt shall be desolate and waste forty years; I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations. At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians, and they shall be there a base kingdom; it shall be the basest of the kingdoms; neither shall it exalt itself any more above the nations.

cases.name: Rehoboam
cases.charge: Forsaking the counsel of the old men; forsaking the law of the Lord
cases.summary: Solomon's son rejected the elders' advice to serve the people and took his young companions' line: my little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins. Ten tribes left him that day. Later, when the kingdom was established, he forsook the law of the Lord and all Israel with him.
cases.offense: Pride in the first instance, apostasy in the second. Chronicles: he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek the Lord. Sirach calls him the foolishness of the people, one that had no understanding.
cases.judgment: Shishak of Egypt came up with twelve hundred chariots and took the treasures of the house of the Lord and the shields of gold. When the princes humbled themselves the Lord granted some deliverance, that they might know the difference between serving him and serving the kingdoms of the countries.

cases.name: Sennacherib and Rabshakeh
cases.charge: Reproaching the living God; setting him among the gods of the nations that could not save
cases.summary: Rabshakeh stood by the conduit of the upper pool and told Jerusalem in the Jews' language that no god of any nation had ever delivered a land from the king of Assyria. Hezekiah spread the letter before the Lord. That night an angel slew a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib went home to be murdered by his sons in the house of his god.
cases.offense: Who are they among all the gods of the countries, that have delivered their country out of mine hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of mine hand? Sennacherib wrote letters to rail on the Lord God of Israel, and to speak against him, saying, As the gods of the nations of other lands have not delivered their people, so shall not the God of Hezekiah deliver his people out of mine hand. Tobit, a captive in Nineveh, buried the Israelites Sennacherib slew in his rage when he came back from Judea.
cases.judgment: Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice? even against the Holy One of Israel. I will put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest. The angel of the Lord went out and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand. Sennacherib returned with shame of face to Nineveh, and as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword.

cases.name: Shebna the treasurer
cases.charge: Hewing himself a sepulchre on high; a shame to his lord's house
cases.summary: Over the house of the king in Hezekiah's day, Shebna cut himself a tomb in the rock as if Jerusalem were his to be buried in on high. Isaiah was sent to him with a sentence: the Lord would toss him like a ball into a large country and give his office to Eliakim.
cases.offense: What hast thou here? and whom hast thou here, that thou hast hewed thee out a sepulchre here, as he that heweth him out a sepulchre on high, and that graveth an habitation for himself in a rock? A steward building for his own name out of the house he was set over.
cases.judgment: Behold, the Lord will carry thee away with a mighty captivity, and will surely cover thee. He will surely violently turn and toss thee like a ball into a large country: there shalt thou die, and there the chariots of thy glory shall be the shame of thy lord's house. And I will drive thee from thy station, and from thy state shall he pull thee down. The key of the house of David was laid on the shoulder of Eliakim the son of Hilkiah instead. By the time Rabshakeh came, Shebna was already only the scribe.

cases.name: Shemaiah the Nehelamite
cases.charge: Sending letters from Babylon to have Jeremiah put in prison and in the stocks; prophesying a lie
cases.summary: From the first captivity Shemaiah wrote to the priests in Jerusalem, naming Jeremiah a madman and asking why he had not been put in the stocks. Zephaniah the priest read the letter in Jeremiah's ears, and the answer came back to Babylon: Shemaiah would have no man to dwell among the people, and would not see the good the Lord would do.
cases.offense: He sent letters in his own name to all the people at Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah the priest: The Lord hath made thee priest, that ye should be officers in the house of the Lord, for every man that is mad, and maketh himself a prophet, that thou shouldest put him in prison and in the stocks. Now therefore why hast thou not reproved Jeremiah of Anathoth? He had prophesied to the captives that the captivity would be long, and taught them to trust in a lie.
cases.judgment: Because that Shemaiah hath prophesied unto you, and I sent him not, and he caused you to trust in a lie: therefore thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite, and his seed: he shall not have a man to dwell among this people; neither shall he behold the good that I will do for my people, because he hath taught rebellion against the Lord.

cases.name: The captivity of Israel (the northern kingdom)
cases.charge: Two centuries of the sins of Jeroboam; secret sins; idols, high places, and children through the fire
cases.summary: Second Kings 17 is the indictment of a nation: they feared other gods, walked in the statutes of the heathen and of the kings of Israel, built high places in every city, served idols the Lord had said they should not, made their sons and daughters pass through the fire, used divination and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil.
cases.offense: The Lord testified against Israel and against Judah by all the prophets and all the seers, and they hardened their necks like the necks of their fathers. Hosea's summary: swearing, lying, killing, stealing, adultery; my people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.
cases.judgment: The Lord was very angry with Israel and removed them out of his sight: Assyria carried them away and placed them in Halah and Habor and the cities of the Medes. Deuteronomy had said it: the Lord shall scatter thee among all people. There was none left but the tribe of Judah only.

cases.name: The captivity of Judah
cases.charge: Polluting the house of the Lord; mocking the messengers of God; refusing the Sabbath and the land's sabbaths
cases.summary: All the chief of the priests and the people transgressed very much after all the abominations of the heathen and polluted the house of the Lord. The Lord sent messengers because he had compassion; they mocked them, despised his words, and misused his prophets until there was no remedy.
cases.offense: Ezekiel's catalogue of Jerusalem: princes shedding blood, fathers and mothers set light by, strangers oppressed, sabbaths profaned, incest, bribes for blood, usury, priests who put no difference between holy and profane, prophets daubing with untempered mortar. Jeremiah adds the Sabbath gates: bear no burden on the sabbath day, and they would not hear.
cases.judgment: Nebuchadnezzar slew their young men in the sanctuary, burned the house of God, and carried the remnant to Babylon, to fulfil threescore and ten years until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths. Daniel and Baruch both confess it in the same words: the curse is poured upon us, as it is written in the law of Moses.

cases.name: The elders with idols in the temple (Ezekiel 8)
cases.charge: The image of jealousy; creeping things on the walls; women weeping for Tammuz; twenty-five men worshipping the sun with their backs to the temple
cases.summary: Carried in vision to Jerusalem, Ezekiel was shown four scenes of greater and greater abomination inside the house of the Lord: an idol at the gate, seventy elders with censers in a chamber of painted beasts, women mourning a pagan god, and men between the porch and the altar bowing east to the sun. The elders said, the Lord seeth us not.
cases.offense: Idolatry practiced by the leadership in the sanctuary itself, in secret, on the assumption that God had forsaken the earth. The land was also full of blood and the city of perverseness. Ezekiel 14 adds: these men have set up their idols in their heart.
cases.judgment: The glory departed by stages. Six men with slaughter weapons were told to begin at the sanctuary and slay utterly old and young, sparing only those marked who sighed and cried for the abominations. Mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity.

cases.name: The lord on whose hand the king leaned
cases.charge: Scoffing at the word of the Lord by Elisha in the famine of Samaria
cases.summary: In a siege so hard that women ate their children, Elisha said that by the next day fine flour would sell for a shekel in the gate. The king's officer answered that it could not happen if the Lord opened windows in heaven. He saw it, and was trampled in the gate by the crowd rushing to buy.
cases.offense: Elisha said, Hear ye the word of the Lord; Thus saith the Lord, To morrow about this time shall a measure of fine flour be sold for a shekel in the gate of Samaria. A lord on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God: Behold, if the Lord would make windows in heaven, might this thing be? The unbelief was spoken aloud, in the king's hearing, against a word that had just been named as the Lord's.
cases.judgment: Elisha answered, Behold, thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof. The Syrians fled in the night from a noise the Lord made them hear; the people went out and spoiled their tents; and the king appointed that same lord to have charge of the gate, and the people trode upon him in the gate, and he died, as the man of God had said.

cases.name: The man of God from Judah
cases.charge: Turning back to eat and drink at Bethel against the word of the Lord
cases.summary: Sent to cry against Jeroboam's altar, the prophet was charged to eat no bread, drink no water, and not return the way he came. An old prophet of Bethel lied to him, claiming an angel had said otherwise; he went back and ate. A lion met him on the road.
cases.offense: He had refused the king's table and reward; he accepted a colleague's word over God's own. Test the spirits: another prophet's claim did not cancel a command he had received himself. The old prophet's lie is recorded without excuse.
cases.judgment: The word of the Lord came through the very man who had deceived him: thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers. The lion killed him and stood by the body without eating it or the ass; the old prophet buried him in his own grave.

cases.name: The prince of Tyre
cases.charge: Saying, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God
cases.summary: Ezekiel's word to the ruler of the merchant city: because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art a man, and not God. Wiser than Daniel, richer by his traffick, and undone by both.
cases.offense: Self-deification on the strength of trade. By the multitude of thy merchandise they have filled the midst of thee with violence, and thou hast sinned. Tyre had also rejoiced at Jerusalem's fall: aha, she is broken, I shall be replenished.
cases.judgment: They shall bring thee down to the pit, and thou shalt die the deaths of them that are slain in the midst of the seas. Wilt thou yet say before him that slayeth thee, I am God? Nebuchadnezzar besieged the mainland city; Alexander finished the island.

cases.name: The prophets of Baal at Carmel
cases.charge: Prophesying in the name of other gods
cases.summary: Four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal cried from morning to noon and cut themselves with knives until the blood gushed out, and there was neither voice nor any to answer. Elijah's bullock, drenched three times, was consumed by fire from heaven with the water and the stones.
cases.offense: Deuteronomy 13 and 18 are the statutes: the prophet who speaks in the name of other gods shall die, and the one who says, let us go after other gods, shall be put to death. They had done it in front of all Israel for years at the queen's table.
cases.judgment: When the people fell on their faces and said, the Lord, he is the God, Elijah had the prophets taken down to the brook Kishon and slain there. Then the rain came.

cases.name: The shepherds of Israel
cases.charge: Feeding themselves and not the flock; scattering the sheep
cases.summary: Ezekiel 34 arraigns the rulers and pastors of Israel as shepherds who ate the fat and clothed themselves with the wool, but did not strengthen the diseased, heal the sick, bind up the broken, bring back the driven away, or seek the lost. The flock was scattered on every hill and became meat to the beasts.
cases.offense: With force and with cruelty have ye ruled them. Jeremiah brings the same charge: ye have scattered my flock and driven them away and not visited them. Zechariah's idol shepherd leaves the flock and is cursed in his arm and his eye.
cases.judgment: Behold, I am against the shepherds; I will require my flock at their hand and cause them to cease from feeding the flock. Then the Lord promises to search his sheep himself and set up one shepherd, his servant David. Christ claimed the office: I am the good shepherd.

cases.name: The young mockers of Bethel
cases.charge: Mocking the prophet of the Lord
cases.summary: As Elisha went up to Bethel, the seat of Jeroboam's calf, a company came out of the city mocking him: go up, thou bald head. He cursed them in the name of the Lord, and two she-bears came out of the wood and tore forty-two of them.
cases.offense: Contempt for the office, in the city that had made contempt for the Lord its religion. Go up mocks Elijah's ascent, which the sons of the prophets had just witnessed. The Hebrew word covers youths, not infants; forty-two of them were a crowd, not a prank.
cases.judgment: Leviticus warned that if Israel walked contrary to him, the Lord would send wild beasts among them which should rob them of their children. Forty-two were torn. Elisha went on to Carmel.

cases.name: Uzziah
cases.charge: Entering the temple to burn incense, which belonged to the priests
cases.summary: A strong and prosperous king who sought God in the days of Zechariah. When he was strong his heart was lifted up, and he went into the temple with a censer. Eighty priests withstood him; while he raged at them, leprosy rose in his forehead.
cases.offense: Usurping an office God had assigned to the sons of Aaron. The stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death was the statute; Korah had died for the same claim. Azariah said it plainly: it appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah.
cases.judgment: A leper to the day of his death, cut off from the house of the Lord, dwelling in a several house while his son judged the people. He was buried in a field near the kings' sepulchres, not among them, for they said, he is a leper.

cases.name: Zedekiah
cases.charge: Breaking his oath to Nebuchadnezzar; stiffening his neck against the Lord's word by Jeremiah
cases.summary: Sworn by God to serve Babylon, Zedekiah rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar and would not humble himself before Jeremiah speaking from the mouth of the Lord. Warned to the last that surrender would save the city and his life, he feared the Jews who had defected more than he feared the word.
cases.offense: Ezekiel names the oath-breaking as the Lord's own quarrel: seeing he despised the oath by breaking the covenant, when, lo, he had given his hand. Chronicles adds that he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart from turning unto the Lord God of Israel.
cases.judgment: Taken fleeing by night near Jericho, he watched his sons slain at Riblah, then had his eyes put out, and was carried in chains to Babylon, where he died in prison. The city and the temple burned behind him. Ezekiel's thou profane wicked prince of Israel, whose day is come.

cases.name: Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah, and the four hundred prophets
cases.charge: Prophesying victory at Ramoth-gilead by a lying spirit; smiting Micaiah on the cheek
cases.summary: Four hundred prophets told Ahab to go up and prosper. One, Micaiah, saw the Lord on his throne and a lying spirit sent into the mouths of the rest. Zedekiah struck him for it and asked which way the Spirit had gone. The battle answered for Ahab; scripture leaves Zedekiah hiding in an inner chamber.
cases.offense: Zedekiah made him horns of iron and said, Thus saith the Lord, With these shalt thou push the Syrians, until thou have consumed them; and all the prophets prophesied so. When Micaiah spoke the true word, Zedekiah went near and smote him on the cheek, and said, Which way went the Spirit of the Lord from me to speak unto thee?
cases.judgment: Micaiah answered, Behold, thou shalt see in that day, when thou shalt go into an inner chamber to hide thyself. Ahab was killed by a bow drawn at a venture, and the dogs licked his blood as the true prophet had said. What became of Zedekiah in the inner chamber is not written; the law's own sentence on a prophet whose word does not come to pass is.

cases.name: Zimri
cases.charge: Conspiring against his master Elah as he drank himself drunk; slaying all the house of Baasha
cases.summary: Captain of half the chariots, Zimri killed his king in a steward's house and took the throne. Seven days later the army chose Omri, Tirzah was taken, and Zimri burned the king's house over his own head. His name became a byword: Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?
cases.offense: Elah was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk, and Zimri went in and smote him. He slew all the house of Baasha, sparing not one, and reigned in his stead. Scripture records that he too walked in the way of Jeroboam, in his sin which he did, making Israel to sin.
cases.judgment: The people that were encamped heard, and made Omri king that same day, and besieged Tirzah. When Zimri saw that the city was taken, he went into the palace of the king's house, and burnt the king's house over him with fire, and died, for his sins which he sinned. Jezebel would throw his name at Jehu a generation later as the name of a traitor who did not last.

cases.name: Asa in his first years
cases.charge: Taking away the strange altars and the high places; commanding Judah to seek the Lord and do the law; crying to the Lord against a million Ethiopians
