cases.summary: Before the failure that is its own case, Asa did thirty-five years of what a king was for. He removed the idols, removed his own mother from being queen for her grove, made Judah swear to seek the Lord with all their heart, and when Zerah came against him with a million men he prayed one prayer and won.
cases.offense: Asa did that which was good and right in the eyes of the Lord his God: for he took away the altars of the strange gods, and the high places, and brake down the images, and cut down the groves: and commanded Judah to seek the Lord God of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment. Asa cried unto the Lord his God, and said, Lord, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Lord our God; for we rest on thee. And also concerning Maachah his mother, he removed her from being queen, because she had made an idol in a grove.
cases.judgment: So the Lord smote the Ethiopians before Asa, and before Judah; and the Ethiopians fled. The Lord is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you. They sware unto the Lord, and all Judah rejoiced at the oath: and the Lord was found of them, and gave them rest round about. And there was no more war unto the five and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa.

cases.name: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian
cases.charge: Going to the king for Jeremiah, and drawing him up out of the dungeon with old cast clouts and rotten rags
cases.summary: The princes had put Jeremiah in a dungeon of mire to die. A eunuch of the king's house, an Ethiopian, went out to Zedekiah at the gate and told him the prophet was likely to die of hunger where he was. The king gave him thirty men and he drew Jeremiah up with rags under his armholes. Before the city fell the Lord sent him his own word: thy life for a prey, because thou hast put thy trust in me.
cases.offense: Ebed-melech went forth out of the king's house, and spake to the king, saying, My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have cast into the dungeon; and he is like to die for hunger in the place where he is. So Ebed-melech took the men with him, and went into the house of the king under the treasury, and took thence old cast clouts and old rotten rags, and let them down by cords into the dungeon to Jeremiah. And they drew up Jeremiah with cords, and took him up out of the dungeon.
cases.judgment: Go and speak to Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, saying, Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring my words upon this city for evil, and not for good; and they shall be accomplished in that day before thee. But I will deliver thee in that day, saith the Lord: and thou shalt not be given into the hand of the men of whom thou art afraid. For I will surely deliver thee, and thou shalt not fall by the sword, but thy life shall be for a prey unto thee: because thou hast put thy trust in me, saith the Lord.

cases.name: Hezekiah
cases.charge: Trusting in the Lord God of Israel; cleaving to him and keeping his commandments; breaking the brasen serpent; keeping the passover; spreading Sennacherib's letter before the Lord
cases.summary: He opened the doors of the house of the Lord in the first month of his first year, kept a passover Jerusalem had not seen since Solomon, broke the brasen serpent of Moses because Israel burned incense to it, and prayed his way through Sennacherib and through a sentence of death. The one pride of his heart is its own case. This is the rest.
cases.offense: He trusted in the Lord God of Israel; so that after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor any that were before him. For he clave to the Lord, and departed not from following him, but kept his commandments, which the Lord commanded Moses. He brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it. And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart. Hezekiah received the letter, and went up into the house of the Lord, and spread it before the Lord.
cases.judgment: And the Lord was with him; and he prospered whithersoever he went forth. Then Isaiah sent to Hezekiah: that which thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard. I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake. Of his sickness: I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will add unto thy days fifteen years; and the shadow went back ten degrees. Thus the Lord saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and guided them on every side; and he was magnified in the sight of all nations from thenceforth.

cases.name: Jehoiada the priest
cases.charge: Hiding the king's son six years from Athaliah; making a covenant between the Lord, the king, and the people; doing good in Israel, both toward God and toward his house
cases.summary: When Athaliah killed the seed royal, Jehoiada's wife stole the baby Joash out of the slaughter and the priest hid him in the house of the Lord six years. In the seventh he armed the Levites, crowned the boy, had Athaliah taken out and slain, tore down the house of Baal, and set the temple in order. He was buried among the kings.
cases.offense: Jehoshabeath the daughter of the king took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king's sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber, and hid him from Athaliah. Jehoiada brought out the king's son, and put upon him the crown, and gave him the testimony, and made him king. And Jehoiada made a covenant between him, and between all the people, and between the king, that they should be the Lord's people. And all the people went to the house of Baal, and brake it down. And Jehoiada appointed the offices of the house of the Lord by the hand of the priests the Levites, whom David had distributed.
cases.judgment: And all the people of the land rejoiced: and the city was quiet, after that they had slain Athaliah with the sword. And Joash did that which was right in the sight of the Lord all the days of Jehoiada the priest. Jehoiada waxed old, and was full of days when he died; an hundred and thirty years old was he when he died. And they buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel, both toward God, and toward his house. What Joash did after Jehoiada died is his own case.

cases.name: Jehoshaphat
cases.charge: Seeking the Lord and walking in his commandments; sending Levites to teach the book of the law through all the cities of Judah; setting the battle in array with singers
cases.summary: He sent princes and Levites round Judah with the book of the law to teach it, and the fear of the Lord fell on the kingdoms round about. When Moab, Ammon and Edom came against him he proclaimed a fast, prayed in the congregation, and put the singers in front of the army. They came to the watchtower and found only dead bodies. His alliances with Ahab's house are their own case.
cases.offense: The Lord was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father David, and sought not unto Baalim; but sought to the Lord God of his father, and walked in his commandments. He sent to his princes, and with them the Levites, and they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people. Before the battle: O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee. He appointed singers unto the Lord, that should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army.
cases.judgment: Therefore the Lord stablished the kingdom in his hand; and all Judah brought to Jehoshaphat presents; and he had riches and honour in abundance. And the fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were round about Judah, so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat. Ye shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the Lord with you. When they began to sing and to praise, the Lord set ambushments, and they were smitten. They were three days in gathering of the spoil, it was so much. So the realm of Jehoshaphat was quiet: for his God gave him rest round about.

cases.name: Jonadab and the Rechabites
cases.charge: Obeying the commandment of Jonadab their father for over two hundred years: no wine, no house, no vineyard, no field
cases.summary: The Lord had Jeremiah set wine before a whole clan in a chamber of the temple. They refused it: their father Jonadab had commanded them to drink none, build no house and sow no seed, and they had kept it all their days. The Lord held them up against Judah, who would not obey him though he rose early and spoke, and promised Jonadab a man before him for ever.
cases.offense: But they said, We will drink no wine: for Jonadab the son of Rechab our father commanded us, saying, Ye shall drink no wine, neither ye, nor your sons for ever: neither shall ye build house, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyard, nor have any: but all your days ye shall dwell in tents. Thus have we obeyed the voice of Jonadab the son of Rechab our father in all that he hath charged us. The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, that he commanded his sons not to drink wine, are performed; for unto this day they drink none, but obey their father's commandment: notwithstanding I have spoken unto you, rising early and speaking; but ye hearkened not unto me.
cases.judgment: Because ye have obeyed the commandment of Jonadab your father, and kept all his precepts, and done according unto all that he hath commanded you: therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Jonadab the son of Rechab shall not want a man to stand before me for ever. The fifth commandment's promise, kept by a house for eight generations, and answered for ever.

cases.name: Josiah
cases.charge: A tender heart at the reading of the book; turning to the Lord with all his heart, soul, and might, according to all the law of Moses
cases.summary: Eight years old when crowned, sixteen when he began to seek the God of David, twenty when he began to purge Judah, twenty-six when the book of the law was found in the house and read to him. He rent his clothes, gathered the people, read it to them himself, and kept a passover like none since Samuel. He was promised he would be gathered to his grave in peace before the evil came. His death at Megiddo is its own case.
cases.offense: When the king had heard the words of the book of the law, he rent his clothes. He read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant, and the king stood by a pillar, and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk after the Lord, and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all their heart and all their soul. He put down the idolatrous priests; he brake down the houses of the sodomites; he defiled Topheth, that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech; he brake in pieces the images, and cut down the groves. Surely there was not holden such a passover from the days of the judges.
cases.judgment: Because thine heart was tender, and thou hast humbled thyself before the Lord, when thou heardest what I spake against this place, and hast rent thy clothes, and wept before me; I also have heard thee, saith the Lord. Behold therefore, I will gather thee unto thy fathers, and thou shalt be gathered into thy grave in peace; and thine eyes shall not see all the evil which I will bring upon this place. And like unto him was there no king before him, that turned to the Lord with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses; neither after him arose there any like him. Sirach: the remembrance of Josias is like the composition of the perfume that is made by the art of the apothecary.

cases.name: Jotham
cases.charge: Preparing his ways before the Lord his God; not entering the temple as his father had
cases.summary: Uzziah's son had watched his father go into the temple to burn incense and come out a leper. Jotham did what was right, and stayed out of the priests' place. The chronicler gives the cause of his strength in one line: he prepared his ways before the Lord his God.
cases.offense: He did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Uzziah did: howbeit he entered not into the temple of the Lord. He built the high gate of the house of the Lord, and on the wall of Ophel he built much. He fought with the king of the Ammonites and prevailed against them.
cases.judgment: So Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the Lord his God. The children of Ammon gave him an hundred talents of silver, and ten thousand measures of wheat, and ten thousand of barley, the same year, and the second year, and the third. Sixteen years, and no judgment written.

cases.name: Naaman the Syrian
cases.charge: Going down and dipping himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God, after his anger
cases.summary: Captain of the host of Syria, a mighty man of valour, and a leper. He came with horses and chariots and a letter from his king, and was sent to wash in Jordan by a messenger who did not come to the door. He went away in a rage, was talked round by his servants, obeyed, and came up with the flesh of a little child. He went home with two mules' burden of earth and a vow to sacrifice to no other god.
cases.offense: Naaman was wroth: Behold, I thought, He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the Lord his God. Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? His servants said, If the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldest thou not have done it? how much rather then, when he saith to thee, Wash, and be clean? Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God. He refused nothing afterward: thy servant will henceforth offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice unto other gods, but unto the Lord.
cases.judgment: His flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean. And he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him: and he said, Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel. Christ named him against Nazareth: many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian. The servant who ran after him for a gift is his own case.

cases.name: The prophet's widow, and the pot of oil
cases.charge: Borrowing not a few vessels, as the prophet said, and shutting the door
cases.summary: A widow of the sons of the prophets had a creditor coming to take her two sons for bondmen and one pot of oil in the house. Elisha told her to borrow empty vessels, not a few, shut the door, and pour. The oil stopped when the vessels did. She paid the debt and lived on the rest.
cases.offense: Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels; borrow not a few. And when thou art come in, thou shalt shut the door upon thee and upon thy sons, and shalt pour out into all those vessels. So she went from him, and shut the door upon her and upon her sons, who brought the vessels to her; and she poured out. The measure of the miracle was the measure of her borrowing.
cases.judgment: It came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said unto her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said unto her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed. Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, Go, sell the oil, and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest. The law against selling a brother into bondage for debt and the promise to the widow met in one pot of oil.

cases.name: The Shunammite woman
cases.charge: Constraining the man of God to eat bread; building him a little chamber on the wall, with a bed, a table, a stool, and a candlestick
cases.summary: A great woman of Shunem noticed that a holy man of God passed by continually and made him a room. She asked nothing. She was given a son; when he died on her knees she laid him on the prophet's bed, saddled the ass, and said, It is well. He was raised. Years later, back from a famine, she got her whole house and land restored by the king in one morning.
cases.offense: She said unto her husband, Behold now, I perceive that this is an holy man of God, which passeth by us continually. Let us make a little chamber, I pray thee, on the wall; and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick. Asked what could be done for her, she answered, I dwell among mine own people. When the child was dead she said to her husband and to Gehazi, It is well, and did not stop until she caught the prophet by the feet.
cases.judgment: About this season, according to the time of life, thou shalt embrace a son. And the woman conceived, and bare a son at that season. The child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes; and Elisha said, Take up thy son. Then she went in, and fell at his feet, and bowed herself to the ground, and took up her son. After seven years' famine she came to cry to the king for her house and land at the very moment Gehazi was telling him how Elisha had restored a dead body to life; and the king appointed an officer: Restore all that was hers, and all the fruits of the field since the day that she left the land, even until now.

cases.name: The widow of Zarephath
cases.charge: Making the prophet's cake first, out of the last handful of meal
cases.summary: A Gentile widow gathering two sticks to cook a last meal for herself and her son was asked by a stranger to feed him first from it, on a promise from the God of Israel. She did. The barrel of meal did not waste and the cruse of oil did not fail until the rain came, and when her son died the prophet raised him.
cases.offense: As the Lord thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die. Elijah said, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son. And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah. Christ named her against Nazareth: unto none of the widows of Israel was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta.
cases.judgment: For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the Lord sendeth rain upon the earth. And she, and he, and her house, did eat many days. When her son fell sick and there was no breath left in him, Elijah stretched himself upon the child three times and cried unto the Lord, and the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived. The woman said, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth.

cases.name: Belshazzar
cases.charge: Drinking from the temple vessels and praising the gods of gold and silver
cases.summary: At a feast for a thousand lords, Belshazzar called for the gold and silver vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the house of God in Jerusalem, drank wine from them with his wives and concubines, and praised the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone. Fingers of a man's hand wrote on the plaster.
cases.offense: Daniel's indictment: thou hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven, and the God in whose hand thy breath is, and whose are all thy ways, hast thou not glorified. He knew what had happened to his father and humbled not his heart.
cases.judgment: Mene, mene, tekel, upharsin: numbered, weighed and found wanting, divided. In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain, and Darius the Median took the kingdom.

cases.name: Bigthan and Teresh
cases.charge: Conspiring to lay hands on king Ahasuerus
cases.summary: Two chamberlains who kept the door were wroth and sought to lay hand on the king. Mordecai heard of it and told Esther, who told the king in Mordecai's name. They were hanged, and the thing was written in the chronicles, where a sleepless king found it years later on the night before Haman meant to hang Mordecai.
cases.offense: In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king's gate, two of the king's chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.
cases.judgment: The thing was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king thereof in Mordecai's name. And when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king. The record of their sentence became the instrument of Haman's.

cases.name: Daniel's accusers
cases.charge: Conspiring by law against an innocent man
cases.summary: Finding no fault in Daniel except concerning the law of his God, the presidents and princes flattered Darius into signing a decree that no one might petition any god or man for thirty days, then caught Daniel praying. The king labored till sunset to deliver him and could not.
cases.offense: A snare built from the machinery of law itself: a statute designed to make righteousness a crime, and a king manipulated into executing it. Deuteronomy's rule for a false witness is that what he thought to do to his brother be done to him.
cases.judgment: Daniel came out of the den without a mark because he believed in his God. The king commanded those who had accused him, with their children and wives, cast into the den; the lions broke all their bones before they reached the bottom.

cases.name: Eliashib and Tobiah the Ammonite
cases.charge: Lodging an Ammonite enemy in a chamber of the house of God; a priest's house allied to Sanballat
cases.summary: While Nehemiah was away, Eliashib the priest, allied to Tobiah by marriage, cleared out a storechamber of the temple that had held the tithe and the vessels and gave it to the Ammonite who had mocked and opposed the wall. Nehemiah returned and threw Tobiah's household stuff out.
cases.offense: Deuteronomy had barred the Ammonite from the congregation of the Lord for ever, and this one was an active enemy. The law also required the priests to keep the charge of the sanctuary and the Levites to be supplied from it; instead the tithe was displaced to house him. The high priest's grandson had married Sanballat's daughter.
cases.judgment: It grieved me sore: therefore I cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber, and commanded the chambers cleansed and the vessels and the tithe brought back. The son-in-law of Sanballat he chased from him. Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood.

cases.name: Haman the Agagite
cases.charge: Plotting the destruction of all the Jews; building a gallows for Mordecai
cases.summary: Because one Jew would not bow to him, Haman sought to destroy all the Jews in the empire, bought the decree with ten thousand talents, cast lots for the day, and built a gallows fifty cubits high for Mordecai. Esther exposed him at her second banquet.
cases.offense: Genocide from wounded pride, purchased by bribe on a false report to the king: their laws are diverse from all people, neither keep they the king's laws. The Agagite's name recalls Amalek, whose remembrance Israel was commanded to blot out.
cases.judgment: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai; his ten sons followed. Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein. The feast of Purim keeps the memory of the lot that turned.

cases.name: Judah robbing God in tithes and offerings
cases.charge: Withholding the tithe from the storehouse
cases.summary: Will a man rob God? Yet ye have robbed me. But ye say, wherein? In tithes and offerings. The returned community had left the Levites unsupported so that they fled to their fields, and the house of God was forsaken while every man ran to his own house.
cases.offense: The tenth of the land's increase belongs to the Lord; withholding it is theft from him. Haggai had already named the consequence: ye have sown much and bring in little, because of mine house that is waste. Nehemiah found the same neglect on his return and contended with the rulers over it.
cases.judgment: Ye are cursed with a curse: for ye have robbed me, even this whole nation. The remedy offered in the same breath: bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, and prove me now herewith, if I will not open you the windows of heaven.

cases.name: Nebuchadnezzar
cases.charge: Pride: is not this great Babylon, that I have built?
cases.summary: Warned by Daniel's interpretation of the tree dream to break off his sins by righteousness and his iniquities by showing mercy to the poor, the king walked on his palace roof twelve months later and took the credit for the empire. While the word was in his mouth a voice fell from heaven.
cases.offense: The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, says Sirach; Nebuchadnezzar's was the claim of the builder over the Builder. He had already burned three men for refusing his image and been told whose hand had given him the kingdom.
cases.judgment: Driven from men, he ate grass as oxen, his body wet with dew, his hair grown like eagles' feathers and his nails like birds' claws, until seven times passed and he lifted up his eyes to heaven. His reason returned; his kingdom was restored; and he wrote the confession himself: those that walk in pride he is able to abase.

cases.name: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin
cases.charge: Weakening the hands of the people; hiring counsellors against them to frustrate the building of the house of God
cases.summary: The people of the land offered to help build the temple and were refused, and turned to hindrance: hired counsellors, letters to Artaxerxes, and a stop-work order enforced by force and power. The work lay still until the second year of Darius, whose decree turned the tables: whoever altered it would be hanged on timber from his own house.
cases.offense: The people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building, and hired counsellors against them, to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius. Rehum and Shimshai wrote to Artaxerxes that Jerusalem was the rebellious and the bad city, and the king's answer was used to make them cease by force and power.
cases.judgment: Scripture records no sentence on the adversaries themselves. What it records is Darius's decree: let the work of this house of God alone; whosoever shall alter this word, let timber be pulled down from his house, and being set up, let him be hanged thereon; and let his house be made a dunghill for this. Tatnai and his companions did speedily as the king sent, and the elders of the Jews builded and prospered through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah.

cases.name: The nobles who exacted usury of their brethren
cases.charge: Lending on interest; taking brethren's lands and children for debt
cases.summary: During the rebuilding of the wall, the poor cried out that they had mortgaged their fields and vineyards and sold their sons and daughters into bondage to pay the king's tribute and the nobles' interest. Nehemiah was very angry and set a great assembly against the nobles and rulers.
cases.offense: Ye exact usury, every one of his brother. The law forbids taking usury from a poor brother or holding him as a bondservant; Nehemiah adds that they were buying back Jews sold to the heathen while their own class was selling them again.
cases.judgment: Restore, I pray you, to them, even this day, their lands, their vineyards, their oliveyards, and their houses, also the hundredth part of the money. They said, we will restore them, and swore before the priests. Nehemiah shook his lap: so God shake out every man that performeth not this promise.

cases.name: The priests who despised the Name
cases.charge: Offering polluted bread and blemished beasts; being partial in the law
cases.summary: After the return, the priests offered the blind, the lame, and the sick on the altar and said the table of the Lord was contemptible and its service a weariness. Offer it now unto thy governor, Malachi says; will he be pleased with thee? They also departed out of the way and caused many to stumble at the law.
cases.offense: Leviticus forbids any offering with a blemish; they kept the best for themselves and the defective for God, while men of other nations feared his name more than they did. Priests are to keep knowledge and teach the law; these corrupted the covenant of Levi.
cases.judgment: I will curse your blessings; yea, I have cursed them already. I will spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your solemn feasts. Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people, according as ye have been partial in the law.

cases.name: The returned exiles who married strange wives
cases.charge: Mingling the holy seed with the peoples of the lands
cases.summary: Ezra was told that the people, priests, and Levites had taken wives of the Canaanites, Hittites, Ammonites, Moabites, and Egyptians, and that the princes and rulers had been chief in the trespass. He rent his garment and sat astonished until the evening sacrifice. A generation later Nehemiah found children who could not speak the Jews' language.
cases.offense: Deuteronomy 7 was the statute: neither shalt thou make marriages with them, for they will turn away thy son from following me. Ezra's prayer cites it and names the reason it cut deeper after the exile: after all that is come upon us for our evil deeds, should we again break thy commandments? Nehemiah pointed at Solomon.
cases.judgment: The people confessed, and by covenant separated themselves from the strange wives and from such as were born of them, case by case before the elders and judges of every city, over three months. First Esdras preserves the same proceedings. Nehemiah contended with the later offenders, smote certain of them, and chased away the priest who had married Sanballat's daughter.

cases.name: The Sabbath traders of Jerusalem and Tyre
cases.charge: Treading winepresses, bringing in sheaves, and selling fish and wares on the Sabbath
cases.summary: Nehemiah saw men of Judah treading winepresses and loading asses on the Sabbath, and Tyrian merchants selling fish in Jerusalem on the holy day. He testified against the nobles, shut the gates at dusk, set his own servants to guard them, and threatened to lay hands on the merchants who camped outside.
cases.offense: Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city? Yet ye bring more wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath. Jeremiah had named Sabbath burdens through those very gates as a cause of the city's burning.
cases.judgment: The merchants lodged outside the wall once or twice; Nehemiah warned them, and from that time forth came they no more on the sabbath. He commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates. Remember me, O my God, concerning this also.

cases.name: Daniel
cases.charge: Purposing in his heart not to defile himself with the king's meat; praying three times a day with his windows open toward Jerusalem, decree or no decree
cases.summary: A captive boy in Babylon refused the king's meat and wine and asked for pulse and water; ten days later he looked better than the rest. Sixty years later, an old man under Darius, he kept his windows open and prayed as before, knowing the den was signed. He was in the den one night and the God he served shut the lions' mouths.
cases.offense: Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat, nor with the wine which he drank. When Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime. His enemies had already ruled out every other charge: we shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, except we find it against him concerning the law of his God.
cases.judgment: God had brought Daniel into favour and tender love with the prince of the eunuchs. At the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer and fatter in flesh than all the children which did eat the portion of the king's meat. God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams. My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me. So Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian. Ezekiel names him with Noah and Job; Gabriel calls him greatly beloved.

cases.name: Ezra
cases.charge: Preparing his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments
cases.summary: A ready scribe in the law of Moses came up from Babylon with the king's letter and the king's silver, refused a guard because he had told the king the hand of God is on all that seek him, fasted at the river Ahava, and arrived. He read the law to the people from morning to midday, and they wept, and kept the feast of tabernacles as it had not been kept since Joshua.
cases.offense: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments. I was ashamed to require of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help us against the enemy in the way: because we had spoken unto the king, saying, The hand of our God is upon all them for good that seek him. So we fasted and besought our God for this: and he was intreated of us. He read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.
cases.judgment: And the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of the Lord his God upon him. Blessed be the Lord God of our fathers, which hath put such a thing as this in the king's heart, to beautify the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem. The hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy, and of such as lay in wait by the way. And all the people went their way to eat, and to drink, and to send portions, and to make great mirth, because they had understood the words that were declared unto them. Since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Israel done so. And there was very great gladness.

cases.name: Mordecai and Esther
cases.charge: Mordecai: bowing not to Haman. Esther: going in to the king against the law, after three days' fast: if I perish, I perish
cases.summary: A Jew in the king's gate would not bow to an Agagite, and the Agagite bought a decree to kill every Jew in the empire. His cousin the queen fasted three days with all the Jews of Shushan and went in to the king uncalled. Haman was hanged on his own gallows, the Jews were given the day, and Mordecai was next unto the king. The feast of Purim keeps it.
cases.offense: All the king's servants bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence; for he had told them that he was a Jew. Esther: Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish. Mordecai's word to her: who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
cases.judgment: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king's wrath pacified. The king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it unto Mordecai. The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour. Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed. The Greek Esther adds Mordecai's dream and the Lord's answer: the Lord hath done wonders for his people.

cases.name: Nehemiah
cases.charge: Building the wall in fifty-two days with a sword in one hand; taking no governor's bread; forbidding usury; shutting the gates on the Sabbath; remember me, O my God, for good
cases.summary: A cupbearer wept for the walls of Jerusalem, prayed four months, asked the king, and came. He built the wall against Sanballat with half the people holding spears, made the nobles give back the usury they had taken from their brethren, refused the governor's allowance for twelve years, threw Tobiah's furniture out of the temple, chased Sanballat's son-in-law out of the priesthood, and shut the gates on the Sabbath. Four times his prayer is the same: remember me, O my God, for good.
cases.offense: The former governors that had been before me were chargeable unto the people; but so did not I, because of the fear of God. I rebuked the nobles: ye exact usury, every one of his brother. Restore, I pray you, to them, even this day, their lands, their vineyards, their oliveyards, and their houses, also the hundredth part of the money. And they said, We will restore them. I commanded that the gates should be shut, and charged that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and some of my servants set I at the gates, that there should no burden be brought in on the sabbath day. Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God.
cases.judgment: And the king granted me, according to the good hand of my God upon me. So the wall was finished in the twenty and fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty and two days. And it came to pass, that when all our enemies heard thereof, and all the heathen that were about us saw these things, they were much cast down in their own eyes: for they perceived that this work was wrought of our God. Think upon me, my God, for good, according to all that I have done for this people. Sirach: among the elect was Neemias, whose renown is great, who raised up for us the walls that were fallen, and set up the gates and the bars, and raised up our ruins again.

cases.name: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego
cases.charge: Refusing to fall down and worship the golden image; not careful to answer the king in this matter
cases.summary: Every people, nation and language fell down at the sound of the music. Three officers of the province of Babylon stood. Told they would go into the furnace and asked who was the God that should deliver them out of the king's hands, they answered that their God was able, and that if he did not, they would still not serve Nebuchadnezzar's gods. The furnace killed the men who threw them in and did not singe their hair.
cases.offense: Be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up. If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods. In the Song of the Three Children, Azarias prayed in the midst of the fire: we have sinned and committed iniquity; yet deliver us not up wholly, for thy name's sake.
cases.judgment: Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of God. Upon whose bodies the fire had no power, nor was an hair of their head singed, neither were their coats changed, nor the smell of fire had passed on them. Nebuchadnezzar spake: Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who hath sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king's word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own God. Then the king promoted them in the province of Babylon. The men that took them up were slain by the flame of the fire.

cases.name: Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest
cases.charge: Obeying the voice of the Lord by Haggai; rising up and working on the house of the Lord
cases.summary: Sixteen years the temple foundation lay bare while the people built themselves ceiled houses and said the time was not come. Haggai spoke, and the governor and the high priest with the remnant of the people obeyed and came and worked, twenty-four days after the word. The Lord said, I am with you, and by Zechariah, not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit.
cases.offense: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the Lord their God had sent him, and the people did fear before the Lord. And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, and the spirit of Joshua, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the Lord of hosts, their God. Zechariah: Joshua stood before the angel clothed with filthy garments, and Satan at his right hand to resist him; and the Lord rebuked Satan and clothed him with change of raiment.
cases.judgment: Then spake Haggai the Lord's messenger in the Lord's message unto the people, saying, I am with you, saith the Lord. From this day will I bless you. In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee. The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it. And the elders of the Jews builded, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah, and finished it in the sixth year of Darius. Sirach names them together: Zorobabel, as a signet on the right hand; Jesus the son of Josedec, who set up the holy temple to the Lord.

cases.name: Alcimus
cases.charge: Slandering Judas to the king; slaying sixty Asideans under a sworn peace; pulling down the wall of the inner court
cases.summary: Alcimus, who had defiled himself wilfully in the times of the mingling with the Gentiles, sought the high priesthood from Demetrius by accusing Judas Maccabeus of sedition. Sent with an army, he swore peace to the Asideans and killed sixty of them in one day. Later he commanded the wall of the inner court of the sanctuary pulled down, the work of the prophets.
cases.offense: Perjury, judicial murder, and sacrilege by a priest. The people remembered the psalm over the dead: the flesh of thy saints have they cast out, and their blood have they shed round about Jerusalem, and there was none to bury them.
cases.judgment: As he began to pull down the wall, Alcimus was plagued; his mouth was stopped, he was taken with a palsy, and could no more speak or set his house in order. So Alcimus died at that time with great torment.

cases.name: Aman, who ensnared Achiacharus
cases.charge: Treachery against the man who brought him up
cases.summary: Tobit's dying counsel to his son holds up one case: remember how Aman handled Achiacharus that brought him up, how out of light he brought him into darkness, and how he rewarded him again. Achiacharus, the king's cupbearer and Tobit's kinsman, had once interceded for Tobit himself.
cases.offense: Ingratitude become betrayal, against a benefactor who stood as a father. The story assumed by the text is the tale of Ahikar: the adopted nephew who forged evidence to have his uncle executed.
cases.judgment: Achiacharus was saved, but the other had his reward: for he went down into darkness. Aman fell into the snare and perished. Tobit's moral: consider what alms doeth, and how righteousness doth deliver.

cases.name: Andronicus
cases.charge: Murder of Onias the high priest under a sworn assurance
cases.summary: Onias, having exposed Menelaus' theft of the temple vessels, took sanctuary at Daphne. Menelaus persuaded the king's deputy Andronicus to lure him out; he came to Onias in deceit, gave him his right hand with oaths, and though suspected, persuaded him to leave the sanctuary, and shut him up immediately without regard of justice.
cases.offense: A murder achieved by a false oath and the violation of asylum. Even the Greeks, the text says, were grieved for the unjust death of a man who had lived soberly and in virtue.
cases.judgment: When Antiochus heard of it he was sorry in his mind, and sent for Andronicus, stripped him of his purple, rent his clothes, led him through the city, and slew him in the same place where he had committed impiety against Onias. Thus the Lord rewarded him his punishment, as he had deserved.

cases.name: Antiochus Epiphanes
cases.charge: Defiling the temple; forbidding the law; murdering the faithful
cases.summary: The Seleucid king outlawed the law of Moses, defiled the temple with an idol, and put to death those who kept the covenant. The books of Maccabees record both his persecution and his end.
cases.offense: He forbade circumcision and the sabbaths, set up the abomination on the altar, forced sacrifice to idols, and killed mothers who circumcised their sons and families who kept the law in secret.
cases.judgment: Struck with an incurable disease of the bowels, worms rising from the living body, he died in a strange land in bitter grief, by the account, confessing at the last that it was right to be subject to God.

cases.name: Apollonius
cases.charge: Falling upon Jerusalem on the Sabbath under a pretence of peace; slaying a great multitude; taking women and children captive
cases.summary: Sent by Antiochus with twenty-two thousand men, Apollonius spoke peaceable words to Jerusalem, waited for the Sabbath when the people would not fight, and slew them going out to see the show. Judas Maccabeus met him in the field, killed him, and carried his sword for the rest of his life.
cases.offense: He came to Jerusalem, and speaking peaceable words unto them, but all was deceit: for when they had given him credence, he fell suddenly upon the city, and smote it very sore, and destroyed much people of Israel. He took the spoils of the city, set it on fire, and pulled down the houses and walls round about. He commanded his men to arm themselves, and to slay all those that went out to see the holy Sabbath, and there were slain great multitudes.
cases.judgment: Judas gathered those that were willing, and Apollonius gathered the Gentiles together, and a great host out of Samaria, to fight against Israel. Judas perceived it, and went forth to meet him, and so he smote him, and slew him: many also fell down slain, but the rest fled. Wherefore Judas took their spoils, and Apollonius' sword also, and therewith he fought all his life long.

cases.name: Heliodorus
cases.charge: Attempting to plunder the temple treasury
cases.summary: Sent by King Seleucus on the information of Simon the temple governor, Heliodorus came to seize the money laid up in the treasury, though the high priest Onias told him it was the relief of widows and fatherless children and deposits held in trust. The whole city lay in sackcloth. He went in anyway.
cases.offense: Sacrilege against the place, and theft from the poor the place protected. The law that forbids afflicting widows and the fatherless, and the law that makes God's house holy, were both in front of him. He proceeded as he had resolved.
cases.judgment: A horse with a terrible rider in golden armor struck him with its forefeet, and two young men scourged him without ceasing; he fell to the ground in darkness and was carried out on a litter. Onias offered sacrifice for his life, and he lived. He returned to the king and testified: if thou hast any enemy or traitor, send him thither, and thou shalt receive him well scourged.

cases.name: Holofernes
cases.charge: Making Nebuchadnezzar a god; blasphemy against the God of Israel; lust and drunkenness
cases.summary: Nebuchadnezzar's captain, sent to make all the earth worship the king alone as god, cut down the groves and gods of every nation and besieged Bethulia. Who is God but Nebuchadnezzar, he asked, and told Achior that the God of Israel would not save his people. Judith came to his camp.
cases.offense: Idolatry enforced by the sword, and contempt for the Lord spoken to his face through Achior. On the fourth night his heart was ravished with Judith and he was filled with wine, more than he had drunk at any time in one day since he was born.
cases.judgment: Judith took his own fauchion, smote twice upon his neck with all her might, and took away his head; his army, finding him headless in his tent, fled and was cut down. Judith's song: the Lord Almighty hath disappointed them by the hand of a woman.

cases.name: Jason the high priest
cases.charge: Buying the priesthood; setting up a Greek gymnasium; drawing his countrymen to heathen customs
cases.summary: Onias' brother Jason obtained the high priesthood from Antiochus for three hundred and sixty talents and a promise of more, then built a place of exercise under the tower itself, brought the young men under the Greek hat, and had the priests neglect the sacrifices to hasten to the games. He sent silver for the sacrifice of Hercules.
cases.offense: The narrator's summary: such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest. A bought office, a foreign religion imported into the sanctuary's shadow, and the law despised for the sake of the games. Then Menelaus outbid him.
cases.judgment: Driven out, he attacked Jerusalem with a thousand men, slew his own citizens without mercy, and was driven out again. He fled from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws; he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, and perished in a strange land.

cases.name: Judas' soldiers with idol tokens under their coats
cases.charge: Carrying things consecrated to idols into battle
cases.summary: After the battle near Adullam, Judas and his company came to bury their dead and found under the coat of every slain man things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which is forbidden the Jews by the law. Then every man saw that this was the cause wherefore they were slain.
cases.offense: Deuteronomy: thou shalt not bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it. Joshua's men had died at Ai for Achan's hidden spoil; these had died in a battle they otherwise won.
cases.judgment: The survivors praised the Lord, the righteous Judge, who had opened the things that were hid, and prayed that the sin might be wholly put out of remembrance. Judas took a collection and sent it to Jerusalem for a sin offering for the dead.

cases.name: Lysimachus
cases.charge: Sacrilege: robbing the temple with Menelaus' consent
cases.summary: Menelaus' brother committed many sacrileges in the city by his brother's consent and carried away much gold. The multitude gathered against him; he armed three thousand men under a captain of years and madness and attacked the crowd.
cases.offense: Plunder of the sanctuary treated as family business, then armed force against the people who objected. The narrator calls him the church-robber.
cases.judgment: The people took up stones and clubs and ashes, wounded many, killed some, put the rest to flight, and slew Lysimachus himself beside the treasury. Judgment executed by the congregation at the scene of the crime.

cases.name: Menelaus
cases.charge: Buying the priesthood over Jason; stealing the temple vessels; procuring the murder of Onias; bribing his way past the king's judgment
cases.summary: Sent by Jason to carry the king's money, Menelaus outbid him by three hundred talents and came back high priest, though he was not of Aaron's line by the account. He stole gold vessels from the temple to pay his debt, had the righteous Onias murdered for exposing him, and bought off the king when the Jews accused him.
cases.offense: Second Maccabees lists him as the cause of all the mischief: a great traitor to the laws and to his own country, bringing nothing worthy the high priesthood, but having the fury of a cruel tyrant and the rage of a savage beast. The bribe that acquitted him sent his three accusers to death instead.
cases.judgment: At last the King of kings moved Antiochus Eupator against him. In Beroea he was thrust into a tower of ashes fifty cubits high, the death for sacrilege, not having so much as burial in the earth: for inasmuch as he had committed many sins about the altar, whose fire and ashes were holy, he received his death in ashes.

cases.name: Nicanor
cases.charge: Blasphemy against the temple; breaking covenant with Judas; resolving to attack on the Sabbath
cases.summary: Demetrius' general, having sworn friendship to Judas and broken it at Alcimus' instigation, stretched out his hand toward the temple and swore that if Judas were not delivered to him he would burn the house and build a temple to Bacchus. He resolved to attack on the Sabbath; asked if there were a Mighty one in heaven who commanded the day, he answered that he was mighty on earth.
cases.offense: Contempt for the sanctuary, for the Sabbath, and for the God of both, spoken aloud as policy. The priests prayed at the altar for vengeance on the blasphemer; Judas' army prayed the prayer of Hezekiah against Sennacherib.
cases.judgment: Nicanor fell first in the battle at Adasa, and his army fled. They cut off his head and the right hand which he stretched out so proudly, cut out the tongue of the blasphemer, hung the head from the tower over against the temple, and ordained the day a yearly feast, the day before Mordecai's day.

cases.name: Ptolemy the son of Abubus
cases.charge: Murdering Simon the high priest and two of his sons at a banquet in his own castle
cases.summary: Simon's son in law, captain of the plain of Jericho, wanted the country and the crown. He received Simon and his sons Mattathias and Judas in the castle of Docus, made them a great banquet, and killed them when they had drunk well. He sent men to kill John Hircanus too; John was told first and killed the messengers.
cases.offense: Ptolemeus the son of Abubus, being made captain in the plain of Jericho, had abundance of silver and gold, for he was the high priest's son in law. Wherefore his heart being lifted up, he thought to get the country to himself, and thereupon consulted deceitfully against Simon and his sons to destroy them. When Simon and his sons had drunk largely, Ptolemee and his men rose up, and took their weapons, and came upon Simon into the banqueting place, and slew him and his two sons.
cases.judgment: In which doing he committed a great treachery, and recompensed evil for good. He wrote to the king to send him an host and deliver him the country, and sent others to take Jerusalem. One ran before to Gazara and told John that his father and brethren were slain, and he laid hands on them that came to destroy him, and slew them. The first book of the Maccabees ends there; the murderer's sentence is not in it. Deuteronomy's is.

cases.name: Simon the governor of the temple
cases.charge: Betraying the temple treasury to the king out of a private quarrel; slandering Onias the high priest
cases.summary: Falling out with Onias over the market of the city, Simon of the tribe of Benjamin told the governor of Coelosyria that the treasury at Jerusalem was full of infinite sums and could be brought under the king's power. That report sent Heliodorus. When it failed, Simon slandered Onias as the author of the mischief and had a man of his party commit murders.
cases.offense: Simon of the tribe of Benjamin, who was made governor of the temple, fell out with the high priest about disorder in the city. When he could not overcome Onias, he went to Apollonius the son of Thraseas and told him that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money. Afterward he slandered Onias, as if he had terrified Heliodorus and been the worker of these evils, and so proceeded in his malice that murders were committed by one Apollonius, a furious man.
cases.judgment: Onias went to the king, not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all. Scripture does not record Simon's end; it records that his brother Menelaus bought the priesthood with the same appetite, and how that ended. The law's word on the man who takes a bribe against the innocent, and on the false accuser, stands over him unrecorded.

cases.name: The Hellenizers who forsook the holy covenant
cases.charge: Covenanting with the heathen; removing circumcision; profaning the Sabbath; sacrificing to idols
cases.summary: In the days of Antiochus, wicked men went out of Israel persuading many to make a covenant with the heathen round about. They built a place of exercise at Jerusalem, made themselves uncircumcised, forsook the holy covenant, and were sold to do mischief. When the king's decree came, many Israelites consented to his religion.
cases.offense: First Maccabees calls them sinners and wicked men; Second Maccabees traces the profaneness to Jason. Every mark of the covenant was surrendered by choice: circumcision, Sabbath, sacrifice, food, and the company of the nations.
cases.judgment: Mattathias and his friends smote sinful men in their anger and wicked men in their wrath; the rest fled to the heathen for succour. Judas burnt up those that vexed his people, and the wicked shrunk for fear of him. After Antiochus, the ungodly out of Israel who sought Alcimus' priesthood found Judas had taken vengeance on their sort.

cases.name: The Jew who sacrificed at Modin
cases.charge: Sacrificing on the heathen altar at the king's command
cases.summary: The king's officers came to Modin to compel sacrifice and offered Mattathias silver, gold, and the title of king's friend to go first. He refused for himself and his sons. A Jew stepped forward in the sight of all to sacrifice on the altar according to the king's commandment.
cases.offense: Deuteronomy 13 and 17: the man who serves other gods, or entices to it, in Israel shall be put to death, and the hand of the witnesses first upon him. He did it publicly, for reward, to lead the rest.
cases.judgment: Mattathias was inflamed with zeal, ran upon him, and slew him at the altar, and the king's commissioner with him, and pulled down the altar. Thus dealt he zealously for the law of God, like as Phinees did unto Zambri. The revolt began there.

cases.name: The priests of Bel
cases.charge: Deceiving the king and the people with an idol that seemed to eat
cases.summary: The Babylonians spent twelve measures of fine flour, forty sheep, and six vessels of wine daily on Bel, and the king asked Daniel why he would not worship a living god who ate so much. Daniel laughed. Ashes strewn on the temple floor showed the footprints of the seventy priests, their wives and children, who came in by a secret door under the table every night.
cases.offense: Priests feeding themselves on offerings made to a lump of clay and brass, and threatening Daniel with death to protect the trade. The Epistle of Jeremiah describes the same racket: as for the things sacrificed unto them, their priests sell and abuse.
cases.judgment: Therefore the king slew them, and delivered Bel into Daniel's power, who destroyed him and his temple. When Daniel then destroyed the dragon, the Babylonians forced the king to throw him to the lions; he came out unharmed, and those that were the cause of his destruction were cast into the den and devoured in a moment.

cases.name: The two elders who accused Susanna
cases.charge: Attempted adultery by extortion; false witness against an innocent woman
cases.summary: Two elders of Babylon's Jews, appointed judges, hid in Joacim's garden, tried to force his wife Susanna, and when she cried out, accused her of adultery with a young man. The assembly believed them, as elders and judges, and condemned her to death. Daniel stopped the execution and examined them apart.
cases.offense: Lust turned to extortion and then to perjury: they perverted their own hearts and turned away their eyes that they might not look unto heaven nor remember just judgments. Examined separately, one said the pair were under a mastick tree and the other under a holm tree. Their own mouths convicted them of false witness.
cases.judgment: According to the law of Moses they did unto them in such sort as they maliciously intended to do to their neighbour: and they put them to death. Thus the innocent blood was saved the same day. Deuteronomy 19 is the statute; this is its clearest case.

cases.name: Timotheus
cases.charge: Gathering the heathen to root out the Jews; a second campaign after being once spared
cases.summary: Timotheus raised the Ammonites and Arabians against the returned Jews, was beaten at the river and shut up in Gazara, and was let go alive when he pleaded his hostages. He came again with a hundred and twenty thousand, and Judas's men found him hid in a pit and slew him.
cases.offense: Timotheus, whom the Jews had overcome before, when he had gathered a great multitude of foreign forces, and horses out of Asia not a few, came as though he would take Jewry by force of arms. He had boasted over the Jews and blasphemed, and the Jews would not spare his men who had provoked them.
cases.judgment: Judas and his company, calling upon the Lord, came to the Jews' ease: Timotheus and his host were overthrown at Raphon and thirty thousand slain. Timotheus fell into the hands of Dositheus and Sosipater, whom he besought with much craft to let him go with his life, and they let him go for the saving of their brethren. At last, in the second campaign, he fled to Gazara, and Judas's men, finding Timotheus hid in a certain pit, killed him and his brother Chereas, and Apollophanes.

cases.name: Tryphon
cases.charge: Taking Jonathan the high priest by treachery under a covenant of friendship; slaying him and the young king Antiochus
cases.summary: Tryphon set up a boy king to reach the crown himself, feared Jonathan would not suffer it, and took him at Ptolemais with fair words and a thousand men, killing the rest. He took Jonathan's sons as hostages, took a hundred talents for his release, kept both, and killed Jonathan on the way home. Then he killed the boy.
cases.offense: Tryphon went forth to deceive Jonathan: he said, Why hast thou brought all this people to so much trouble? Send them home, and choose a few men to wait on thee, and come thou with me to Ptolemais. When Jonathan entered, they of Ptolemais shut the gates and took him, and all them that came with him they slew with the sword. Afterward he sought to slay Simon's men as well, and having deceived Simon of the hundred talents and the children, went and slew Jonathan at Bascama.
cases.judgment: Tryphon dealt deceitfully with the young king Antiochus and slew him, and reigned in his stead, and brought a great calamity upon the land. Scripture records his crown, not his sentence: Antiochus the son of Demetrius came against him, the men of war forsook him, he fled by ship to Orthosias, and the book leaves him running. The law's sentence on the murderer and on the man who breaks a covenant of peace is written elsewhere and does not run out.

cases.name: Eleazar the scribe
cases.charge: Choosing to die gloriously rather than eat swine's flesh, or pretend to, at ninety years old
cases.summary: One of the principal scribes, an aged man and of a well favoured countenance, was compelled to open his mouth and eat swine's flesh. He spat it out. Old friends offered to let him bring his own meat and only pretend. He refused, so that the young would not be deceived by Eleazar, being fourscore years old and ten, into thinking he had gone over to a strange religion. He went to the torment and died leaving his death for an example.
cases.offense: But he choosing rather to die gloriously, than to live stained with such an abomination, spit it forth, and came of his own accord to the torment. Being fourscore years old and ten: it becometh not our age in any wise to dissemble, whereby many young persons might think that Eleazar was now gone to a strange religion. For though for the present time I should be delivered from the punishment of men: yet should I not escape the hand of the Almighty, neither alive, nor dead. Wherefore now, manfully changing this life, I will shew myself such an one as mine age requireth, and leave a notable example to such as be young to die willingly and courageously for the honourable and holy laws.
cases.judgment: And thus this man died, leaving his death for an example of a noble courage, and a memorial of virtue, not only unto young men, but unto all his nation. When he was ready to die with stripes, he groaned, and said, It is manifest unto the Lord, that hath the holy knowledge, that whereas I might have been delivered from death, I now endure sore pains in body by being beaten: but in soul am well content to suffer these things, because I fear him. The blessing recorded is the memorial: his name and his refusal, kept by his nation for ever, and the resurrection the next chapter's martyrs claim aloud.

cases.name: Judas Maccabeus
cases.charge: Going to battle with prayer and the law, keeping the ordinances of war, and cleansing the sanctuary
cases.summary: Mattathias' third son gathered those that kept the law, sent home the fearful and the newly married as Deuteronomy commands, prayed before every battle, and beat Apollonius, Seron, Gorgias, Lysias and Nicanor with a fraction of their numbers. He cleansed the sanctuary on the twenty-fifth of Chislev, three years to the day from its defiling, and ordained the eight days of Dedication. His prayer for the dead after Adullam is the plainest hope of resurrection in the Old Testament.
cases.offense: It is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with the God of heaven it is all one, to deliver with a great multitude, or a small company: for the victory of battle standeth not in the multitude of an host; but strength cometh from heaven. He commanded, according to the law, those who were building houses, or had betrothed wives, or were planting vineyards, or were fearful, to return home. He gave the army the watchword, The help of God. And Judas and his brethren said, Behold, our enemies are discomfited: let us go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary. He made a reconciliation for the dead, that they might be delivered from sin.
cases.judgment: So Judas fell upon them, and they fled; and the fame of him was spread abroad even to the utmost part of the earth. They built the sanctuary anew and offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of burnt offerings; and there was very great gladness among the people, for that the reproach of the heathen was put away. Judas and his brethren with the whole congregation of Israel ordained, that the days of the dedication of the altar should be kept in their season from year to year by the space of eight days. Onias and Jeremiah appeared to him in a dream, and Jeremiah gave him a sword of gold: take this holy sword, a gift from God, with the which thou shalt wound the adversaries.

cases.name: Judith
cases.charge: A widow who feared God greatly, fasting all the days of her widowhood; going out to Holofernes in the name of the Lord
cases.summary: When Bethulia's elders promised to surrender in five days if God did not help, a widow who had fasted since her husband died told them they were tempting the Lord. She prayed, put off her sackcloth, went out to the Assyrian camp with her maid, ate only her own clean food, and came back with the head of Holofernes in a bag. Israel praised her, she gave the spoil to the temple, and no one made the Israelites afraid in her days.
cases.offense: She was a widow three years and four months; she fasted all the days of her widowhood, save the eves of the sabbaths and the sabbaths, and the eves of the new moons and the new moons. She feared God greatly, and there was none that gave her an ill word. To the elders: who are ye, that have tempted God this day, and stand instead of God among the children of men? In the camp she would not eat the meat of Holofernes, but ate of her own that she had prepared, and went out every night to the valley to pray. Then she took his sword, and she smote twice upon his neck with all her might, and she took away his head from him.
cases.judgment: Blessed art thou of the most high God above all the women upon the earth: and blessed be the Lord God, which hath created the heavens and the earth, which hath directed thee to the cutting off of the head of the chief of our enemies. Thou art the exaltation of Jerusalem, thou art the great glory of Israel, thou art the great rejoicing of our nation. Judith dedicated all the stuff of Holofernes unto the Lord. And there was none that made the children of Israel any more afraid in the days of Judith, nor a long time after her death.

cases.name: Mattathias
cases.charge: Zealous for the law: refusing the king's commandment at Modin, and executing the apostate on the altar as Phinehas did Zambri
cases.summary: The king's officers came to Modin to make the people sacrifice, and offered Mattathias the priest wealth and the king's friendship to go first. He answered that though every nation obeyed, he and his sons would walk in the covenant of their fathers. When a Jew came forward to sacrifice, Mattathias killed him on the altar, killed the king's commissioner, pulled the altar down, and fled to the mountains with his sons. The Maccabean deliverance began there.
cases.offense: Though all the nations that are under the king's dominion obey him, and fall away every one from the religion of their fathers, and give consent to his commandments: yet will I and my sons and my brethren walk in the covenant of our fathers. God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances. We will not hearken to the king's words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand, or the left. He ran and slew the Jew upon the altar, and killed the king's commissioner, and the altar he pulled down. Thus dealt he zealously for the law of God, like as Phinees did unto Zambri the son of Salom. And Mattathias cried throughout the city with a loud voice, saying, Whosoever is zealous of the law, and maintaineth the covenant, let him follow me.
cases.judgment: His deathbed roll of the fathers is the blessing he claimed: Phinees our father in being zealous and fervent obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. Daniel for his innocency was delivered from the mouth of lions. And thus consider ye, throughout all ages, that none that put their trust in him shall be overcome. He blessed his sons and was gathered to his fathers, and all Israel made great lamentation for him. Judas and Simon after him took the city and the temple back, and the feast of the dedication is kept to this day.

cases.name: Onias the high priest
cases.charge: Godliness and hatred of wickedness, so that the laws were kept very well and the city lived in peace
cases.summary: While Onias was high priest the holy city was inhabited with all peace and the laws kept very well, and even the kings of the nations sent gifts to the temple. When Heliodorus came to rob the treasury, Onias' prayer and the priests' brought the horse and the two young men that scourged him, and Onias' sacrifice restored him. He was murdered afterward under a sworn peace; Judas saw him after death, praying for the people.
cases.offense: Because of the godliness of Onias the high priest, and his hatred of wickedness, the holy city was inhabited with all peace, and the laws were kept very well. When Simon slandered him, he went to the king, not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both publick and private; for he saw that it was impossible that the state should continue quiet, without the king's providence. When the king's messenger was struck down in the treasury, the high priest, fearing lest the king should misconceive that some treachery had been done to Heliodorus by the Jews, offered a sacrifice for the health of the man.
cases.judgment: Then the high priest offered sacrifice for the health of the man; and the Lord restored Heliodorus to life. Heliodorus testified to all men the works of the great God, which he had seen with his eyes. After his murder, Judas saw in a dream Onias, who had been high priest, a virtuous and a good man, reverend in conversation, gentle in condition, well spoken also, and exercised from a child in all points of virtue, holding up his hands and praying for the whole body of the Jews. The blessing recorded is a city at peace under the law, a martyr's honour, and a place among those who pray for the people.

cases.name: Susanna
cases.charge: Choosing to fall into the hands of the elders rather than sin in the sight of the Lord
cases.summary: Two elders and judges of the people caught her alone in her husband's garden and gave her a choice: consent, or be accused of adultery and put to death. She cried out. They testified, the assembly condemned her, and she cried to the Lord on the way to die. Daniel, a young man, separated the witnesses and caught them in a lie about a tree. They died by the law of Moses for false witness, and the innocent blood was saved.
cases.offense: Susanna sighed, and said, I am straitened on every side: for if I do this thing, it is death unto me: and if I do it not I cannot escape your hands. It is better for me to fall into your hands, and not do it, than to sin in the sight of the Lord. With that Susanna cried with a loud voice. Condemned, she cried out with a loud voice, and said, O everlasting God, that knowest the secrets, and knowest all things before they be: thou knowest that they have borne false witness against me, and, behold, I must die; whereas I never did such things as these men have maliciously invented against me.
cases.judgment: And the Lord heard her voice. Therefore when she was led to be put to death, the Lord raised up the holy spirit of a young youth whose name was Daniel. Under what tree sawest thou them? Under a mastick tree. Under an holm tree. With that all the assembly cried out with a loud voice, and praised God, who saveth them that trust in him. And according to the law of Moses they did unto them in such sort as they maliciously intended to do to their neighbour: and they put them to death. Thus the innocent blood was saved the same day. Therefore Chelcias and his wife praised God for their daughter Susanna, because there was no dishonesty found in her.

cases.name: The seven brethren and their mother
cases.charge: Refusing to taste swine's flesh under torture, seven times over, in hope of the resurrection
cases.summary: Seven brothers and their mother were taken and compelled by the king to taste swine's flesh, and tormented with scourges and whips when they would not. One after another they were flayed, dismembered and fried, each speaking the law and the resurrection to the king before he died. The mother watched all seven and exhorted them in her own language, and died last. Their hope is written plainly: the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, unto everlasting life.
cases.offense: We are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers. Thou like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, unto everlasting life. The mother: I cannot tell how ye came into my womb; the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again, as ye now regard not your own selves for his laws' sake. To the youngest: fear not this tormentor, but, being worthy of thy brethren, take thy death, that I may receive thee again in mercy with thy brethren.
cases.judgment: The blessing they claimed is the one the law's own words hold out: everlasting life, and to be received again with their brethren. The seventh: our brethren, who now have suffered a short pain, are dead under God's covenant of everlasting life. The chronicler: let this be enough now to have spoken concerning the idolatrous feasts, and the extreme tortures. Hebrews remembers them without naming them: others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection. Antiochus' own end is his own case, and it followed within the year.

cases.name: Tobit
cases.charge: Walking in truth and justice all his days; alms, tithes, and burying the dead of his people at the risk of his own life
cases.summary: A captive of Naphtali in Nineveh, he went alone to Jerusalem for the feasts when all his tribe went to Dan's calf, gave the double tithe, fed the hungry, clothed the naked, and buried the men Sennacherib killed even after it cost him everything he owned. He was blinded by sparrows' dung and prayed to die. The angel Raphael was sent, his son came home with a wife and the money, and his eyes were opened.
cases.offense: I Tobit have walked all the days of my life in the ways of truth and justice. I alone went often to Jerusalem at the feasts, as it was ordained unto all the people of Israel by an everlasting decree, having the firstfruits and tenths of increase, with that which was first shorn; and them gave I at the altar to the priests. I gave many alms to my brethren, and gave my bread to the hungry, and my clothes to the naked: and if I saw any of my nation dead, or cast about the walls of Nineve, I buried him. Alms doth deliver from death, and suffereth not to come into darkness.
cases.judgment: Raphael: When thou didst pray, and Sara thy daughter in law, I did bring the remembrance of your prayers before the Holy One: and when thou didst bury the dead, I was with thee likewise. I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One. The whiteness pilled away from the corners of his eyes: and when he saw his son, he fell upon his neck. He was an hundred and eight and fifty years old, and buried honourably; and before he died he saw Nineveh destroyed as Jonas had said, and rejoiced.

cases.name: Barabbas
cases.charge: Insurrection and murder
cases.summary: A notable prisoner, lying bound with them that had made insurrection and had committed murder in the insurrection. Pilate offered the crowd a choice between him and Jesus; the chief priests moved them to ask for Barabbas. He was released and Jesus was crucified.
cases.offense: Rebellion against the government and murder, both capital under the law of Moses and of Rome. Peter states the exchange to the men of Israel: ye denied the Holy One and the Just, and desired a murderer to be granted unto you.
cases.judgment: Released, by the custom of the feast and the demand of the crowd. The guilty man walked free because the innocent was condemned in his place; the gospels leave the figure there and say no more of him.

cases.name: Caiaphas and the council
