cases.charge: Seeking false witness against Christ; condemning him by night; delivering him to the Gentiles; forbidding the apostles; stoning Stephen
cases.summary: Caiaphas had already ruled that it was expedient one man die for the people. The council sought false witness to put Jesus to death and found none that agreed; then the high priest adjured him and condemned him for his answer. They delivered him to Pilate, chose Barabbas, and afterward beat and forbade his apostles, and gnashed on Stephen and stoned him.
cases.offense: Every rule of the court broken in one night: witnesses suborned, testimony not agreeing, a capital sentence at night by the accusers themselves, and the prisoner condemned by his own compelled confession. Stephen's charge to them: ye stiffnecked, which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and ye have been now the betrayers and murderers of the Just One.
cases.judgment: Christ told them the kingdom would be taken from them and their house left desolate; Paul says the wrath is come upon them to the uttermost. Peter to their faces: the stone which was set at nought of you builders. Within the generation the temple in which they sat was rubble.

cases.name: Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum
cases.charge: Not repenting after the mighty works done in them
cases.summary: Most of Christ's miracles were done in three towns on the north shore of Galilee, and they did not repent. He measured them against Tyre, Sidon and Sodom and found them worse off in the judgment, because more had been shown them. Capernaum, exalted unto heaven, was to be brought down to hell.
cases.offense: Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not. If the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes. Capernaum had heard the sermon in the synagogue, seen the centurion's servant healed and the paralytic carried down through the roof, and stayed as it was.
cases.judgment: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you. And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day. It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.

cases.name: Herod Antipas and Herodias
cases.charge: Taking his brother's wife; beheading John for saying so
cases.summary: Herod the tetrarch married Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, and John told him it was not lawful. Herodias wanted John dead; Herod feared him and heard him gladly, but at his birthday feast swore to give her dancing daughter whatever she asked. She asked for John's head on a charger.
cases.offense: Leviticus twice: thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy brother's wife. Then a rash oath kept at the cost of a prophet's life, for the sake of them which sat with him. Christ called him that fox and would not answer him at his trial.
cases.judgment: Scripture records no sentence on Herod or Herodias; the gospels leave them at Christ's trial, mocking him. History records Antipas exiled by Caligula at his wife's ambition. The record here is the crime and the statute.

cases.name: Herod the Great and the children of Bethlehem
cases.charge: Slaying all the male children of Bethlehem from two years old and under
cases.summary: Mocked by the wise men who did not return to report the child, Herod was exceeding wroth and sent and slew all the children in Bethlehem and its coasts from two years old and under, according to the time he had inquired of them. Matthew hears Rachel weeping in Ramah.
cases.offense: Innocent blood on a scale of a town, from a king's fear for his throne. The children's only crime was their age and their address.
cases.judgment: Matthew records only that Herod died and Joseph brought the child back from Egypt. Scripture pronounces no sentence on him; secular history records a hideous death. The law's word on innocent blood stands over the case regardless.

cases.name: Jerusalem, that killeth the prophets
cases.charge: Killing the prophets and stoning them that are sent; not knowing the time of her visitation
cases.summary: Christ wept over the city and told it what was coming: thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee, because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation. He said not one stone of the temple would be left on another, and that this generation would see it.
cases.offense: The blood of all the prophets shed from the foundation of the world, from Abel to Zacharias, required of this generation; and the rejection of the one who would have gathered her children as a hen her chickens. Daniel had said the people of the prince that shall come would destroy the city and the sanctuary.
cases.judgment: There shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people. And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled. Deuteronomy 28 had described the siege in detail.

cases.name: Judas Iscariot
cases.charge: Theft from the common purse; betraying innocent blood for thirty pieces of silver
cases.summary: One of the twelve, keeper of the bag, and a thief who took what was put in it. He went to the chief priests and asked what they would give him; they weighed thirty pieces of silver. He delivered Christ with a kiss. In the morning he brought the silver back: I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood.
cases.offense: Covetousness ripened into treachery. Zechariah had priced the shepherd at thirty pieces of silver, the price of a gored slave. His own confession names the statute: cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. Christ: good were it for that man if he had never been born.
cases.judgment: The priests would not take the money back; he cast it down in the temple, went and hanged himself, and the silver bought the potter's field. Acts adds that he fell headlong and burst asunder. Peter, citing the Psalms, says he went to his own place, and his bishoprick passed to another.

cases.name: Nazareth, his own country
cases.charge: Being offended at him; seeking to cast him down the hill
cases.summary: In the synagogue where he had been brought up he read Isaiah and said the scripture was fulfilled that day. They marvelled, then asked if this was not the carpenter's son, then were filled with wrath and led him to the brow of the hill. He did no mighty work there, and passed through the midst of them.
cases.offense: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary? And they were offended at him. When he reminded them that Elijah was sent to a widow of Sidon and Elisha cleansed a Syrian, all they in the synagogue were filled with wrath, and rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.
cases.judgment: A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house. And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief; he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them; and he marvelled because of their unbelief. He passing through the midst of them went his way, and Nazareth kept what it had chosen: a carpenter's son and no miracles.

cases.name: Peter's denial
cases.charge: Denying Christ three times with cursing and swearing
cases.summary: Though I should die with thee, yet will I not deny thee. Before the cock crew twice he had denied him three times, the last with oaths and curses, to a maid and to bystanders in the high priest's courtyard. The Lord turned and looked upon Peter, and he went out and wept bitterly.
cases.offense: Whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father. Peter did it three times and sealed it with a false oath. The sin was foretold, and so was the mercy: I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.
cases.judgment: No sentence but the look and the tears. After the resurrection Christ asked him three times, lovest thou me? and three times restored him: feed my sheep. Peter's godly sorrow worked repentance; Judas' sorrow worked death.

cases.name: Pontius Pilate
cases.charge: Condemning a man he had three times pronounced innocent
cases.summary: Pilate found no fault in him, said so three times, was warned by his wife's dream, and offered the crowd Barabbas instead. When they threatened that he was not Caesar's friend, he washed his hands, said, I am innocent of the blood of this just person, and delivered Jesus to be crucified.
cases.offense: The judge who justifies the wicked and condemns the just is an abomination; the judge who follows a multitude to do evil is forbidden by name. He knew, he said so, and he signed. Water does not answer for a sentence.
cases.judgment: Scripture pronounces nothing on Pilate personally; Acts names him with Herod and the Gentiles and the people of Israel as gathered together against the Lord's holy child, to do whatsoever thy hand and thy counsel determined before to be done. Paul cites his court as the place where Christ witnessed a good confession.

cases.name: The penitent thief
cases.charge: Robbery, under sentence of crucifixion
cases.summary: Two malefactors were crucified with Christ. One railed on him; the other rebuked his fellow: we indeed justly, for we receive the due reward of our deeds, but this man hath done nothing amiss. Then: Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
cases.offense: Matthew calls them thieves, Luke malefactors; the man's own confession is that the sentence was just. He owned the law's verdict on himself in the hour of its execution.
cases.judgment: The sentence of the state was carried out; he died on the cross that day. The sentence of heaven was reversed in the same hour: verily I say unto thee, to day shalt thou be with me in paradise. Isaiah had said the servant would be numbered with the transgressors.

cases.name: The Samaritan village, and the sons of thunder
cases.charge: Refusing to receive him because his face was toward Jerusalem; James and John asking for fire from heaven
cases.summary: A village of Samaria would not take him in, and James and John asked leave to call down fire as Elias did. He rebuked them, not the village: ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of; the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them. They went to another village.
cases.offense: They did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem. And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?
cases.judgment: He turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of. For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them. And they went to another village. The village was spared a sentence, and the disciples were taught the difference between Elijah's day and theirs; one of those two sons of thunder later went down to Samaria with Peter to lay hands on believers there.

cases.name: The scribes and Pharisees
cases.charge: Shutting up the kingdom against men; devouring widows' houses; tithing mint and omitting judgment, mercy and faith; whited sepulchres
cases.summary: They sat in Moses' seat and were to be heard; their works were not to be followed. Eight woes in Matthew 23 name the crimes, and the sentence at the end gathers all the righteous blood from Abel to Zacharias on that generation: your house is left unto you desolate.
cases.offense: They bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers. Ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men. Ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer. Ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith. Ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones. Ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.
cases.judgment: Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell? Behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias. Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation. Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. Forty years later the house was.

cases.name: The traders in the temple
cases.charge: Making the house of prayer a den of thieves
cases.summary: Twice Christ found the temple court full of those that sold oxen, sheep, and doves, and the changers of money sitting. He made a scourge of small cords, drove them out, poured out the changers' money, overthrew the tables, and would not suffer any man to carry a vessel through the temple.
cases.offense: Isaiah had called it a house of prayer for all people; Jeremiah had asked, is this house become a den of robbers in your eyes? The trade occupied the court of the Gentiles, the only place the nations could pray, and did it, on the gospel's account, for profit under the priests' patronage.
cases.judgment: Driven out with a whip. The chief priests sought how they might destroy him for it. Zechariah's last verse hangs over the scene: in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite, the trafficker, in the house of the Lord of hosts.

cases.name: The woman taken in adultery
cases.charge: Adultery, in the very act
cases.summary: The scribes and Pharisees brought a woman taken in adultery and set her in the midst: Moses commanded that such should be stoned; what sayest thou? They said it to tempt him. He wrote on the ground, and then: he that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.
cases.offense: Hers was capital under Leviticus 20 and Deuteronomy 22, and the accusers were right about the statute. But the same statute requires the man, absent here, and Deuteronomy 17 requires the witnesses to cast the first stones on their own testimony. Christ put the witnesses to the test the law itself imposes.
cases.judgment: Convicted by their own conscience, they went out one by one, beginning at the eldest. With no witness remaining there was no case: hath no man condemned thee? Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more. Spared, and commanded.

cases.name: Zacchaeus
cases.charge: Extortion as chief of the publicans
cases.summary: A rich chief tax-collector of Jericho climbed a sycamore to see Jesus and was called down by name. Standing in his house he said: the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
cases.offense: The publican's trade as commonly practiced: assessment by false accusation and extortion, which Leviticus 6 classes with theft and fraud. Fourfold was the law's rate for a stolen sheep, the highest ordinary restitution, and Zacchaeus chose it for himself.
cases.judgment: This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham. The restitution was not the price of the salvation but its evidence: fruits meet for repentance, the very thing John had told the publicans to bring.

cases.name: Zacharias
cases.charge: Not believing the words of the angel Gabriel, and asking for a sign
cases.summary: A righteous priest, walking in all the commandments blameless, was told at the altar of incense that his prayer was heard. He answered that he was old and his wife well stricken in years. He came out of the temple unable to speak, and stayed so until the day he wrote, His name is John.
cases.offense: Zacharias said unto the angel, Whereby shall I know this? for I am an old man, and my wife well stricken in years. The angel answering said, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God; and am sent to speak unto thee, and to shew thee these glad tidings.
cases.judgment: And, behold, thou shalt be dumb, and not able to speak, until the day that these things shall be performed, because thou believest not my words, which shall be fulfilled in their season. The judgment was bounded exactly to the promise: when the child was circumcised and named, his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue loosed, and he spake, and praised God.

cases.name: Joseph, the husband of Mary
cases.charge: A just man; doing as the angel of the Lord bade him, four times, without a word recorded
cases.summary: Betrothed to a woman found with child, and a just man, he meant to put her away privily rather than make her a public example. An angel told him in a dream whose the child was and he took her, and knew her not till she had brought forth. He was told to flee to Egypt and went by night; told to return, and returned; warned, and turned aside to Galilee. Scripture records no word he spoke, only what he did.
cases.offense: Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily. Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife. When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt. Every year his parents went to Jerusalem at the feast of the passover. And he did all things according to the law of the Lord: the circumcision on the eighth day, the presentation, the pair of turtledoves.
cases.judgment: Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name Jesus: for he shall save his people from their sins. The blessing on him is the charge itself: the Son of God was subject unto him, and grew up under his roof in Nazareth, and was called the carpenter's son. Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel: for they are dead which sought the young child's life.

cases.name: Mary of Bethany
cases.charge: Sitting at his feet to hear his word; anointing his body aforehand to the burying
cases.summary: While her sister served, she sat at his feet and heard, and he called it the good part that would not be taken from her. Six days before the passover she broke an alabaster box of spikenard, very precious, over his head and feet and wiped them with her hair. The disciples called it waste. He called it a memorial for the whole world.
cases.offense: Mary sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word. Then took Mary a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment. Some had indignation: why was this waste of the ointment made? for it might have been sold for more than three hundred pence, and given to the poor.
cases.judgment: Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her. Let her alone; why trouble ye her? she hath wrought a good work on me. She hath done what she could: she is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying. Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, this also that she hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.

cases.name: Mary, the mother of Jesus
cases.charge: Be it unto me according to thy word; blessed is she that believed
cases.summary: A virgin of Nazareth, espoused, was told she would conceive by the Holy Ghost and bear the Son of the Highest, and that with God nothing shall be impossible. She answered, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. Elisabeth's word to her is the verdict: blessed is she that believed. Her own song says all generations shall call her blessed, and they have.
cases.offense: And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. She arose in those days and went into the hill country with haste to Elisabeth. She kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart. When the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord; as it is written in the law of the Lord. At Cana her word to the servants was the rule she lived by: Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it. She stood by the cross.
cases.judgment: Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. And blessed is she that believed: for there shall be a performance of those things which were told her from the Lord. My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. For he hath regarded the low estate of his handmaiden: for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. From the cross her Son gave her to the disciple he loved, and from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.

cases.name: Simeon and Anna
cases.charge: Just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel; a widow who departed not from the temple, serving God with fastings and prayers night and day
cases.summary: An old man had been told by the Holy Ghost that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord's Christ. He came by the Spirit into the temple the day a poor couple brought a forty-day-old child with a pair of turtledoves, took him in his arms, and asked to be let go in peace. A prophetess of eighty-four who had lived in the temple since her husband died came in that same hour and spoke of him to all that looked for redemption.
cases.offense: Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Ghost was upon him. He came by the Spirit into the temple. Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser: she was of a great age, and had lived with an husband seven years from her virginity; and she was a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day.
cases.judgment: It was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord's Christ. Then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said, Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word: for mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; a light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. And she coming in that instant gave thanks likewise unto the Lord, and spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem. Two who kept the law past the end of their strength were the first in the temple to know whom they had been waiting for.

cases.name: The centurion of Capernaum
cases.charge: Loving the nation and building the synagogue; not counting himself worthy that the Lord should come under his roof: speak the word only
cases.summary: A Roman officer whose servant was dying sent the elders of the Jews, who pleaded that he was worthy, for he loved their nation and had built them a synagogue. He himself sent to say he was not worthy, and that a word would do, since he too was a man under authority. Christ marvelled, said he had not found so great faith in Israel, and the servant was healed in that hour.
cases.offense: Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed. For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth. The elders of the Jews besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this: for he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue. A Gentile who had done good to Israel and did not presume upon it.
cases.judgment: When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel. And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven. Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour.

cases.name: The Samaritan leper who returned
cases.charge: One of ten: turning back to glorify God with a loud voice, and giving thanks at his feet
cases.summary: Ten lepers stood afar off and cried for mercy, and were sent to shew themselves to the priests as the law commands. As they went they were cleansed. Nine kept going. One, a Samaritan, turned back, fell on his face at his feet and gave thanks. He alone was told, thy faith hath made thee whole.
cases.offense: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, and fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan. The other nine had obeyed the letter, going to the priests; this one came back to the one who had sent them.
cases.judgment: And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine? There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger. And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole. Ten were cleansed of leprosy; one went home whole.

cases.name: The widow and her two mites
cases.charge: Casting in all that she had, even all her living
cases.summary: He sat over against the treasury and watched the rich cast in much. A poor widow threw in two mites, which make a farthing. He called his disciples to see it, and weighed it against everything else in the box: she had cast in more than they all.
cases.offense: And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing. The rich cast in of their abundance; she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living. No one had asked her for it.
cases.judgment: And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: for all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living. Her gift is the standard by which every other gift in the temple that day was found smaller, and it is read in every generation since.

cases.name: The woman with the issue of blood
cases.charge: Believing that if she might but touch his clothes she should be whole
cases.summary: Twelve years unclean under the law, spent to her last penny on physicians and worse for it, she came behind him in the press and touched the border of his garment. The flow dried up in the same hour. He turned and made her say it before everyone, and gave her the verdict in front of them: thy faith hath made thee whole.
cases.offense: A certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years, and had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse, when she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment. For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole. When she saw that she was not hid, she came trembling, and falling down before him, she declared unto him before all the people for what cause she had touched him.
cases.judgment: And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague. And he said unto her, Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague. Under the law her touch should have made him unclean; instead his made her clean, and she went home with the word that did it.

cases.name: Zacharias and Elisabeth
cases.charge: Both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless
cases.summary: A priest of the course of Abia and a daughter of Aaron, old, childless, and blameless in the whole law. Their prayer was heard at the altar of incense: a son, to be called John, filled with the Holy Ghost from his mother's womb, who would go before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elias. Zacharias' unbelief at the news is its own case; the blessing stood.
cases.offense: They were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. He executed the priest's office before God in the order of his course, according to the custom of the priest's office. Elisabeth hid herself five months, saying, Thus hath the Lord dealt with me in the days wherein he looked on me, to take away my reproach among men. On the eighth day they circumcised the child, and against all their kindred named him as the angel had said.
cases.judgment: Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John. And thou shalt have joy and gladness; and many shall rejoice at his birth. For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord. Her neighbours and her cousins heard how the Lord had shewed great mercy upon her; and they rejoiced with her. Zacharias was filled with the Holy Ghost and prophesied: and thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest. Christ's own verdict on their son: among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist.

cases.name: Alexander the coppersmith
cases.charge: Doing Paul much evil; greatly withstanding his words
cases.summary: Named in Paul's last letter as a man to beware of. Whether he is the Alexander delivered to Satan with Hymenaeus for blasphemy, or the Alexander the Jews put forward in the Ephesian theatre, the sentence Paul leaves is the law's own: the Lord reward him according to his works.
cases.offense: Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: of whom be thou ware also; for he hath greatly withstood our words. In the first letter to Timothy, Hymenaeus and Alexander had put away faith and a good conscience and made shipwreck, and were delivered unto Satan that they might learn not to blaspheme.
cases.judgment: The Lord reward him according to his works. Paul does not curse him in his own name; he cites the judgment already written for every man, and leaves Alexander under it. Timothy was told to beware of him, which is the church's share of the sentence: a man marked and avoided.

cases.name: Ananias and Sapphira
cases.charge: Lying to the Holy Spirit about a gift
cases.summary: A couple sold property and gave part of the proceeds to the apostles while claiming it was the whole. The gift was never required; the lie was the offense. Each fell dead as it was exposed.
cases.offense: They agreed together to keep back part of the price and present the rest as the full amount, a staged generosity meant to buy standing. Peter named it: not a lie to men but to God.
cases.judgment: Ananias fell dead at Peter's word; Sapphira, questioned three hours later and holding to the same story, fell dead as well. Great fear came on the whole church.

cases.name: Ananias the high priest
cases.charge: Commanding Paul to be smitten on the mouth, contrary to the law, while sitting to judge him by the law
cases.summary: Paul had said one sentence to the council when the high priest ordered him struck. Paul answered as a prophet answers: God shall smite thee, thou whited wall; for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law? Then he withdrew the words toward the office, not the man.
cases.offense: Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day. And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth. The law forbids condemning a man before he is heard, and forbids the judge to strike the accused; Ananias did both from the judgment seat.
cases.judgment: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall. Told it was the high priest, he answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people. Scripture records the word spoken and not its performance; the office was honoured, the man was named, and the sentence was left with God.

cases.name: Demas
cases.charge: Forsaking Paul, having loved this present world
cases.summary: Three times Demas appears in Paul's letters: a fellowlabourer sending greetings from Rome, then a name without a word, then a name with a verdict. Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica. Scripture says nothing more of him.
cases.offense: He had stood with Paul in the first imprisonment, named with Luke among the fellowlabourers. In the second, with Paul's death near, he loved this present world and went to Thessalonica. The love of the world is named by John as the thing that cannot share a heart with the love of the Father.
cases.judgment: No sentence is written; the departure is the record. The law's word on the man who puts his hand to the plough and looks back, and the apostle's on the friendship of the world, stand over the empty place where his name had been. Whether he came back is not told.

cases.name: Diotrephes
cases.charge: Loving the preeminence; prating against the apostle with malicious words; casting the brethren out of the church
cases.summary: John wrote to the church, but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, received him not. He spoke against the apostle with malicious words, refused to receive the traveling brethren himself, forbade those who would, and cast them out of the church.
cases.offense: Pride in office, slander of an apostle, refusal of hospitality to the brethren, and excommunication used as a weapon. The law's word on the slanderer and on hospitality to strangers both apply; so does Christ's on those who would be greatest.
cases.judgment: Wherefore, if I come, I will remember his deeds which he doeth. The epistle records the charge and the intention; the sentence is not recorded. Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good.

cases.name: Elymas the sorcerer
cases.charge: Withstanding the apostles; seeking to turn the deputy from the faith
cases.summary: At Paphos the proconsul Sergius Paulus sent for Barnabas and Saul to hear the word. Bar-jesus, a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet attached to his court, withstood them, seeking to turn away the deputy from the faith. Paul, filled with the Holy Ghost, set his eyes on him.
cases.offense: O full of all subtilty and all mischief, thou child of the devil, thou enemy of all righteousness, wilt thou not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord? A sorcerer, forbidden by the law outright, using his influence to keep a ruler from the truth.
cases.judgment: The hand of the Lord is upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun for a season. Immediately there fell on him a mist and a darkness, and he went about seeking some to lead him by the hand. The deputy, seeing it, believed.

cases.name: Herod Agrippa
cases.charge: Accepting worship due to God alone
cases.summary: Arrayed in royal robes, the king gave an oration and the crowd shouted that his was the voice of a god, not a man. He accepted the acclaim. The judgment was immediate and public.
cases.offense: The sin was not the speech but the silence after it: he took to himself the honor owed to God, receiving worship he should have refused as Paul and Barnabas had refused it at Lystra.
cases.judgment: Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him because he gave not God the glory; he was eaten of worms and died. The contrast follows at once: but the word of God grew and multiplied.

cases.name: Hymenaeus, Alexander, and Philetus
cases.charge: Making shipwreck of the faith; blasphemy; teaching that the resurrection is past already
cases.summary: Paul names Hymenaeus and Alexander as men who put away faith and a good conscience and made shipwreck, whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme. Hymenaeus and Philetus erred concerning the truth, saying the resurrection is past already, and overthrew the faith of some. Alexander the coppersmith did him much evil.
cases.offense: Heresy that eats as doth a canker, spread inside the church by teachers. Titus gives the procedure: a man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject, knowing that he is subverted and sinneth, being condemned of himself.
cases.judgment: Delivered unto Satan, the apostolic form of putting out, with the stated aim of correction. Of Alexander Paul adds only: the Lord reward him according to his works.

cases.name: Jezebel of Thyatira
cases.charge: Calling herself a prophetess; teaching the servants of God to commit fornication and eat things sacrificed to idols
cases.summary: Christ's word to the angel of the church in Thyatira: thou sufferest that woman Jezebel, which calleth herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce my servants. He had given her space to repent of her fornication, and she repented not.
cases.offense: The two things the apostles' council had bound on the Gentiles, abstinence from idol meats and from fornication, taught as liberty by a self-appointed prophetess, under a name that carried Ahab's queen with it. The church's toleration is charged against the church.
cases.judgment: Behold, I will cast her into a bed, and them that commit adultery with her into great tribulation, except they repent of their deeds. And I will kill her children with death; and all the churches shall know that I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts.

cases.name: Peter at Antioch
cases.charge: Dissembling: withdrawing from the Gentiles for fear of them of the circumcision
cases.summary: At Antioch Peter had eaten with the Gentiles until certain came from James; then he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision, and the other Jews and even Barnabas were carried away with his dissimulation. Paul withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.
cases.offense: Hypocrisy in a pillar of the church, contradicting the vision God had given him at Joppa and the judgment he himself had argued at Jerusalem. Paul's charge: they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, and by the example compelled the Gentiles to live as do the Jews.
cases.judgment: A public rebuke before them all, and no more; the epistle records the correction and leaves the reconciliation to be inferred. Peter later commends Paul's letters as scripture. The case stands as the law's own rule for reproof: a trespass taken openly to the transgressor.

cases.name: Saul of Tarsus
cases.charge: Persecuting the church; consenting to Stephen's death; compelling the saints to blaspheme
cases.summary: The young man at whose feet Stephen's killers laid their clothes made havock of the church, entering every house and haling men and women to prison, and set out for Damascus with letters to bind any he found of that way. A light from heaven and a voice met him on the road: why persecutest thou me?
cases.offense: By his own later account: I persecuted this way unto the death; I punished them oft in every synagogue and compelled them to blaspheme; being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities. He was a blasphemer, a persecutor, and injurious.
cases.judgment: Three days blind and fasting in Damascus, then sight, baptism, and a commission. I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief. He calls himself the chief of sinners and the pattern of the longsuffering shown to them which should hereafter believe. Ananias was told he would be shown how great things he must suffer.

cases.name: Simon Magus
cases.charge: Offering money for the gift of the Holy Ghost
cases.summary: A sorcerer of Samaria who had long bewitched the people and given out that he was some great one, Simon believed and was baptized under Philip. When he saw that the Spirit was given through the apostles' hands he offered them money for the same power.
cases.offense: Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money. Peter names the state behind the offer: thy heart is not right in the sight of God; thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity. A sorcerer's instinct, to buy power.
cases.judgment: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee. Simon asked Peter to pray for him that none of these things come upon him, and the record ends there. His name became the word for buying office in the church.

cases.name: The churches of Ephesus, Sardis, and Laodicea
cases.charge: Leaving the first love; a name to live while dead; lukewarm, and saying, I am rich
cases.summary: Three of the seven letters in the Revelation carry a sentence with a condition. Ephesus, sound in doctrine and patient, had left her first love and would lose her candlestick. Sardis had a name that it lived and was dead. Laodicea was neither cold nor hot, and was about to be spued out. Each was told what to do, and given time.
cases.offense: Ephesus: I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love. Sardis: thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead; I have not found thy works perfect before God. Laodicea: thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot; thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked.
cases.judgment: Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief. I will spue thee out of my mouth. As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent. Behold, I stand at the door, and knock. The sentence is written in full and stayed on the condition.

cases.name: The Corinthian who had his father's wife
cases.charge: Fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles: a man with his father's wife
cases.summary: Paul heard that a member of the Corinthian church was living with his father's wife and that the church, instead of mourning, was puffed up. He judged the case in absence: deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.
cases.offense: Leviticus 18 and 20 and Deuteronomy 27 all name it, the last with a curse and the middle with death. Paul's rule follows the statute's shape: put away from among yourselves that wicked person. The church's tolerance was a second offense: a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.
cases.judgment: Excommunicated by the assembly. The second letter shows the outcome: the punishment inflicted of many was sufficient, the man was overwhelmed with sorrow, and Paul urged them to forgive and comfort him and confirm their love toward him, lest Satan get an advantage. Banishment, then restoration on repentance.

cases.name: The Corinthians at the Lord's supper
cases.charge: Eating and drinking unworthily; shaming them that have not
cases.summary: When the Corinthians came together it was not to eat the Lord's supper: every one took his own supper before another, one was hungry and another drunken, and the poor were shamed in the assembly of the church. Paul: what, have ye not houses to eat and to drink in?
cases.offense: Contempt for the assembly and for the brethren who had nothing, in the very meal that proclaimed the Lord's death. Whosoever shall eat this bread and drink this cup unworthily shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.
cases.judgment: For this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. Paul frames it as chastening: when we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world. The remedy: let a man examine himself, and tarry one for another.

cases.name: The seven sons of Sceva
cases.charge: Exorcising in the name of Jesus whom Paul preacheth
cases.summary: Vagabond Jewish exorcists at Ephesus, seven sons of a chief priest, took up the name of the Lord Jesus as a formula over those that had evil spirits. The spirit answered, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?
cases.offense: The Name used as a spell by men who did not belong to it, in a city given to curious arts. Taking the name in vain in its most literal form.
cases.judgment: The man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded. Fear fell on the city, the name was magnified, and the practitioners of curious arts burned their books, fifty thousand pieces of silver worth.

cases.name: Antipas, Smyrna, and Philadelphia
cases.charge: Faithful unto death; keeping the word of his patience; not denying his name in the place where Satan's seat is
cases.summary: Of the seven churches, two are given no rebuke at all, and one man in a third is named by the Lord himself. Smyrna, poor and slandered, is promised a crown of life. Philadelphia, with a little strength, has an open door no man can shut and will be kept from the hour of temptation. Antipas of Pergamos is called my faithful martyr, slain among them where Satan dwelleth.
cases.offense: I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich). Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried. Be thou faithful unto death. Thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith, even in those days wherein Antipas was my faithful martyr, who was slain among you, where Satan dwelleth. Thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name. Because thou hast kept the word of my patience.
cases.judgment: Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life. He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death. Behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it. I will make them of the synagogue of Satan to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee. I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world. Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God. Behold, I come quickly: hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown.

cases.name: Barnabas
cases.charge: Selling his land and laying the money at the apostles' feet; a good man, full of the Holy Ghost and of faith
cases.summary: A Levite of Cyprus sold his land and brought the whole price to the apostles, in the same chapter and by the same rule that Ananias and Sapphira broke with theirs. He took Saul in when the disciples were afraid of him, went to find him in Tarsus when Antioch needed a teacher, and was the man Antioch's Gentiles first believed under. The apostles named him: the son of consolation.
cases.offense: Joses, who by the apostles was surnamed Barnabas, (which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation,) a Levite, and of the country of Cyprus, having land, sold it, and brought the money, and laid it at the apostles' feet. But Barnabas took Saul, and brought him to the apostles. When he came to Antioch, and had seen the grace of God, he was glad, and exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would cleave unto the Lord. For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith.
cases.judgment: And much people was added unto the Lord. The Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them. The Spirit's own naming of him for the first mission to the Gentiles is the blessing; the church's naming of him is the other: son of consolation. His gift and Ananias' lie stand a few verses apart so no one can miss the difference.

cases.name: Cornelius
cases.charge: A devout man, one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway
cases.summary: A centurion of the Italian band at Caesarea, a Gentile, was praying at the ninth hour when an angel told him his prayers and alms were come up for a memorial before God, and to send for Peter. Peter came, learned on the way that God is no respecter of persons, preached, and the Holy Ghost fell on the whole house before he had finished. They were the first Gentiles baptized.
cases.offense: A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway. Cornelius said, Four days ago I was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed in my house. When Peter came, Cornelius met him and fell down at his feet; Peter took him up: I myself also am a man. Now therefore are we all here present before God, to hear all things that are commanded thee of God.
cases.judgment: Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God. Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: but in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him. While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word. And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost. And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord.

cases.name: Dorcas (Tabitha)
cases.charge: Full of good works and almsdeeds which she did; the coats and garments she made for the widows
cases.summary: A disciple at Joppa who clothed the widows died, and they washed her and laid her in an upper chamber and sent two men for Peter. When he came, the widows stood by him weeping and showing the coats and garments she had made. He put them out, kneeled, prayed, and said, Tabitha, arise. She opened her eyes, and he presented her alive.
cases.offense: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did. All the widows stood by him weeping, and shewing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them. Her works were her witnesses, and they were held up in the room where she lay.
cases.judgment: Peter kneeled down, and prayed; and turning him to the body said, Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes: and when she saw Peter, she sat up. And he gave her his hand, and lifted her up, and when he had called the saints and widows, presented her alive. And it was known throughout all Joppa; and many believed in the Lord. The one woman raised from the dead in the Acts is the one whose alms were in every widow's hands.

cases.name: Gaius, the wellbeloved
cases.charge: Walking in the truth; doing faithfully to the brethren and to strangers; bringing them forward on their journey after a godly sort
cases.summary: The third epistle of John is written to him. He kept the travelling brethren, strangers to him, and sent them on their way supplied, and they testified of his charity before the church. In the same short letter Diotrephes is cast out of the church for the opposite. John has no greater joy than to hear that his children walk in truth.
cases.offense: Beloved, thou doest faithfully whatsoever thou doest to the brethren, and to strangers; which have borne witness of thy charity before the church: whom if thou bring forward on their journey after a godly sort, thou shalt do well: because that for his name's sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles. We therefore ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth.
cases.judgment: Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth. For I rejoiced greatly, when the brethren came and testified of the truth that is in thee, even as thou walkest in the truth. I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth. Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God.

cases.name: Lydia
cases.charge: A seller of purple who worshipped God; whose heart the Lord opened; who constrained the apostles to abide in her house
cases.summary: Paul crossed into Europe on a vision and found no synagogue at Philippi, only women at prayer by the river. One of them, a merchant of Thyatira, heard, believed, was baptized with her household, and would not let the apostles lodge anywhere else. Her house became the church at Philippi, and after the prison and the earthquake it was where Paul and Silas went first.
cases.offense: A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us. And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there. And she constrained us. Leaving the prison, they entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
cases.judgment: Whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul. The first believer in Europe recorded by name, and the first house of the church that later sent to Paul's necessity once and again, and to which he wrote that he thanked God upon every remembrance of them. The blessing on hospitality is the guests: an apostle and the gospel under her roof.

cases.name: Onesiphorus
cases.charge: Oft refreshing Paul, and not ashamed of his chain; seeking him out very diligently in Rome
cases.summary: When everyone in Asia had turned from Paul, one man from Ephesus went to Rome, hunted through the prisons until he found him, and kept coming. Paul's blessing on him is in the last letter he wrote: the Lord give mercy unto the house of Onesiphorus, and grant that he may find mercy of the Lord in that day.
cases.offense: He oft refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain: but, when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me. And in how many things he ministered unto me at Ephesus, thou knowest very well. This thou knowest, that all they which are in Asia be turned away from me.
cases.judgment: The Lord give mercy unto the house of Onesiphorus. The Lord grant unto him that he may find mercy of the Lord in that day. I was in prison, and ye came unto me: inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. Salute the household of Onesiphorus.

cases.name: Paul, at the end of his course
cases.charge: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith
cases.summary: The man who had held the coats at Stephen's stoning wrote his last letter from a Roman prison, alone except for Luke, with the time of his departure at hand. He gave his own account of himself in one sentence and claimed the crown by name. Before that, five times forty stripes save one, three times beaten with rods, once stoned, three shipwrecks, a night and a day in the deep; and the churches of the Gentiles.
cases.offense: For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith. At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge. Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear. I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel; these hands have ministered unto my necessities.
cases.judgment: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing. And the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work, and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom: to whom be glory for ever and ever. The blessing on Saul of Tarsus, whose own case is his persecution of the church, is written by his own hand at the end of it.

cases.name: Stephen
cases.charge: Full of faith and of the Holy Ghost; a face like an angel before the council; forgiving those who stoned him
cases.summary: One of the seven chosen to serve tables, full of faith and power, he did great wonders and out-argued every synagogue that tried him. Accused by suborned witnesses, he preached Abraham to Solomon to a council that stopped their ears and stoned him. He saw heaven opened and the Son of man standing, and asked that the sin not be laid to their charge. A young man named Saul held the coats.
cases.offense: Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost. And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he spake. All that sat in the council, looking stedfastly on him, saw his face as it had been the face of an angel. He, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God. And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge.
cases.judgment: Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God. The Lord had said, whosoever shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of man also confess before the angels of God; Stephen saw him stand to do it. Devout men carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation over him. The blessing recorded is a witness received in heaven in sight of the witness himself, and the persecution that scattered the church to preach the word everywhere, and the coat-holder who became Paul.

cases.name: The Bereans
cases.charge: Receiving the word with all readiness of mind, and searching the scriptures daily, whether those things were so
cases.summary: Driven from Thessalonica by a mob, Paul and Silas came to Berea and found a synagogue that did two things at once: welcomed the message and checked it against the scriptures every day. Luke calls them more noble than the Thessalonians for it. Many of them believed, including honourable Greek women and men.
cases.offense: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so. They did not believe Paul because he was Paul; they believed the scriptures, and found him in them.
cases.judgment: Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few. When the Thessalonian Jews came to stir up the city, the brethren sent Paul away, and Silas and Timotheus abode there still. Search the scriptures, Christ had said; the Bereans are the one church named for having done it, and the church was theirs.

cases.name: The Philippian jailer
cases.charge: Believing on the Lord with all his house the same night; washing the stripes of the men he had put in the stocks
cases.summary: He thrust Paul and Silas into the inner prison and made their feet fast in the stocks. At midnight they sang, the earthquake opened every door, and he drew his sword to kill himself. Paul cried out that they were all there. He fell down trembling, asked what he must do to be saved, was told, and before dawn had washed their wounds, been baptized with all his house, set meat before them, and rejoiced.
cases.offense: Sirs, what must I do to be saved? And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house. And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway. And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them.
cases.judgment: And rejoiced, believing in God with all his house. The prisoners he had chained became his guests, the sword he had drawn on himself went back in its sheath, and the magistrates who had beaten Roman citizens uncondemned came the next morning to beg them to leave. The church at Philippi that Lydia opened her house to had a jailer in it.

cases.name: Timothy, with Lois and Eunice
cases.charge: Unfeigned faith that dwelt first in his grandmother and his mother; knowing the holy scriptures from a child
cases.summary: A boy of Lystra with a Greek father and a believing Jewish mother had been taught the scriptures from a child by two women. Paul found him well reported of, circumcised him for the Jews' sake, and took him. He became Paul's own son in the faith, the man he trusted with Ephesus, and the one he wrote his last letter to.
cases.offense: When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also. From a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation. Timotheus was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium. I have no man likeminded, who will naturally care for your state. For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's. But ye know the proof of him, that, as a son with the father, he hath served with me in the gospel.
cases.judgment: Him would Paul have to go forth with him. Timothy, my own son in the faith. This charge I commit unto thee, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on thee, that thou by them mightest war a good warfare. Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery. The blessing on the two women's teaching is the man it made: named in the address of six epistles, and left in charge of the church at Ephesus.
